2026-10-23.bodyText:
News window: Thu Oct 22 9:00am – Fri Oct 23 9:00am ET

MARKETS

1. SpaceX is in talks to secure at least 80,000 US cell sites (about half of the 158,500 purpose-built US towers) to build Starlink Mobile into a fourth nationwide carrier, including with Crown Castle, Bloomberg reported Thursday evening; AT&T, Verizon and T-Mobile fell 4.2%-5% after hours and were still down more than 4% premarket, while Crown Castle rose 8.6% and American Tower 6.1% premarket, SPCX was up about 1.5%, and TD Cowen puts a nationwide terrestrial network at more than $80B (Bloomberg via Reuters, Investing.com, Forbes).

2. SpaceX is finalizing a $40B debt package led by Apollo and Goldman Sachs that is set to close next week at about 8.3% on the riskiest tranche and about 7.75% on a tranche backed by its AI chips, more than a point above its existing bonds, as lenders demand more after the AI-credit selloff (Semafor, Yahoo Finance).

3. US spot bitcoin ETFs lost -$635.6M on Thursday, their biggest daily outflow since Jun 25, erasing Wednesday's +$524.8M (IBIT -$254.1M, FBTC -$217.5M, ARKB -$109.4M, GBTC -$29.5M; Morgan Stanley's MSBT the only inflow at +$2.3M), leaving the week at +$439M and October back below zero, with ether ETFs -$110.6M; bitcoin held around $81,550-$81,700 overnight after a low near $81,000 and its first daily close below the 50-day average in two months, with traders eyeing the Oct 27-28 FOMC (Farside, CryptoWatchDesk, Fortune, CoinDesk).

4. Update on the Tesla-SpaceX merger: CNBC laid out the hurdles, with Musk saying a deal needs 50% of all Tesla shares (he owns 19.8% of Tesla versus about 80% voting control of SpaceX), former Tesla director Steve Westly expecting a proposal quickly, ideally before the Nov 3 midterms, William Blair calling it a play for control, and China (22% of Tesla's revenue last year) seen as a major regulatory hurdle; TSLA closed Thursday down 17% for the year (CNBC).

5. The 10-year Treasury yield stayed under 5% at 4.997% Friday morning (+4bp) after Thursday's flight-to-quality took it below 5% for the first time in a month, with the 2-year at 4.692% and 30-year at 5.31%, even as Brent rose to $114.06 and WTI to $100.61 on new Houthi attacks on Saudi oil sites and reports that the US and Israel could resume strikes on Iran after the midterms (CNBC).

6. Stock futures were modestly lower after Thursday's AI rout, with S&P 500 futures -0.2%, Nasdaq 100 -0.1% and the Dow -0.6% (-315 points) at 7:15am ET as Meta, Nvidia and AMD tried to bounce; flash S&P Global PMIs land at 9:45am and final University of Michigan sentiment at 10am (consensus 46.3 vs 48.1 prior), ahead of Microsoft, Alphabet and Amazon earnings and the Fed next week (Investing.com, Reuters, Yahoo Finance, Briefing.com).

7. Capital Group is again Metaplanet's largest shareholder, holding 143,301,084 shares (11.11% of voting rights) as of Oct 16, up about 17.8M shares from 9.76%, per a filing with Japan's Kanto Local Finance Bureau on Oct 23 that also shows share-lending arrangements with JPMorgan and Fidelity; Metaplanet holds about 44,000 BTC (CryptoBriefing, CryptoTimes).

Gap-catch: I rechecked Thursday 6-9am ET and found no treasury-company 8-K or other pre-market item that yesterday's briefing missed.

AI, ROBOTICS, TECH & LONGEVITY

1. OpenAI is close to a round of up to $30B at a $1.25T pre-money valuation, led by UAE investors and Coatue and pitched as a bridge ahead of a 2027 IPO, with signatures targeted by the end of next week; it would be the highest valuation ever for a private company, and OpenAI has not confirmed it (CNBC, sent as an alert at 5:34pm).

2. Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang told CNBC that neocloud demand is "off the charts" but that "there is a scarcity of capital" for AI infrastructure, which fed Thursday's rout as Nvidia closed -4.4%, AMD more than -8% and Meta nearly -8% after reporting its first cash outflow in more than a decade; all three were slightly higher premarket, and CoreWeave was up about 2% after a 17-month low of $53.50 (CNBC, Yahoo Finance, Reuters).

3. A Science study found Microsoft's MAI-DxO diagnostic agent reached 83% accuracy on complex NEJM cases versus 36% for primary-care doctors, and pairing it with GPT-5.5 lifted accuracy on those cases from 72% to nearly 87% (The GPU Daily, citing trade press).

4. Microsoft blamed China-aligned hackers using AI agents for a ConnectWise breach in which stolen cloud-backup credentials let attackers compromise about 2,250 organizations at nearly 3,000 sign-in attempts per minute (The GPU Daily, citing trade press).

5. Former OpenAI executive Kevin Weil launched Warp Sciences with a $215M Series A led by Lightspeed at an $865M valuation, building US-based AI-driven robotic labs that test molecules around the clock for biotech companies, with DJ Patil among the co-founders (X News summary of company posts).

6. Google Cloud made an Anthropic-managed deployment of Claude generally available, giving day-one access to Claude platform features including Claude Managed Agents in beta at the same price as the Google-managed option, a day after OpenAI said its models and Codex are coming to Google Cloud's Model Garden (Google Cloud, OpenAI).

READS

1. Have We Seen This Movie Before?, by Canaan (@canaaninamerica, X Article newsletter, Oct 21): A tight comparison of today's debt-financed neoclouds with 2021's bitcoin miners, from CoreWeave's 2032 notes below 80 cents to who survived mining's 2022 credit cycle.
https://x.com/canaaninamerica/status/2113080021393056027

2. Is the Bitcoin Treasury Playbook Still Working?, by RootstockLabs (@RootstockLabs, X Article, Oct 22): A useful one-year-after-the-peak look at what broke in the issue-and-buy model, how Strategy adapted with its dollar reserve and buybacks, and why bitcoin per share, not holdings, is the scoreboard.
https://x.com/RootstockLabs/status/2113207891242975283

3. Analysis: Musk's political baggage clouds prospects for SpaceX-Tesla deal, Reuters (Oct 22): Covers the political and regulatory side of the merger, a good complement to the deal-mechanics pieces from earlier this week.
https://www.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/analysismusks-political-baggage-clouds-prospects-for-spacextesla-deal-4965229

Carriers (Forbes): https://www.forbes.com/sites/siladityaray/2026/10/23/att-verizon-t-mobile-shares-slip-as-spacex-reportedly-holds-cell-tower-talks-for-starlink-mobile/

2026-10-24.bodyText:
News window: Fri Oct 23 9:00am – Sat Oct 24 9:00am ET

MARKETS

1. Bitcoin slipped overnight to a low of $80,389 and was $80,705 at 8:38am ET Saturday (-1.1% on the day), below Friday's $81K-$82K range, after US spot bitcoin ETFs lost -$137.9M on Friday, a second straight outflow day (IBIT -$110.3M, FBTC -$31.8M, MSBT the only inflow at +$4.2M, VanEck's HODL not yet reported), leaving the week at +$301.2M (IBIT +$565.7M, FBTC -$116.6M, ARKB -$99.6M) and October at -$313.5M after 17 sessions, while ether ETFs took in +$4.4M (Yahoo Finance, Farside, CryptoWatchDesk).

2. Missed Friday (6-9am ET gap-catch): at 8:25am ET Friday Saylor posted "Our goal is to grow Bitcoin per share" and Strategy published a new MSTR Investor Briefing PDF covering bitcoin per share, digital credit and its capital structure (strategy.com/mstr/brief); there was no new 8-K Friday, so the next weekly update would normally come Monday for Oct 19-25, ahead of Q3 results after the close on Oct 29 (Strategy/Saylor on X, Bloomingbit).

3. CME FedWatch on Friday priced a 92.8% chance the Fed holds at Wednesday's decision but a 74.8% chance of a 25bp hike by December (5.7% for 50bp, 80.5% for at least one hike this year), in a week that also brings Microsoft and Alphabet earnings after Wednesday's close, Amazon on Thursday, and Q3 GDP plus September PCE on Thursday (FXBus citing CME, The Block, investingLive).

4. CNBC reported Saturday that Nvidia's role as AI financier faces its first real stress test: it carries $36B of off-balance-sheet backstops for neoclouds plus a guarantee of up to $105B on OpenAI's planned 10GW Ohio data center, while CoreWeave, Nebius and IREN are each down at least 30% in October, CoreWeave's CDS spread is above 11% and its 2031-32 bond yields topped 15%, and Nvidia itself is -7.6% in October after a third straight down week, the backdrop for SpaceX's pricier $40B debt package (CNBC).

5. NASA laid out its revised Artemis plan Friday: Orion will dock with SpaceX's Starship lunar lander in high-Earth orbit rather than lunar orbit, the Artemis III docking demo stays on track for summer 2027 and the Artemis IV landing for 2028, and Musk disputed a NASA safety panel's estimate of about 22 tanker flights per landing, saying it will be 6-8, which Administrator Isaacman called possible but the "ultimate potential end state" (Ars Technica).

6. Tesla's Texas robotaxi roster on the state DMV record reached 927 vehicles on Oct 23, including 420 Cybercabs (up 71 from 349 on Oct 16) and 507 Model Ys, as Tesla readies Cybercab service in Dallas next month; the roster counts registrations, not vehicles carrying riders (Cybercab Collective, Sawyer Merritt on X).

7. HSBC began rolling out its Hong Kong dollar stablecoin RedCoin (RCHKD) to about 3.3M PayMe users with payments at 100,000+ merchants, Sen. Richard Blumenthal asked Tether for records of reported multimillion-dollar payments to Nxum, the consulting firm founded by former White House crypto adviser Bo Hines, and Initia halted its chain after an attacker minted about $2.7M in unauthorized tokens (The Block, CryptoRank).

AI, ROBOTICS, TECH & LONGEVITY

1. Moonshot released Kimi K3.1 Pro, a 2.8T-parameter model (104B active, 1M-token context) that scored 55 on Artificial Analysis's Intelligence Index, 4th behind Claude Opus 5.5 (58), Claude Sonnet 5.5 (56) and Muse Wonder Full (56), with the top Terminal-Bench 4.0 score of any model at 67% and prices cut 33% to $2/$10 per million input/output tokens; open weights are due Nov 4, which would make it the leading open model and shrink the open-vs-closed gap from 12 points to 3 (Artificial Analysis, Kimi).

2. Anthropic and formal-methods firm Theorem used Claude to write about 180 million lines of machine-checked Rocq proofs covering 239 entry points in 123 OSS-Fuzz open-source libraries, proving the compiled RISC-V binaries can't crash on any input under 64MB, and surfaced hundreds of bugs including ones years of fuzzing missed; Anthropic says Opus 5.5 needs about 40% fewer tokens than Opus 5 on such tasks (Anthropic, DevOps.com).

3. Munich's Agile Robots unveiled the 1.4m, 71-degree-of-freedom Agile ONE SN humanoid built on Nvidia's GR00T and Jetson Thor at GTC Berlin and told Reuters it is targeting 1,000-2,000 units in 2027 for university and corporate research labs, with production starting by the end of 2026 (eWeek, Reuters).

4. A Yale study in Cell (Oct 23) found that macrophages release up to 80% of their taurine as the NLRP3 inflammasome assembles, that restoring taurine blocks the inflammatory cascade, and that lowering it accelerates inflammation even in young mice, pointing to taurine as a brake on age-related "inflammaging" (Yale School of Medicine).

READS

1. The Entire Tech Industry Is About To Be "Musked", by Porter Stansberry (Porter & Company, via ZeroHedge, Oct 22): A bull's deep dive on SpaceX's Q3, from Starlink's subscriber curve to its 10GW compute plan, with three 2027 capex scenarios and what each does to its debt-to-EBITDA and investment-grade rating.
https://www.zerohedge.com/news/2026-10-22/entire-tech-industry-about-be-musked

2. The Asset Everyone Prices, The Security Nobody Buys, by Saša Čoh, CEO of NiceHash (@NiceHashMining, X Article, Oct 23): A sharp argument that AI is outbidding bitcoin mining for power, capital and chips, and what that means for the security budget behind ETF and treasury-company holdings.
https://x.com/NiceHashMining/status/2113574721400734107

3. Strategy Nowcast #02: The Last $447 Million, by @ThePostAustrian (X Article, Oct 23): A small independent account, but a well-sourced walk through Strategy's 8-Ks asking whether $193M-a-week STRC buybacks can continue with $447.3M of flexible USD cash against $1.16B of remaining authorization, useful ahead of Monday's update.
https://x.com/ThePostAustrian/status/2113731026677809177

2026-10-25.subject: Sun Oct 25 briefing: BTC breaks $80K, $815M liquidations, US Mideast evacuations, Saylor tease, Falcon Heavy wins Space Force missions, Claude Duet
2026-10-25.bodyText:
News window: Sat Oct 24 9:00am – Sun Oct 25 9:00am ET

MARKETS

1. Bitcoin broke below $80,000 on Saturday for the first time since Sep 18, hitting about $79,146 around 11:20am ET as $404M of longs were liquidated in four hours (two bursts of $208M and $131M), the most since Oct 14, and $815M in 24 hours across 201,012 traders; it reclaimed $80K by 1pm and was about $80,330 early Sunday (-0.4% on the day), while ether fell to about $2,289 (-4.7%), its lowest in roughly two months, and BitMEX co-founder Arthur Hayes said he had sold out of his fund's directional book ("I dumped it all") (The Block, CoinDesk, Yahoo Finance).

2. The trigger was geopolitical: the WSJ reported Saturday that the US is quickly evacuating personnel from embassies and bases across the Middle East after a DNI memo said Iranian plotting against Americans had "reached advanced stages," Trump said at a Friday rally "we may do another little 'Epic Fury'" after the midterms, and Brent heads into the Sunday-evening futures open at Friday's $116.72 settle after unconfirmed Houthi claims of strikes on Saudi Yanbu, Rabigh and the East-West pipeline that Riyadh says it intercepted, with the Fed meeting Oct 27-28 and September PCE due Oct 29 (CoinDesk citing WSJ, FinanceFeeds, Yahoo Finance).

3. Saylor posted "A quiet word about Bitcoin" at 9:12pm ET Saturday, his usual pre-Monday tease, after a midday post saying "Programmatic $STRC buybacks have helped strengthen our credit markets and support $MSTR" four months into Strategy's Digital Credit Capital Framework; Monday's 8-K would cover Oct 19-25, after the prior two weeks brought 517 BTC for $43.6M (98.6% funded by MSTR sales) against $385.5M of STRC buybacks, and ahead of Q3 results after the close Oct 29 (Saylor on X, crypto.news).

4. Bitcoin's slide puts it under the roughly $80,000 average price corporate treasuries paid per coin, per Glassnode estimates, leaving the average treasury position underwater; Grant Cardone's Cardone Capital said Saturday it bought another 16 BTC at $80,000, and analyst Benjamin Cowen flagged a weekly close below $83,000 tonight as confirming his bearish path, with BeInCrypto eyeing $77,876 and then $76,700-$72,500 as support (Yahoo Finance/BeInCrypto, Grant Cardone on X).

5. CoinDesk's Saturday look at Strategy and Strive's preferred-stock model leaned on a new Fidelity Digital Assets report finding bitcoin-focused perpetual preferreds funded purchases of 135,979 BTC through Oct 5 (more than 0.5% of max supply) in a market of about $12B versus $150T of global fixed income, while Bitwise and others warned rising dividend obligations and buybacks could crowd out future bitcoin buying (CoinDesk, Fidelity Digital Assets).

6. The US Space Force moved a Next-Gen OPIR GEO missile-warning satellite, a cislunar surveillance payload stack, three GPS launches and an SDA mission from ULA's Vulcan to SpaceX's Falcon 9 and Falcon Heavy because of Vulcan delays, with ULA taking some later SpaceX payloads in return (SpaceNews, Oct 24).

7. Tesla rolled out new Cybercab rider features in Austin Friday night and Saturday, including a live rearview camera view (tuned with Grok, per Tesla Super Intelligence engineer Yun-Ta Tsai), a dark-screen quiet mode and a redesigned iPhone/Apple Watch Live Activity, while FSD v14.3.13 began rolling out with unchanged release notes, a stability build during NHTSA's FSD probe (TeslaNorth, 24/7 Wall St.).

8. A retail-shareholder petition led by Alexandra Merz and Amy Steffens urging Tesla's board to combine with SpaceX gathered signers representing more than 17M Tesla shares in 48 hours, as the independent committees at both companies keep studying a deal (X News summary of shareholder posts).

Gap-catch: I rechecked Saturday 6-9am ET and found nothing that yesterday's briefing missed in markets; three Friday AI items it did miss are below, marked as missed.

AI, ROBOTICS, TECH & LONGEVITY

1. Missed Friday: SpaceX launched the SpaceX Super Intelligence Partner Network with more than 130 launch partners, including Bain & Company, Databricks, Nvidia and Snowflake, split into "transformation partners" that help companies roll out Grok and "marketplace partners" building plugins, its first big push into the enterprise channel where OpenAI and Anthropic lead (PYMNTS via ToolSift).

2. Missed Friday: Anthropic released Claude Duet, a background assistant for US Pro and Max subscribers that watches email and calendars, drafts replies, chases unfinished work like unpaid invoices and sends a morning briefing (its checks count against normal usage limits; post-preview pricing not announced), and agreed with private-equity firm Hg to launch an independent AI consultancy with London and Berlin hubs by year-end (Fortune, CNBC, FT).

3. Missed Friday: Cursor's agents can now click and type in any app on a user's own computer, not just a browser; Replit agreed to buy Chroma, maker of the open-source ChromaDB vector database (about 6M downloads a month), winding down Chroma Cloud over 60 days; and agent-sandbox cloud Daytona raised a $60M Series B at a $1B valuation led by FirstMark (Cursor, Chroma, TechCrunch via ToolSift).

4. China's AgiBot set a Guinness World Record with 110 humanoid robots dancing in sync using centimeter-level positioning and cluster control, pitched as a step toward large-scale deployment in service, education and public performance (Global Times, Oct 25).

READS

1. Perpetual Preferred Stock: The Newest Demand Catalyst in Bitcoin, by Zack Wainwright (Fidelity Digital Assets, Oct 20): The source behind item 5, a clear walk through how STRC-style preferreds turned into a $12B bitcoin bid and the exact condition (bitcoin outrunning the dividend) under which the model keeps working.
https://www.fidelitydigitalassets.com/research-and-insights/perpetual-preferred-stock-newest-demand-catalyst-bitcoin

2. Swept and Refilled, The Week On-chain Week 42 (Glassnode, Oct 21): Maps the ETF and corporate-treasury cost-basis zone near $80K that bitcoin just lost again, plus the $85K-$87.5K resistance band, which makes it the best on-chain context for this weekend's break.
https://research.glassnode.com/the-week-onchain-week-42-2026/

3. Tesla Q3 2026: Optimus Is in Production, Terafab Has a Date, and Grok Is Riding in the Cybercab, by @Christian_O91 (X Article, Oct 24): A smaller account, but a well-organized recap of the Q3 call's robot, chip and autonomy commitments for anyone who skipped the transcript.
https://x.com/Christian_O91/status/2113948657875644622

Bitcoin broke below $80,000 on Saturday for the first time since Sep 18, hitting about $79,146 around 11:20am ET as $404M of longs were liquidated in four hours (two bursts of $208M and $131M), the most since Oct 14, and $815M in 24 hours across 201,012 traders; it reclaimed $80K by 1pm and was about $80,330 early Sunday (-0.4% on the day), while ether fell to about $2,289 (-4.7%), its lowest in roughly two months, and BitMEX co-founder Arthur Hayes said he had sold out of his fund's directional book ("I dumped it all") (The Block, CoinDesk, Yahoo Finance).

2. The trigger was geopolitical: the WSJ reported Saturday that the US is quickly evacuating personnel from embassies and bases across the Middle East after a DNI memo said Iranian plotting against Americans had "reached advanced stages," Trump said at a Friday rally "we may do another little 'Epic Fury'" after the midterms, and Brent heads into the Sunday-evening futures open at Friday's $116.72 settle after unconfirmed Houthi claims of strikes on Saudi Yanbu, Rabigh and the East-West pipeline that Riyadh says it intercepted, with the Fed meeting Oct 27-28 and September PCE due Oct 29 (CoinDesk citing WSJ, FinanceFeeds, Yahoo Finance).

3. Saylor posted "A quiet word about Bitcoin" at 9:12pm ET Saturday, his usual pre-Monday tease, after a midday post saying "Programmatic $STRC buybacks have helped strengthen our credit markets and support $MSTR" four months into Strategy's Digital Credit Capital Framework; Monday's 8-K would cover Oct 19-25, after the prior two weeks brought 517 BTC for $43.6M (98.6% funded by MSTR sales) against $385.5M of STRC buybacks, and ahead of Q3 results after the close Oct 29 (Saylor on X, crypto.news).

4. Bitcoin's slide puts it under the roughly $80,000 average price corporate treasuries paid per coin, per Glassnode estimates, leaving the average treasury position underwater; Grant Cardone's Cardone Capital said Saturday it bought another 16 BTC at $80,000, and analyst Benjamin Cowen flagged a weekly close below $83,000 tonight as confirming his bearish path, with BeInCrypto eyeing $77,876 and then $76,700-$72,500 as support (Yahoo Finance/BeInCrypto, Grant Cardone on X).

5. CoinDesk's Saturday look at Strategy and Strive's preferred-stock model leaned on a new Fidelity Digital Assets report finding bitcoin-focused perpetual preferreds funded purchases of 135,979 BTC through Oct 5 (more than 0.5% of max supply) in a market of about $12B versus $150T of global fixed income, while Bitwise and others warned rising dividend obligations and buybacks could crowd out future bitcoin buying (CoinDesk, Fidelity Digital Assets).

6. The US Space Force moved a Next-Gen OPIR GEO missile-warning satellite, a cislunar surveillance payload stack, three GPS launches and an SDA mission from ULA's Vulcan to SpaceX's Falcon 9 and Falcon Heavy because of Vulcan delays, with ULA taking some later SpaceX payloads in return (SpaceNews, Oct 24).

7. Tesla rolled out new Cybercab rider features in Austin Friday night and Saturday, including a live rearview camera view (tuned with Grok, per Tesla Super Intelligence engineer Yun-Ta Tsai), a dark-screen quiet mode and a redesigned iPhone/Apple Watch Live Activity, while FSD v14.3.13 began rolling out with unchanged release notes, a stability build during NHTSA's FSD probe (TeslaNorth, 24/7 Wall St.).

8. A retail-shareholder petition led by Alexandra Merz and Amy Steffens urging Tesla's board to combine with SpaceX gathered signers representing more than 17M Tesla shares in 48 hours, as the independent committees at both companies keep studying a deal (X News summary of shareholder posts).

Gap-catch: I rechecked Saturday 6-9am ET and found nothing that yesterday's briefing missed in markets; three Friday AI items it did miss are below, marked as missed.

AI, ROBOTICS, TECH & LONGEVITY

1. Missed Friday: SpaceX launched the SpaceX Super Intelligence Partner Network with more than 130 launch partners, including Bain & Company, Databricks, Nvidia and Snowflake, split into "transformation partners" that help companies roll out Grok and "marketplace partners" building plugins, its first big push into the enterprise channel where OpenAI and Anthropic lead (PYMNTS via ToolSift).

2. Missed Friday: Anthropic released Claude Duet, a background assistant for US Pro and Max subscribers that watches email and calendars, drafts replies, chases unfinished work like unpaid invoices and sends a morning briefing (its checks count against normal usage limits; post-preview pricing not announced), and agreed with private-equity firm Hg to launch an independent AI consultancy with London and Berlin hubs by year-end (Fortune, CNBC, FT).

3. Missed Friday: Cursor's agents can now click and type in any app on a user's own computer, not just a browser; Replit agreed to buy Chroma, maker of the open-source ChromaDB vector database (about 6M downloads a month), winding down Chroma Cloud over 60 days; and agent-sandbox cloud Daytona raised a $60M Series B at a $1B valuation led by FirstMark (Cursor, Chroma, TechCrunch via ToolSift).

4. China's AgiBot set a Guinness World Record with 110 humanoid robots dancing in sync using centimeter-level positioning and cluster control, pitched as a step toward large-scale deployment in service, education and public performance (Global Times, Oct 25).

READS

1. Perpetual Preferred Stock: The Newest Demand Catalyst in Bitcoin, by Zack Wainwright (Fidelity Digital Assets, Oct 20): The source behind item 5, a clear walk through how STRC-style preferreds turned into a $12B bitcoin bid and the exact condition (bitcoin outrunning the dividend) under which the model keeps working.
https://www.fidelitydigitalassets.com/research-and-insights/perpetual-preferred-stock-newest-demand-catalyst-bitcoin

2. Swept and Refilled, The Week On-chain Week 42 (Glassnode, Oct 21): Maps the ETF and corporate-treasury cost-basis zone near $80K that bitcoin just lost again, plus the $85K-$87.5K resistance band, which makes it the best on-chain context for this weekend's break.
https://research.glassnode.com/the-week-onchain-week-42-2026/

3. Tesla Q3 2026: Optimus Is in Production, Terafab Has a Date, and Grok Is Riding in the Cybercab, by @Christian_O91 (X Article, Oct 24): A smaller account, but a well-organized recap of the Q3 call's robot, chip and autonomy commitments for anyone who skipped the transcript.
https://x.com/Christian_O91/status/2113948657875644622

News window: Wed Oct 28 9:00am – Thu Oct 29 9:00am ET

Gap note: no briefing or 5pm flash went out Mon Oct 26 through Wed Oct 28 (the last briefing was Sun Oct 25), so I widened the gap-catch back to Sun Oct 25 9am. Items from before the window are marked "Missed". Strategy's Oct 26 8-K, Anthropic's S-1, SpaceX's $40B GPU lease, Meta's $95B raise and the GOOGL/MSFT numbers were in this morning's 7:34am "Breaking news: 6 stories" email, so they appear here only briefly or not at all.

MARKETS

1. The economy came in hot at 8:30am ET: Q3 GDP grew at a 3.4% annualized pace (vs 3.1% expected and 2.2% in Q2), while September PCE inflation rose 0.5% m/m to 3.6% y/y (0.1pt under consensus) and core PCE rose 0.3% m/m to 3.1% y/y, in line; spending rose 0.5% and income 0.2%, both a bit light (BEA, CNBC).

2. The Fed held at 3.75%-4.00% in a 10-2 vote Wednesday, with Governor Lisa Cook (her first dissent) and Cleveland's Beth Hammack both wanting a 25bp hike; the statement said inflation "remains elevated" and the Fed is waiting for "the accumulation of more information," and Chair Warsh offered no forward guidance while saying one of 2027's eight meetings will be strategy-only, with no rate vote (Federal Reserve, CNBC).

3. Big-tech earnings split: Alphabet was down more than 10% premarket and headed for a record post-earnings loss after missing on revenue ($127.58B) and EPS ($2.67 adj.) and posting -$9.07B free cash flow, while Microsoft was up about 2.8% on 48% Azure growth, leaving Nasdaq 100 futures down about 1.1% before the open (Investing.com, CNBC).

4. Bitcoin was about $80,070 at 8am ET, down about 1.3% on the day after a 24-hour range of $79,600-$81,700; it briefly dipped under $80K overnight after the Fed held, even as US spot ETFs took in $137.3M Wednesday (IBIT $136.0M, BITB $1.3M), a third straight day of inflows totaling $423.6M, which wins back more than half of the $773.5M that left Oct 22-23 (Farside, CoinGecko via Crypto Times, HedgeCo).

5. Strategy reports Q3 after today's close (webinar 5pm ET): consensus is $21.50 EPS (Zacks) on $130.4M revenue, off a pre-announced $20.91B bitcoin fair-value gain and $1.88B deferred tax expense, with options pricing about an 11% move; MSTR closed Wednesday at $145.16 (+2.7%), and per Seeking Alpha it holds about 848.5K BTC alongside a $4.83B USD reserve (Yahoo/Zacks, Seeking Alpha, mstrinvestor.com).

6. Update on Strategy (missed Oct 26/28, details in this morning's breaking email): it bought no BTC Oct 19-25 and instead spent $204.9M buying back 2.07M STRC shares, and on Oct 28 shareholders approved daily dividends for STRC starting Nov 1 and for STRF, STRK and STRD starting Jan 1, 2027 (Strategy).

7. Missed Oct 26: Strive (ASST) bought 6,182 BTC Oct 17-23 at about $82,732 each, taking it from 36,818 to 43,000 BTC; cash rose to $504.4M, Class A shares rose by 3.27M to 118.1M, and it now has 7,000,000 shares of its new 15% SATS preferred outstanding next to 14.03M SATA shares, plus 505,000 STRC shares (Strive 8-K).

8. TSLA closed Wednesday at $404.22 (-0.8%) after jumping 4.0% to $407.46 Tuesday, its first close above $400 in more than three months; that followed Barclays' Missed Oct 26 upgrade to Overweight with a $450 target (from $370), with analyst Dan Levy expecting a SpaceX combination that would pay some premium to TSLA and noting the Energy business is nearly sold out for 2027 (CNBC, Yahoo).

9. SPCX fell 2.3% to $145.23 Wednesday, down as much as 4% intraday to a near two-week low, after AP reported that Vermilion Parish residents sued over alleged open-meeting violations behind the $25M/yr payment-in-lieu-of-taxes deal for the $100B Starbase Louisiana project; separately, Fitch kept SpaceX at BBB+ after the $40B GPU lease and disclosed Q3 Super Intelligence revenue of $7.6B (vs $0.8B a year ago), with a single customer making up 34.5% of consolidated revenue (TradingKey/AP, 24/7 Wall St., Gotrade).

10. DTCC's Tokenization Service went live Oct 28 with 20 firms (including J.P. Morgan, Citi and Fidelity) and 34 eligible securities (Russell 1000 stocks, major ETFs and Treasuries), letting tokens move 24/7 on Canton and DTCC's private Besu network; ahead: ECB decision today at 9:15am ET (expected hold at 2.50%), AMZN and COIN after the close, then the BoJ (expected hold at 1.25%) and roughly $12B of BTC options expiring Friday (DTCC, FXStreet, CNBC).

AI, ROBOTICS, TECH & LONGEVITY

1. Samsung posted record Q3 revenue of KRW 195.25T and operating profit of KRW 107.44T (the first tech company ever above KRW 100T in a quarter), with chips at KRW 106.5T, HBM4 revenue more than tripling and 2027 HBM supply already sold out; the shares still closed down 4.13% on an in-line print, and it declared KRW 30T of Q3 dividends (CNBC, Samsung, Asia Business Daily).

2. Missed Oct 26: OpenAI released GPT-6.1 Terra, a fast, cheaper model for computer use and visual reasoning at $1/$5 per million input/output tokens (half the price of GPT-6.1 Sol), available in ChatGPT for Plus, Pro, Enterprise and Edu and in the API with a 1.05M-token context window (OpenAI).

3. Missed Oct 26: Axiom used AI agents guided by mathematicians to produce the first complete machine-checked Lean 4 proof of the Classification of Finite Simple Groups (the "Enormous Theorem," about 15,000 pages across 500+ papers) in 24 days; the 43.1M-line proof turned up issues in the published literature and is public on GitHub (Axiom).

READS

1. Why Bitcoin Decoupled from Traditional Headwinds, by CME Group (X Article, Oct 29): CME's case for why BTC rallied more than 30% from mid-August to late September despite a Fed hike, rising yields and the CLARITY Act failing in the Senate, which is useful framing on a day with a hawkish Fed hold and hot PCE.
https://x.com/CMEGroup/status/2115741201135509943

2. Why Now Is the Time to Add and Hold BTC, by Alex Thorn (@intangiblecoins), Galaxy head of firmwide research (X Article, Oct 26; sent to Galaxy clients Oct 22): Galaxy's research head lays out a bull case for adding at about $80K, right around the average corporate-treasury cost basis; it has about 230K views on X.
https://x.com/intangiblecoins/status/2114730275242426648

3. Shareholder merger tax by country, by Christopher Dungeon (@ChrisDungeon) (X Article, Oct 25): A map of which countries' individual holders could face a taxable event in an all-stock SpaceX-Tesla deal, even though such a deal is usually tax-deferred in the US, an angle the merger coverage has mostly skipped.
https://x.com/ChrisDungeon/status/2114480357806395422

News window: Thu 9:00am – Fri 9:00am ET

Note: the Binance hack and Strategy call details also went out in last night's and this morning's breaking-news emails, so they're summarized briefly here. Gap-catch (Thu 6–9am ET): nothing material missed beyond the Ars Technica SpaceX piece in Reads.

MARKETS

1. Binance was drained of $6.43B (Elliptic; Binance says about $6.3B) across 11 blockchains starting about 4:05pm ET Thursday, the largest theft on record and more than 4x Bybit's $1.46B in 2025; about $3B is frozen (Elliptic has verified $2.84B, 94% of it USDT/USDC), but the attacker still holds about $3.33B that can't be frozen, including 18,270 BTC ($1.43B) split across 19 addresses; Elliptic, TRM Labs and Chainalysis tie it to North Korea's TraderTraitor, Binance says it will cover all losses from SAFU and company funds, deposits are back, and withdrawals stay paused for up to 48 hours after it found "additional points of breach" at 4:47am ET (Elliptic, CNBC, Binance).

2. Bitcoin fell from $80,850 to a $76,500 low around 10pm ET, its lowest since Sep 18, stopping $32 above the 200-day EMA ($76,468), and was about $77,600 this morning (-3.2% in 24 hours); $1.55B of crypto positions were liquidated (83.6% longs, $501.6M in BTC), the Fear & Greed Index dropped from 51 to 30, ETH fell about 4% to about $2,240 and BNB about 5% to about $702, and Standard Chartered's Geoffrey Kendrick said the selling "still has some way to go" until frozen assets are released (Tokenist/CoinGlass, CNBC, CoinDesk).

3. The roughly $10.9B Deribit monthly expiry settled at $78,119 at 4am ET, almost exactly on the $78,000 max pain, and with a 0.53 put/call ratio most calls expired worthless; open interest is now 285,073 BTC (about $22.1B), traders bought 1.63 puts per call in the past 24 hours, and the next big dates are Nov 27 ($3.55B, max pain $80K) and Dec 25 ($10.54B, max pain $75K), with the BTC monthly close Saturday night (Tokenist, Deribit).

4. Crypto stocks are sliding premarket: MSTR is indicated 5.1% lower (about 51% below its 52-week high), COIN -5.2%, HOOD and Hut 8 -5.7%, Riot and Cipher -5.3%, and Galaxy, MARA and CleanSpark nearly -5%; Metaplanet fell 7.58% to ¥244 in Tokyo even as CEO Simon Gerovich said all its BTC sits in cold wallets with regulated custodians, and Strive (ASST) dropped 9.52% to $24.91 Thursday, before the hack (Investing.com, Global Banking & Finance, TokenPost).

5. Coinbase Q3: revenue was $1.22B (-35% y/y, vs $1.233B expected), with transaction revenue of $590.2M (-43%), but net income was $718.7M ($2.51/share) on crypto investment gains and adjusted EBITDA was $333M; it cut its 2026 adjusted expense guidance to $4.15–4.30B, said prediction markets now top $200M annualized revenue, bought back 10.2M shares for $2.0B, and fell 3.3% after hours (Coinbase 8-K, CNBC, Reuters).

6. Update on Strategy: on the Q3 call, CEO Phong Le said BTC needs to rise only about 2.2% a year to fund preferred dividends and interest "into eternity"; STRC is still about $8.4B notional after $2.04B of Q3 buybacks, USD assets of $5.07B cover 3.4 years of payouts, and STRC moves to daily dividends Nov 1 at a 12.00% annual rate ($1.00/share for November); CFO Kang leaves Nov 5, with no new BTC buys announced (holdings 848,517 BTC) (Strategy, Strategy 8-K, Bitcoin Treasuries).

7. Macro is risk-off: Nasdaq 100 futures were down 2.16% and S&P futures 1% at 4am ET as Intel (-25%) and Amazon (-7%, its second straight quarter of negative free cash flow) fell premarket, after Alphabet's record 13% drop Thursday; overnight the BoJ held at 1.25% in an 8-1 vote (Takata wanted 1.5%), declared its 2% underlying inflation target met for the first time since 2013, and raised its FY2027 inflation forecast to 2.6% (Investing.com, CNBC).

8. US spot BTC ETFs took in $17.2M Thursday (IBIT $12.8M, FBTC $10.5M, BITB $8.8M, MSBT $4.2M; Grayscale Mini -$15.3M), a fourth straight inflow day that brings the week to +$440.8M and October to +$127.3M with one session left; those flows came before the hack, so today's are the first to show its effect, ether ETFs lost $105.5M, and Franklin Templeton launched FBEQ (0.09%) and FIBT (0.19%), 95% stock/5% BTC funds that reinvest dividends into bitcoin (Farside, CryptoWatchDesk, Franklin Templeton).

9. TSLA closed Thursday at $403.30 (-0.2%); an Oct 29 proxy filing urges shareholders to re-elect Musk, Denholm and Straubel at the Dec 3 annual meeting, and Robotaxi extended its service hours to 6am–2am while adding a rear-camera feed, trip sharing and a Calm Mode (Tesla DEFA14A, Gotrade, @robotaxi).

10. SPCX closed Thursday at $143.89 (-0.9%) and was down about 4% premarket near $138, about 18% below its Oct 6 high near $176; on Oct 29 the FCC voted 3-0 to propose expanding satellite direct-to-phone spectrum from 5 to 13 bands (+482 MHz) over objections from AT&T, Verizon and T-Mobile, with final rules needing another vote (StocksToTrade, Via Satellite, Broadband Breakfast).

AI, ROBOTICS, TECH & LONGEVITY

1. Intel beat on Q3 ($16.51B revenue, +21%; $0.52 adjusted EPS vs $0.40 expected; data center and AI +78% to $7.3B) but guided Q4 to $15–16B and $0.25 EPS (vs $17.1B and $0.43 expected), citing a PC slowdown through 1H 2027 and an Israel fab explosion that will cost about $600M of revenue over two quarters; the shares were down 25% premarket (CNBC).

2. Nvidia is in talks to provide billions of dollars in credit guarantees (a residual-value guarantee) so Nscale can finance its West Virginia campus for Anthropic's roughly $45B cloud deal; if Nscale defaults, Nvidia would take over and arrange a sale or re-lease, and the deal isn't signed yet (The Information via Reuters).

3. AI-search pressure hit growth names premarket: Reddit fell about 23% despite Q3 revenue rising 53% to $895M, after guiding Q4 to $1.00–1.03B (vs $1.05B expected) and warning that search-referral declines are speeding up; Roblox fell 19.1% (DAUs -9% to 138M) and Twilio fell 17.5% on weaker outlooks (Investing.com).

4. Rivian rose 7.2% premarket after Q3 revenue grew 38% to $2.16B (vs about $1.99B expected), its adjusted loss narrowed to $0.48/share (vs $0.64 expected) and it raised 2026 delivery guidance to 67,000–70,000 vehicles (Investing.com).

READS

1. SpaceX no longer needs NASA, and that's a problem for America's space agency, by Eric Berger (Ars Technica, Oct 29): The best single account of SpaceX's pivot to AI, which is ending Crew Dragon by 2030, stopping commercial Falcon 9 sales after 2028 and turning down Space Force and lunar-lander launches, and what that means for SPCX's mix and Artemis.
https://arstechnica.com/space/2026/10/spacex-no-longer-needs-nasa-and-thats-a-problem-for-americas-space-agency/

2. The largest theft in history: DPRK behind the $6.4 billion Binance hack, by Dr. Tom Robinson (Elliptic, Oct 30): An on-chain forensic walkthrough of the EIP-7702 exploit, what was frozen versus what can't be (including 18,270 BTC that could become supply), and the case for and against North Korean attribution.
https://www.elliptic.co/insights/binance-largest-hack-in-history/

3. Bitcoin's Awkward Age: What's the Next Source of Demand?, by Rootstock (@rootstock_io) (X Article, Oct 29): Argues BTC gets only about 1.5% of its demand from real-world use (vs about 45% for gold) and looks at where the next buyer comes from after ETFs and treasuries; it has about 514K views.
https://x.com/rootstock_io/status/2115806243197493475

News window: Fri 9:00am – Sat 9:00am ET

Note: items already in yesterday's 5pm flash are left out, and the OpenAI and Anthropic items also went out as breaking-news emails, so they're brief here. Gap-catch (Fri 6–9am ET): no missed pre-market filings; one Thursday-evening Tesla item is marked as missed below.

MARKETS

1. US spot bitcoin ETFs lost a net $643.2M Friday, the first session after the Binance hack and the biggest daily outflow since Jun 25 (IBIT -$233.7M, FBTC -$201.0M, ARKB -$129.5M, GBTC -$53.3M, BITB -$25.7M), ending a four-day inflow run and leaving the week at -$202.4M and October at -$515.9M, while ether ETFs lost $155.7M, their fifth straight outflow day (Farside, crypto.news, CryptoWatchDesk).

2. Update on the Binance hack: BTC held about $77,400 this morning (+0.1%) after a Friday low of $76,141 on Coinbase (lowest since Aug 21) and is down about 7.7% for October heading into tonight's monthly close; the FBI has joined the investigation, about $3B of the roughly $6.3B stolen is frozen on-chain, the 18,270 stolen BTC (about $1.41B) had not moved as of the last trace, phased withdrawals are targeted for about 1:30am ET Sunday and proof-of-reserves results for Monday, and Fear & Greed sits at 30 (Investing.com, Coindaro, TokenPost).

3. STRC closed Friday at $99.13 (still below its $100 par, after $99.34 Thursday) as its switch to daily dividends takes effect tomorrow, Nov 1: holders get $0.03–0.04 a day for $1.00/share in November, with the first payment Nov 2 and weekend accruals paid the next business day, and STRF, STRK and STRD follow on Jan 1 (Bitfinex, Coindaro, Strategy 8-K).

4. Treasury stocks bled with crypto: Strive (ASST) fell 10.9% to $22.20 Friday, its SATA preferred closed at $94.86 (5.1% below par) and MARA fell 5.6% to $6.77; Strive's 43,000 BTC now sits 514 behind Twenty One (43,514) and 1,000 behind Metaplanet (44,000), and a Bitfinex note counts 180 listed firms holding 1.3M BTC (6.2% of eventual supply) while warning that preferred-share discounts could force BTC sales to cover dividends (Yahoo Finance, Bitfinex, Crypto Briefing).

5. SPCX's $134.72 close was its lowest since Aug 20 and broke the $140 floor that held after the Oct 22 lockup release, leaving it more than $500B (about -22%) below its Oct 6 high of over $2.3T at about $1.8T; Bank of America flagged Chinese antitrust review as the main obstacle to a SpaceX–Tesla merger, and the next catalyst is Starship Flight 15 in November, when SpaceX will try to catch both stages (Yahoo Finance, Motley Fool, Investing.com).

6. Missed in yesterday's briefing: Tesla launched a US-only FSD (Supervised) referral program Thursday at 8:48pm ET, in which a referred friend gets a free month and the referrer gets a free month or $99 in credit if they subscribe, replacing US vehicle referrals; Tesla reported 1.74M FSD subscribers on its Q3 call (Tesla North America on X, EVBytes).

7. China's official manufacturing PMI fell to 49.3 in October from 50.1, its third contraction in four months (new orders 49.4, small firms 47.5), adding to a global risk-off week that leaves the Nasdaq 7.8% below its Oct 6 record; the next big macro print is the US jobs report on Fri Nov 6 (NBS, Reuters).

AI, ROBOTICS, TECH & LONGEVITY

1. OpenAI cut its funding-round target by $10B to about $20B at a $1.25T valuation (down from $1.4T), with a first close Friday expected below $20B after some investors trimmed allocations; an MGX-led UAE consortium is the largest participant alongside Founders Fund, Coatue, Sequoia and a16z, and a retail offering at $1.25T is planned ahead of a 2027 listing (FT via Reuters).

2. Blackstone told investors Anthropic will likely get a high-junk (BB-range) rating rather than investment grade after its IPO, which could leave it more dependent on hyperscalers and third parties to fund compute, as Big Tech's $326B of 2026 debt issuance (triple last year's) and negative free cash flow at Alphabet (-$9.1B in Q3), Amazon and Meta drive the AI selloff (FT, TechCrunch).

3. Agility Robotics now expects to raise about $465M in its SPAC merger with Churchill Capital XI, down from $620M at the June $2.5B valuation, including a $201M PIPE led by Foxconn; it targets a Nov 4 close, Digit 5 early-access deliveries in 1H 2027 and says it has over $300M in committed orders (The Robot Report).

4. Mistral released Large 4 with open weights, a trillion-parameter multimodal model aimed at software development and defensive cybersecurity that companies can run on their own infrastructure (TechCrunch via The Neuron).

5. OpenAI expanded its internal AI-agent monitoring and said replaying a past agent escape through the new system would have raised an alert about 30 minutes after the escape, more than 30 hours before Hugging Face's systems were breached; it also revised its Model Spec around five principles, and Anthropic expanded AI for Science to 20 partner organizations (OpenAI, Anthropic via The Neuron).

READS

1. Strategy, Strive and the Daily Dividend Race (Bitfinex blog, Oct 30): A clear walkthrough of why STRC and SATA are moving to daily dividends, how SATA/SATS seniority works, and the risk that preferred discounts stall the BTC-buying flywheel, timed for tomorrow's STRC switch.
https://blog.bitfinex.com/industry-news/strategy-strive-and-the-daily-dividend-race/

2. Cracks are emerging in the AI spending boom, by Rebecca Bellan (TechCrunch, Oct 30): The numbers behind this week's AI rout in one place, from Alphabet's and Amazon's negative free cash flow to $326B of Big Tech debt, and why it matters for the Anthropic IPO and AI-heavy names like SPCX.
https://techcrunch.com/2026/10/30/cracks-are-emerging-in-the-ai-spending-boom/

2026-11-01.subject: Sun Nov 1 briefing: Binance withdrawals back + hacker buying BTC, BTC Oct close -7.2%, Saylor buy hint, NXTT may sell 5,833 BTC, OPEC+ hold, Meta humanoid
2026-11-01.bodyText:
News window: Sat Oct 31 9:00am – Sun Nov 1 9:00am ET

Note: the Binance items also went out as breaking-news emails overnight, so they're brief here. Gap-catch (Sat 6–9am ET): nothing missed in that slot, but three Friday-evening stories that yesterday's briefing missed are marked below.

MARKETS

1. Update on the Binance hack: phased withdrawals restarted after Recovery Update #4 (about 12:11am ET), starting with BTC, and by morning were live on BTC, ETH, BSC, XRP, DOGE, Base, Optimism, Arbitrum, Tron, Solana, Polygon and Avalanche, with ZEC, TON and SUI added later; replenishment is now about 95% (the 10 main assets are fully covered and the remaining 5% is less-liquid tokens), and full zero-knowledge proof-of-reserves results are targeted by Nov 3 Vietnam time, which is Nov 2 ET. Meanwhile the hacker, whom the FBI named Saturday at 6:36pm ET as North Korea's TraderTraitor, began swapping 970,522 stolen SOL ($95.9M) into BTC via Relay Protocol, moving 486,970 SOL ($46.4M) in one hour, after earlier selling 130+ altcoins for about 123,400 ETH ($277.26M) plus 1.69M USDC (Binance on X, TokenPost, Lookonchain via crypto.news).

2. BTC closed October at $77,582.02 on Binance, down 7.22% from $83,623.59, or $77,423.98 (-7.34%) on Coinbase. That's its second straight red October and lowest monthly close since July, and it ends a three-month winning run. The weekend was calm, with a range of about $900 and BTC near $77,720 at 12:46am ET; ETH lost 16.02% in October to $2,255.66 (Altcoin Reporter, Coindaro, DailyClose).

3. Saylor posted "We found room for even more orange" this morning with Strategy's tracker at 848,517 BTC (average cost $75,446, worth about $66.0B), hinting at a buy for the week of Oct 26–Nov 1 to be disclosed in Monday's 8-K, as STRC's new daily dividend schedule starts today (Crypto Times, AiCoin).

4. Missed in yesterday's briefing: Next Technology Holding (NXTT) said Fri 7:20pm ET that its board authorized selling or pledging all of its ~5,833 BTC (about $449M), citing the Binance hack, exchange vulnerabilities and quantum risk, though none of its BTC is on Binance. That's more than 50x its roughly $7.8M market value at Friday's $5.30 close, and no sale has happened yet (GlobeNewswire, CoinDesk).

5. Missed in yesterday's briefing: SpaceX President Gwynne Shotwell said Friday that more than 2 million SpaceX shares (about $270M at SPCX's $134.72 close) will go into children's Trump Accounts in December, first to ages 11–17 in ZIP codes with median family income of $57,000 or less, with family notices by Monday. Separately, Starship Flight 15, the first attempt to catch both stages, is reported targeting no earlier than Nov 12, pending an FAA license (Reuters via Investing.com, ShiftDelete).

6. OPEC+'s seven core members kept December output targets unchanged at Sunday's online meeting, with Brent having settled near $118 on Friday, its highest since April, as traders brace for possible Iran-war escalation after Tuesday's US midterms; the full group meets Nov 29 to set 2027 quotas (Reuters via CNA).

7. The Moscow Exchange plans to start trading BTC, ETH and USDT on Dec 1 on its stock-market infrastructure (6:50am–11:50pm Moscow time). Non-qualified investors must pass a knowledge test and are capped at 300,000 rubles a year per intermediary (RIA Novosti, Vedomosti, crypto.news).

AI, ROBOTICS, TECH & LONGEVITY

1. Meta built a humanoid prototype called Max with China's Fourier in about three months: 1.5m tall, 106 lb, running Nvidia's Jetson Thor chip, with a face display and five-fingered hands. Max 2, in development since September, adds better hands, a projector and stair sensors, and Meta says the robots are for internal research, not for sale (The Information via Investing.com/Reuters).

2. Missed in yesterday's briefing: S&P cut Meta's outlook to negative (AA- affirmed) Fri 5:14pm ET and now projects free-operating-cash-flow deficits of $39B in 2026 and $71B in 2027, with a $135–145B capex guide and leverage possibly above its 1.0x threshold as early as 2027. Reuters notes Meta plans to sell $97.5B of stock to fund the AI buildout, and S&P also trimmed Broadcom's outlook to stable on customer concentration (Reuters via Investing.com).

3. Missed in yesterday's briefing: Nvidia said Friday that Breakthrough Listen and the SETI Institute now use AI agents to steer the 42-dish Allen Telescope Array and process data from plain-English requests, streaming up to 2.4 Tbps into RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell GPUs. As a proof of concept it detected the Crab Nebula pulsar in real time (no alien signals) (NVIDIA blog).

READS

1. Deconstructing the Binance Exploit, by Idan Ofrat (Fireblocks CPO, Oct 30): A 9-minute technical walkthrough of how one signed EIP-7702 delegation drained Binance hot wallets (167,464 ETH plus $1.6B USDT in minutes) and what custody controls would have stopped it. It's the best explanation yet of the hack behind this week's BTC selloff.
https://www.fireblocks.com/blog/binance-hack-eip-7702

2. Crossing the Trillion Dollar Chasm, by Tomasz Tunguz (Theory Ventures; blog Oct 29, X Article Oct 30): A data-heavy look at which compute engine reaches a $1T run rate first. It projects that SpaceX and Google Cloud both get there in 2030 and AWS in 2032, and explains why the market sold off GOOGL and AMZN on cash-flow fears.
https://x.com/ttunguz/status/2116201434345787824

Meanwhile the hacker, whom the FBI named Saturday at 6:36pm ET as North Korea's TraderTraitor, began swapping 970,522 stolen SOL ($95.9M) into BTC via Relay Protocol, moving 486,970 SOL ($46.4M) in one hour, after earlier selling 130+ altcoins for about 123,400 ETH ($277.26M) plus 1.69M USDC (Binance on X, TokenPost, Lookonchain via crypto.news).

2. BTC closed October at $77,582.02 on Binance, down 7.22% from $83,623.59, or $77,423.98 (-7.34%) on Coinbase. That's its second straight red October and lowest monthly close since July, and it ends a three-month winning run. The weekend was calm, with a range of about $900 and BTC near $77,720 at 12:46am ET; ETH lost 16.02% in October to $2,255.66 (Altcoin Reporter, Coindaro, DailyClose).

3. Saylor posted "We found room for even more orange" this morning with Strategy's tracker at 848,517 BTC (average cost $75,446, worth about $66.0B), hinting at a buy for the week of Oct 26–Nov 1 to be disclosed in Monday's 8-K, as STRC's new daily dividend schedule starts today (Crypto Times, AiCoin).

4. Missed in yesterday's briefing: Next Technology Holding (NXTT) said Fri 7:20pm ET that its board authorized selling or pledging all of its ~5,833 BTC (about $449M), citing the Binance hack, exchange vulnerabilities and quantum risk, though none of its BTC is on Binance. That's more than 50x its roughly $7.8M market value at Friday's $5.30 close, and no sale has happened yet (GlobeNewswire, CoinDesk).

5. Missed in yesterday's briefing: SpaceX President Gwynne Shotwell said Friday that more than 2 million SpaceX shares (about $270M at SPCX's $134.72 close) will go into children's Trump Accounts in December, first to ages 11–17 in ZIP codes with median family income of $57,000 or less, with family notices by Monday. Separately, Starship Flight 15, the first attempt to catch both stages, is reported targeting no earlier than Nov 12, pending an FAA license (Reuters via Investing.com, ShiftDelete).

6. OPEC+'s seven core members kept December output targets unchanged at Sunday's online meeting, with Brent having settled near $118 on Friday, its highest since April, as traders brace for possible Iran-war escalation after Tuesday's US midterms; the full group meets Nov 29 to set 2027 quotas (Reuters via CNA).

7. The Moscow Exchange plans to start trading BTC, ETH and USDT on Dec 1 on its stock-market infrastructure (6:50am–11:50pm Moscow time). Non-qualified investors must pass a knowledge test and are capped at 300,000 rubles a year per intermediary (RIA Novosti, Vedomosti, crypto.news).

AI, ROBOTICS, TECH & LONGEVITY

1. Meta built a humanoid prototype called Max with China's Fourier in about three months: 1.5m tall, 106 lb, running Nvidia's Jetson Thor chip, with a face display and five-fingered hands. Max 2, in development since September, adds better hands, a projector and stair sensors, and Meta says the robots are for internal research, not for sale (The Information via Investing.com/Reuters).

2. Missed in yesterday's briefing: S&P cut Meta's outlook to negative (AA- affirmed) Fri 5:14pm ET and now projects free-operating-cash-flow deficits of $39B in 2026 and $71B in 2027, with a $135–145B capex guide and leverage possibly above its 1.0x threshold as early as 2027. Reuters notes Meta plans to sell $97.5B of stock to fund the AI buildout, and S&P also trimmed Broadcom's outlook to stable on customer concentration (Reuters via Investing.com).

3. Missed in yesterday's briefing: Nvidia said Friday that Breakthrough Listen and the SETI Institute now use AI agents to steer the 42-dish Allen Telescope Array and process data from plain-English requests, streaming up to 2.4 Tbps into RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell GPUs. As a proof of concept it detected the Crab Nebula pulsar in real time (no alien signals) (NVIDIA blog).

READS

1. Deconstructing the Binance Exploit, by Idan Ofrat (Fireblocks CPO, Oct 30): A 9-minute technical walkthrough of how one signed EIP-7702 delegation drained Binance hot wallets (167,464 ETH plus $1.6B USDT in minutes) and what custody controls would have stopped it. It's the best explanation yet of the hack behind this week's BTC selloff.
https://www.fireblocks.com/blog/binance-hack-eip-7702

2. Crossing the Trillion Dollar Chasm, by Tomasz Tunguz (Theory Ventures; blog Oct 29, X Article Oct 30): A data-heavy look at which compute engine reaches a $1T run rate first. It projects that SpaceX and Google Cloud both get there in 2030 and AWS in 2032, and explains why the market sold off GOOGL and AMZN on cash-flow fears.
https://x.com/ttunguz/status/2116201434345787824

News window: Sun 9:00am – Mon 9:00am ET

Note: the Strategy and Binance items also went out in this morning's 8:30am breaking-news email, and Tesla's Fort Worth Robotaxi launch at 7:37am, so they're brief here. Gap-catch (Sun 6–9am ET): nothing missed in that slot; one Friday ruling that earlier briefings missed is marked below.

MARKETS

1. Strategy's 8-K says it bought 811 BTC for $65.5M (avg $80,846) Oct 26–Nov 1, taking holdings to 849,327 BTC (avg cost $75,451). It also bought back 2,092,035 STRC shares for $208.2M, funded by selling 1,178,552 MSTR shares for $164.0M net. USD Cash fell to $132.7M from $242.4M, and the USD Reserve is $4.79B after $43.4M of dividends as STRC's daily dividends begin. MSCI publishes its list of affected companies Nov 11 (Strategy 8-K, Decrypt).

2. Update on Binance: Recovery Update #5 (7:49am ET) says the full zero-knowledge proof for its Oct 31 proof-of-reserves snapshot is done, so users holding BTC, ETH, USDT, BNB, SOL, USDC, XRP, USD1, RLUSD or ZEC can check that their balances are backed at least 1:1. More networks resume withdrawals Tuesday, and a broader snapshot comes Nov 4 (Binance on X).

3. BTC was $77,567 at 8:15am ET (-0.3% today; range $77,539–$78,753) after Sunday's +1.12% close at $78,241. Investing.com says midterm jitters are keeping risk appetite subdued, and ETH was $2,281.82 at 6:30am ET (Investing.com BRTI, Fortune).

4. BTCPay Server told merchants Sunday at 5:25pm ET to shut down their servers after attackers swept hot wallets. Later Sunday it traced the attack to versions 2.4.1 and older, with "no credible reports" of drains on the latest 2.4.7, but it hasn't given a loss figure or a count of affected servers. Investing.com cited it as another drag on crypto sentiment (Decrypt, CoinDesk).

5. Strive (ASST) bought 124 BTC (avg ~$80,526) Oct 24–30, taking it to 43,124 BTC. Cash fell to $490.4M from $504.4M, it still holds 505,000 STRC shares ($50.1M), SATS shares outstanding rose 3,418 to 7,003,418, and SATA was unchanged at 14,030,176 (Strive 8-K, 7:50am ET).

6. Metaplanet repaid its ¥8B non-interest 20th Series bonds to EVO FUND early with cash (due April 2027). That raises the bitcoin-purchase allocation from its 27th Series stock acquisition rights to ¥33.422B from ¥25.422B, with spending through April 2028 (Metaplanet disclosure, TokenPost).

7. SpaceX is in talks to buy EchoStar's Boost Mobile (7.38M wireless subscribers at end-Q2) or get access to its network for Starlink Mobile, and Musk met EchoStar chairman Charlie Ergen last month. EchoStar rose 4.9% premarket, AT&T, Verizon and T-Mobile each fell more than 2%, and SpaceX was among the top premarket gainers (Washington Post via Reuters).

8. Tesla's October registrations rose 248% in Sweden, 131% in Norway (its best October on record, top brand with a 9.8% share, though Chinese brands hit a record 22.5%) and 34% in Denmark, where its share was just 0.73%. Separately, Robotaxi went live in Fort Worth at 6am local today (Reuters, @robotaxi).

9. At 8:06am ET, Dow futures were +0.38%, S&P +0.33% and Nasdaq-100 +0.62%, after the Nasdaq-100 shed more than $2.5T in October, and Brent fell 4.2% to $108.66 on Iran–Qatar talks to end the war. ISM Manufacturing is out today. After the close, Apple reports (its first quarter under CEO John Ternus) and so does Palantir (consensus revenue $2.18B, +85%), with the midterms tomorrow (Reuters, Yahoo Finance/Stocktwits).

AI, ROBOTICS, TECH & LONGEVITY

1. OpenAI plans to buy Google's TPUs, its first move away from relying only on Nvidia. Terms and quantities aren't disclosed, and its own Broadcom-designed chip is still slated to deploy before the end of 2026 (The Information via TechRadar).

2. OpenAI policy chief Chris Lehane is planning a post-midterm PR and policy push. It includes rebranding data centers as "AI compute campuses," community compacts giving residents a say in projects, binding AI "speed limits" for frontier models and global standards (Axios, TechCrunch).

3. Missed in earlier briefings: a federal judge on Fri Oct 30 denied xAI/SpaceX's motion to dismiss the NAACP's Clean Air Act suit over the gas turbines powering Colossus 2 in Southaven, Mississippi. The judge rejected the argument that the turbines are exempt "mobile sources." SELC estimates the plant could emit over 5,000 tons of nitrogen oxides and 47 tons of formaldehyde a year (CNBC via Tom's Hardware).

4. Life Biosciences' ER-100, the first human test of OSK epigenetic reprogramming, was tolerated through day 56 by all three low-dose glaucoma patients. In two of them, at least 28% of visual-field points improved by more than 4 dB. The safety board recommended moving to the next dose, but the Phase 1 trial is uncontrolled, so the signal is preliminary (LongevityWatch).

READS

1. Bitcoin's Q3 2026: ETF inflows replaced treasury company buying, by Karim AbdelMawla (21Shares, Nov 2): A data-dense breakdown of who bought Q3's +42.7% rally. ETFs added 79,800 BTC while treasury-company buying fell from $7.1B to ~$1B, long-term holders sold 248,000 BTC, and it covers miner margins ahead of the 2028 halving.
https://www.21shares.com/en-us/insights/bitcoin-etf-inflows-q3-2026

2. Bitcoin Treasury Companies Hit a Stress Test, and Only Some Are Passing (CryptoCompass newsroom, Oct 31): Grades Strategy, Metaplanet, Bitmine and the liquidated Satsuma on funding source, mNAV and dollar cover, including STRC buyback prices by period and K33's math on STRC's dividend drag. Useful context for today's 8-Ks.
https://cryptocompass.com/articles/bitcoin-treasury-companies-hit-a-stress-test-and-only-some-are-passing

3. The Sooner the AI Bubble Bursts the Better!, by Stephen Roach (Substack, Oct 31): The former Morgan Stanley chief economist uses a new Brookings paper to argue the $10T AI buildout (3.6% of GDP, about 3x past tech booms) has tipped into debt funding. Relevant to the AI-capex selloff hitting SPCX and the hyperscalers.
https://stephenroach.substack.com/p/the-sooner-the-ai-bubble-burst-the

News window: Mon 9:00am – Tue 9:00am ET

Note: items already in yesterday's 5pm flash are left out unless there's something new. Tesla's China October sales and Anthropic's amended S-1 also went out as breaking-news emails, so they're brief here. Gap-catch (Mon 6–9am ET): the Strategy and Strive 8-Ks were already covered, and nothing else was missed.

MARKETS

1. US spot bitcoin ETFs lost a net $398.6M on Monday, all of it from BlackRock's IBIT (-$405.3M, its biggest daily outflow since June) while FBTC took in $6.7M. That makes $1.04B out in two sessions and November starts in the red. BTC dipped to about $76,300 overnight and was around $76,900 at 6:28am ET, with near-dated options volatility up to about 51% from 43.5% ahead of the election and $382.6M of liquidations in 24 hours (Farside, CoinDesk).

2. Update on Binance: CEO Richard Teng says customers withdrew $10.97B in the 46 hours after the hack, a net outflow of $5.28B, but hourly deposits topped withdrawals by about $10M by 10pm ET Monday. Recovery Update #6 started a second reopening wave at 11pm ET across nine networks (BSC, ETH, SOL, XRP, SUI, Arbitrum, Optimism, Tron, Base), and by 2:08am ET withdrawals were back for 34 more Ethereum tokens and 22 Solana tokens. The broader proof-of-reserves snapshot is due Wednesday (CoinDesk, CryptoWatchDesk).

3. Brazil's largest exchange, Mercado Bitcoin, had about $40M drained from hot wallets on Monday through ordinary transfers, which points to stolen signing keys rather than a smart-contract bug. It paused deposits and withdrawals and says it will absorb the loss, while Tether froze 4.5M USDT and Chainalysis says about $10M has been frozen so far (Chainalysis, TechReport).

4. MSTR closed Monday at $130.76 and STRC at $99.28. Before the open, B. Riley cut its MSTR target to $180 from $195 (still Buy), lowering its BTC assumption to $82,500 from $90,000. It sees MSTR at about 1.0x NAV and now expects book value per share to double in 9–10 years rather than 7, while H.C. Wainwright reiterated Buy at $250 (Investing.com).

5. Strive's ASST fell 6.3% to $20.80 Monday after its 124 BTC buy, and SATA closed at $95.20. The Block notes it was Strive's first sale under its $1B SATS preferred ATM, and Strive (43,124 BTC) is now about 877 BTC behind Metaplanet for the No. 2 spot (The Block, Bitcoin Treasuries).

6. Tether CEO Paolo Ardoino said in his Plan ₿ Lugano keynote that Tether holds "give or take 150,000 BTC" on its corporate balance sheet, against $8.37B of BTC in its Q3 reserves. It was first widely reported overnight. Separately, Brian Armstrong said Coinbase's treasury hit 18,000 BTC, up from 17,954 at Sept 30 (crypto.news, Bitcoin Treasuries).

7. Update on SpaceX: SPCX closed +1.2% at $136.37 Monday (high $141.70), back above its $135 IPO price, on the Boost Mobile talks and Musk saying SpaceX's capex efficiency is "greatly underestimated". A Reuters analysis this morning says that, by Barclays' estimate, a SpaceX–Tesla merger would give Musk about 56% of the vote on about 37% ownership. Under his Tesla pay plan he'd get nothing unless the deal valued Tesla at $2T or more, against about $1.6T now (Investing.com, Yahoo Finance, Reuters).

8. Tesla's China-made wholesale sales were 67,829 in October, +10.3% y/y but -28.9% m/m, and are up 21.4% year to date at 810,889. TSLA closed +1.0% at $403.82 Monday, and its Brookshire, Texas Megapack plant won a 14-month US customs-duty deferral (CnEVPost, Reuters, TeslaNorth).

9. It's midterm Election Day. At 8:45am ET, S&P futures were +0.2%, Nasdaq-100 +0.8% on a chip bounce, and the Dow -0.2% (about -127 points) dragged by Apple. Monday's close left the Nasdaq-100 more than 10% below its record, which makes it a correction. Prediction markets give Democrats about 75% odds of taking the Senate, and JPMorgan sees a blue wave costing the S&P about 0.5% on Wednesday, while options price a ±0.8% move. Brent rose about 1.3% to around $106 after the US struck Iran's Qeshm Island and an Iranian official said a deal is far off. AMD, SMCI and ANET report tonight (CNBC, Reuters, CoinDesk).

AI, ROBOTICS, TECH & LONGEVITY

1. Update on Apple and Palantir: Apple fell about 4% premarket after guiding December-quarter gross margin to 45–46% (vs 46.3% consensus) on what CEO John Ternus called an "unprecedented" memory-pricing environment, with costs rising beyond the quarter, plus Siri AI ramp costs. That puts more than $170B of its $4.94T value at risk. Palantir fell 6.3% premarket despite its beat-and-raise (Reuters).

2. Oracle priced a $20B raise: 86.2M shares at $116 (about $9.9B net) plus $10B of notes from 2029 to 2046 at coupons of 7.00–8.65%, closing Nov 4, to fund AI capex. Meta is separately weighing at least $20B of bonds, including its first euro tranche (Oracle, Bloomberg Law).

3. Anthropic's amended S-1 shows Q3 revenue of $16.96B (+1,127% y/y but +47% q/q, down from +144%), an operating loss of $567M, and a $23.3B net loss driven mostly by fair-value changes on convertible notes. It also puts total commitments at $895.4B, about $213.8B of which is conditional, and warns it "may imminently meet" its RSP threshold for AI-accelerated research. Marketing to investors reportedly starts the week of Nov 9 (SEC, CNBC, MACCUS).

4. OpenAI signed four Abu Dhabi agreements on Monday covering ADNOC/G42 deployment of frontier models, an AI-native government initiative, AI for Mubadala investment analysis, and a five-year Inception42 program. Separately, it launched a "Grid Protectors" program pledging to free up to 1,000 MW from its Effingham County, Georgia campus during grid emergencies (CNBC, OpenAI).

5. The New York Times sued Brave in Manhattan federal court on Monday, alleging it scraped Times journalism into a 30B-page index sold to AI firms including Anthropic, Perplexity, Mistral, xAI and Cohere, and that it bypasses paywalls. The Daily News, Chicago Tribune and Orlando Sentinel filed a similar suit (TechCrunch, The Verge).

6. Saudi Aramco closed its purchase of 49% of Humain, the PIF-backed AI company, for about $2.6B in cash plus AI, compute and digital assets. Humain targets 3 GW of data-center capacity by 2030 (Aramco, The Decoder).

READS

1. Anthropic has committed $895 billion to compute and still doesn't have enough, by Marc Winer (MACCUS, Nov 3): The clearest breakdown yet of the amended S-1. It splits the $895B into obligations, unstarted leases, post-quarter deals and conditional pieces, names the Google/Amazon/Microsoft/SpaceXAI ($120.5B) contracts, and explains why expensive short-term compute flipped Anthropic to an operating loss. It's directly relevant to SPCX's AI revenue.
https://maccus.fr/en/anthropic-compute-commitments/

2. The Largest Hack Ever Just Happened. Strategy Kept Buying. (Bitcoin Treasuries newsletter, Nov 2): A tight weekly ledger showing STRC buybacks have taken $606.2M since Oct 12 against $87.6M for bitcoin. It also shows Coinbase's buying slowing (1,103 to 819 to 643 BTC a quarter) and Strive closing in on Metaplanet. It's good context for how Strategy is allocating capital now.
https://newsletter.bitcointreasuries.net/p/the-largest-hack-ever-just-happened-strategy-kept-buying

2026-11-04.bodyText:
News window: Tue 9:00am – Wed 9:00am ET

Note: items in yesterday's 5pm flash are left out unless there's something new. The midterm results already went out in this morning's 8:33am breaking-news email, so items 1 and 4 add only the new figures. Gap-catch (Tue 6–9am ET): yesterday's briefing caught the pre-market items, and nothing missed turned up.

MARKETS

1. Update on the midterms: with Democrats taking both chambers (54–44 in the Senate with races still being counted, and past 218 in the House), futures flipped from a 2.4% overnight drop in Nasdaq-100 futures to Dow futures +1.9% (nearly 1,000 points) and S&P +0.9% by 8:42am ET after Trump accepted the results, while the 10-year yield fell 5bp to 4.91%, the dollar index dropped 0.6% to 101.25 and gold jumped 3% to $4,046 (IBD, Benzinga, Reuters).

2. BTC fell to $75,618 on Bitstamp as the results came in (its lowest since Sep 16, briefly under the $75,733 50-week average) and then made a V-shaped recovery to about $78,300 by 7:24am ET, after roughly $660M of election-day options block trades, about $420M of them calls bought; 10x Research's Markus Thielen sees an oversold bounce toward $82,000, and long liquidations reached about $288M in 24 hours (CoinDesk, Cointelegraph).

3. US spot bitcoin ETFs lost another $115.6M on Tuesday (IBIT -$95.0M, Grayscale Mini -$52.6M, Bitwise BITB +$21.9M), the third red session in a row and $1.16B out since Friday, though daily outflows shrank from $643M to $399M to $116M; November is already -$514M, about equal to all of October, and ether ETFs lost $85.3M (Farside, SoSoValue via Cointelegraph).

4. Update on SpaceX and Tesla: at 7:30am ET SPCX was -5.8% at $133.06 and TSLA -5.7% at $375.65, about $200B of combined value, reversing SPCX's 3.6% gain on Tuesday, after Texas governor-elect Gina Hinojosa (who campaigned for a data-center moratorium) beat Abbott; Wells Fargo says 27% of planned data-center gigawatts are in Texas, Musk spent at least $474M on the midterms ($224M in Texas), CoreWeave and IREN were down 7% and 6%, and Musk answered with jokes on X about space lasers and data centers in space (Benzinga, CNBC, Axios).

5. Crypto policy under a Democratic Congress: analysts expect the stalled CLARITY Act (it failed 49–50 in the Senate in September) to come back in 2027 with tougher consumer safeguards and limits on stablecoin yield, while the GENIUS Act's federal or state licensing regime for payment stablecoins still takes effect Jan 18, 2027 alongside the OCC's final rule (CoinDesk).

6. Circle reported Q3 revenue and reserve income of $865M (+17% y/y) and net income from continuing operations of $226M (+5%), with average USDC circulation of $73.3B (+8%), $73.9B at quarter end and $13.9T of onchain USDC volume (+49%), and disclosed a roughly 5% workforce cut with $9.1M of restructuring charges (Circle, CoinDesk, The Block).

7. Update on STRC: the first daily STRC dividend under the new terms was paid Tuesday, Nov 3, at a 12.00% annual rate for November (about $0.03–0.04 a share per day). Strategy's prospectus supplement says it expects to fund these dividends mainly through MSTR common-stock ATM sales, and the same filing covers up to $21B of STRC ATM issuance (Strategy, StockTitan).

8. Update on Binance: the broader proof-of-reserves snapshot, covering more tokens than the 10 in the Oct 31 proof, is scheduled for today, Nov 4. Binance says generating its zero-knowledge proof will take about 40–50 hours, which puts results around Friday (The Block, Binance).

9. Block (which holds bitcoin on its balance sheet) rose more than 6% after hours. It reported Q3 adjusted EPS of $1.13 vs $1.03 expected and revenue of $6.72B vs $6.59B, and raised its full-year guidance (CNBC, LSEG).

AI, ROBOTICS, TECH & LONGEVITY

1. AI hardware beats kept coming after Tuesday's close. Super Micro posted fiscal Q1 revenue of $19.9B with non-GAAP EPS of $1.81 and guided FY2027 sales to $72–82B vs $69.2B consensus (about +9%). Arista's Q3 revenue rose 58.5% to $3.66B, and its Q4 guide of $3.9–4.0B and $1.26–1.30 EPS beat $3.60B and $1.15 (about +12%) (CNBC, company releases).

2. Nvidia took back the title of world's most valuable company on Tuesday, closing at $4.981T vs Apple's $4.823T as chip stocks rebounded and Apple slid on its memory-cost margin warning, just four days after losing the top spot (Forbes Middle East, Barron's).

3. Churchill Capital XI shareholders approved the merger with Agility Robotics, with closing set for today and Nasdaq trading as AGLT expected Thursday, Nov 5, one of the first pure-play humanoid listings. Separately, China released its first national standard for humanoid robots after a three-year drafting process (Embodied AI Frontier).

4. Fal, which hosts image, video and audio models for developers, raised $1.3B in a Series F led by Bessemer with Nvidia and T. Rowe Price at a $16B valuation, double its April mark, with more than $800M of annualized revenue reported (TechCrunch, Bloomberg).

5. OpenAI's ChatGPT consumer chief Adam Fry said ChatGPT search volume now equals about 20% of Google's (OpenAI's own count, for queries that trigger a web lookup) and that ads haven't hurt usage. Separately, Google will switch Gemini and Search off for K-12 student accounts unless schools opt in, because it says the two can no longer be separated (The Verge, TechCrunch).

6.
