News window: Wed 9:00am – Thu 9:00am ET

Note: items already in yesterday's 5pm flash (Dow +1,569 / S&P +1.6%, oil -9%, SPCX/TSLA closes, BTC high $80.7K, MSTR +5.1%/STRC to par, data-center AI split, Arm beat) are left out unless there's something new. Gap-catch (Wed 6–9am ET): ADP at 8:15am ET was missed by yesterday's briefing — marked below.

MARKETS

1. BTC held about $80,250 early Thursday (CoinDesk) after Wednesday's jump from ~$78K, with US spot bitcoin ETFs flipping to a $74.6M net inflow on Wednesday (Fidelity FBTC about +$237M offsetting BlackRock IBIT -$201.2M) that ended a three-day, $1.16B outflow streak, while spot ether ETFs added $53M and snapped a seven-day outflow run (Farside, SoSoValue via Cointelegraph).

2. Update on Binance: Recovery Update #7 (15:23 UTC Wed) said about 98% of assets hit by the Oct 29 incident are replenished (up from ~90% in Update #3), with the last 2% slower because those tokens are less liquid, and the Nov 4 00:00 UTC Proof of Reserves snapshot expanded coverage from 10 to 44 tokens, with the zero-knowledge proof expected to take about 50–60 hours (Binance via Exchange.news).

3. Update on the CLARITY Act: after Democrats took both chambers, CoinDesk's industry roundup called the current bill likely "the final nail in the Clarity Act's coffin," noting crypto PACs spent roughly $170.5M in the midterms and that the measure already failed a September procedural vote under Republican control; some executives still see room for a bipartisan rewrite with tougher consumer protections and conflict-of-interest limits (CoinDesk).

4. Arthur Hayes published "D is for Dilution" arguing SpaceX faces roughly another 50% share unlock by June 2027 (mostly Elon vesting) and Anthropic IPO buyers face about 83% dilution by then, which he says will sour AI equity vibes, widen AI credit spreads, shrink bank balance sheets, and pressure Bitcoin near term — so Maelstrom is sitting out until a crisis forces central-bank easing (Crypto Trader Digest).

5. Update on SpaceX's AI compute: Goldman Sachs and Apollo are already shopping pieces of the record ~$40B GPU lease financing (Apollo SPV buys Nvidia Rubin kit and leases it to SpaceX off-balance-sheet), asking some investors for stakes of up to $500M before formal syndication, with leases expected to start in H1 2027 (Bloomberg via CryptoBriefing / CNA).

6. Premarket Thursday: TSLA about $376 (−2.3%), SPCX about $132 (−2.8%), MSTR about $140 (−1.8%) and STRC near $100 par, while Nasdaq-100 futures were down about 0.8% on chip weakness and S&P futures roughly flat after Wednesday's midterm rally (Public.com, CoinDesk, Reuters).

7. Aave V4 listed Coinbase's tokenized SpaceX stock (SPCXc) as USDC collateral on Base for eligible non-US users on Wednesday, with a 55% collateral factor and a 37,000-token deposit cap, extending the Equities Hub beyond Magnificent Seven names (Aave governance / Base).

8. Missed (Wed 8:15am ET): ADP said private payrolls rose 86,000 in October (vs ~75,000 expected; September revised to 86,000 from 90,000), with base pay +3.2% and gross pay +4.7% y/y, trade/transport/utilities +39,000 and professional and business services −27,000 — a soft preview ahead of Friday's BLS jobs report (ADP, CNBC).

9. Fundstrat's Tom Lee told CNBC a Democratic sweep is positive for stocks because divided government forces negotiation and eases Fed pressure, while CoinDesk/CNBC coverage noted crypto's post-election bounce as Democrats look more open to market-structure talks even as the current CLARITY text stalls (CNBC, CoinDesk).

10. Jobless claims are due Thursday and October nonfarm payrolls Friday (consensus about +59,000 after September's +29,000), keeping the macro calendar live after Wednesday's ADP print (CNBC, CoinDesk).

AI, ROBOTICS, TECH & LONGEVITY

1. Update on Agility: AGLT and AGLTW began Nasdaq trading today as the first US publicly listed pure-play humanoid robotics company with active commercial deployments, after a Churchill Capital XI combination and related financings that raised about $465M gross (Foxconn-led PIPE ~$201M) against more than $300M of committed multi-year Digit 5 orders and 65,000+ hours of Digit operation at customers including GXO, Schaeffler and Toyota (Agility, Quartz).

2. Qualcomm slumped about 9% premarket (~$17.5B of market value) after handset-chip revenue fell 26% to $5.14B and chip-segment sales fell 8% to $9.02B, overshadowing its data-center push; at least eight brokerages cut targets, and CEO Cristiano Amon said the firm prepared early for the memory shortage (Reuters).

3. AppLovin jumped about 16.5% to $316.50 premarket after Q3 revenue of about $2.19B vs $2.08B expected and EPS of $4.30 vs $4.07, with Q4 sales guidance above estimates (Benzinga).

4. Ben Thompson's Stratechery "AI on the Ballot" argues midterm ads and Texas results show political vetoes are now the binding constraint on data-center buildout — bad near term for neoclouds and Nvidia volumes, relatively better for hyperscalers, Apple (edge inference / memory relief), frontier labs' spend discipline, and SpaceX's orbital-compute thesis (Stratechery).

5. Memory and AI-infra names stayed under pressure into Thursday's open (SK Hynix and SanDisk each down more than 5% in related trading commentary) as the post-midterm rotation out of chips continued after Wednesday's Hut 8/IREN/SOX rout (TradingKey, Reuters).

6. Longevity: The Economist's Intelligence podcast "Forever young" (Nov 5) maps the business of longevity drugs — dual-purpose candidates aimed at age-related disease because FDA still doesn't recognize aging itself, with GLP-1s as early candidates and Big Pharma watching biotech for acquisitions (The Economist).

READS

1. D is for Dilution, by Arthur Hayes (Crypto Trader Digest, Nov 5): A sharp math-first case that SpaceX (~50% more unlocks by mid-2027) and Anthropic (~83% IPO dilution) will grind share prices, freeze AI credit, and pressure Bitcoin before any bailout rally. Useful counterweight to the midterm risk-on bounce.
https://cryptohayes.substack.com/p/d-is-for-dilution

2. AI on the Ballot, by Ben Thompson (Stratechery, Nov 4): Election-night read that data-center NIMBYism is now the scarce input. Ten takes on who wins (hyperscalers, Apple, frontier labs, SpaceX orbital) and who loses (neoclouds, Nvidia near term, startups) if Americans keep blocking AI buildout.
https://stratechery.com/2026/ai-on-the-ballot/

3. Anthropic, Amended: The Bridge and the Far Bank, by Cape Fear Advisors (Nov 2): Filing-level unpack of Anthropic's S-1/A — $5.0B of expensive short-term compute in Q3, $213.8B of conditional/terminable commitments, and why the SpaceX line is the one either side can cut on 90 days' notice.
https://capefearadvisors.substack.com/p/anthropic-amended-the-bridge-and

8. Missed (Wed 8:15am ET): ADP said private payrolls rose 86,000 in October (vs ~75,000 expected; September revised to 86,000 from 90,000), with base pay +3.2% and gross pay +4.7% y/y, trade/transport/utilities +39,000 and professional and business services −27,000 — a soft preview ahead of Friday's BLS jobs report (ADP, CNBC).

9. Fundstrat's Tom Lee told CNBC a Democratic sweep is positive for stocks because divided government forces negotiation and eases Fed pressure, while CoinDesk/CNBC coverage noted crypto's post-election bounce as Democrats look more open to market-structure talks even as the current CLARITY text stalls (CNBC, CoinDesk).

Update on Agility: AGLT and AGLTW began Nasdaq trading today as the first US publicly listed pure-play humanoid robotics company with active commercial deployments, after a Churchill Capital XI combination and related financings that raised about $465M gross (Foxconn-led PIPE ~$201M) against more than $300M of committed multi-year Digit 5 orders and 65,000+ hours of Digit operation at customers including GXO, Schaeffler and Toyota (Agility, Quartz).

2. Qualcomm slumped about 9% premarket (~$17.5B of market value) after handset-chip revenue fell 26% to $5.14B and chip-segment sales fell 8% to $9.02B, overshadowing its data-center push; at least eight brokerages cut targets, and CEO Cristiano Amon said the firm prepared early for the memory shortage (Reuters).

Ben Thompson's Stratechery "AI on the Ballot" argues midterm ads and Texas results show political vetoes are now the binding constraint on data-center buildout — bad near term for neoclouds and Nvidia volumes, relatively better for hyperscalers, Apple (edge inference / memory relief), frontier labs' spend discipline, and SpaceX's orbital-compute thesis (Stratechery).

5. Memory and AI-infra names stayed under pressure into Thursday's open (SK Hynix and SanDisk each down more than 5% in related trading commentary) as the post-midterm rotation out of chips continued after Wednesday's Hut 8/IREN/SOX rout (TradingKey, Reuters).

6. Longevity: The Economist's Intelligence podcast "Forever young" (Nov 5) maps the business of longevity drugs — dual-purpose candidates aimed at age-related disease because FDA still doesn't recognize aging itself, with GLP-1s as early candidates and Big Pharma watching biotech for acquisitions (The Economist).

Useful counterweight to the midterm risk-on bounce.

https://stratechery.com/2026/ai-on-the-ballot/

2026-11-06.subject: Fri Nov 6 briefing: Payrolls +165K, BTC ETFs -$430M/$1.27B liqs, Nasdaq futures bounce, Tesla ends Cybertruck for Cybercab, MSTR below 200-day, Starship Nov 13, GPT-6 Cyber, Anthropic IPO pushback

News window: Thu 9:00am – Fri 9:00am ET

Note: Thursday's closes (Dow/S&P/Nasdaq, Mag7, TSLA, SPCX, BTC, MSTR, ASST, SOXX, AGLT) already went out in yesterday's 5pm flash and are left out. Gap-catch for Thu 6–9am ET found nothing missed.

MARKETS

1. October payrolls blew out at +165K vs ~59–70K expected with unemployment down to 4.1%, wages +0.4% m/m / +3.1% y/y, and Aug/Sep revised up a combined +84K, sending the dollar higher and the 10-year up ~6bp to near 4.9% (CNBC, XTB).

2. Futures are splitting after Thursday's rout: Nasdaq 100 +1.1–1.6% and S&P +0.2% but Dow -0.8%, with chips leading the bounce (SOXX ~+5%, Lam +9%, Micron +7.5%, AMD/TSMC +5%, Nvidia +3%), while Nikkei and KOSPI fell ~6% overnight and Brent slipped to ~$96 (Yahoo Finance, Investing.com, Fortune).

3. Spot BTC ETFs bled $430.2M Thursday (FBTC -$199.9M, IBIT -$105M, GBTC -$49.9M), taking the week's net redemptions to $869.8M and the 5-day total to -$1.51B, as >$1.27B of crypto derivatives (about $1.1B longs) were liquidated in 24h (CoinDesk, SoSoValue/Farside).

4. Bitcoin is back near $75.6–76.1K premarket (down ~5% over 24h), and Glassnode says about 60% of short-term-holder supply is now underwater after being in profit a day earlier (CoinDesk, InflowScan, Glassnode on X).

5. Tesla is up ~2.8% premarket to ~$353 after Musk said Giga Texas will phase out Cybertruck production by mid-2027 to free capacity for Cybercab, where installed capacity already tops 125K units/yr (TradingKey).

6. Strategy (MSTR) fell through its 200-day moving average ($133.72) and traded as low as $123.90 Thursday, while Saylor called it a "4σ day for equities" and noted STRC closed at $99.56, just 44 cents under par a day after hitting $100; MSCI's Nov 11 index decision is the next catalyst (MarketBeat, Bitcoin.com, Yahoo/TIKR).

7. SpaceX (SPCX) is up ~2% premarket, and SpaceX VP has targeted Nov 13 for Starship Flight 15 (Ship 42/Booster 22), which will try first catches of both stages and deploy Starlink V3 satellites (PANews, Pad Zero, Teslarati).

8. Strive (ASST) now holds 43,124 BTC, about 876 BTC behind Metaplanet's 44,000 for the #2 corporate treasury spot, with buys funded mainly through SATA/SATS perpetual preferred (~$630M October raise) while Metaplanet has paused buying to focus on buybacks and debt paydown (Crypto Briefing, Yahoo Finance).

9. Miners and neoclouds are bouncing premarket, led by IREN +14% on a fiscal Q1 revenue beat and CoreWeave +6.3%, after Bernstein earlier cut MARA's target to $10 from $17 over Texas data-center risk; MARA reports Nov 9 (Investing.com, PANews, Yahoo/TIKR).

AI, ROBOTICS, TECH & LONGEVITY

1. Potential Anthropic IPO investors are questioning whether it can launch its roadshow the week of Nov 9 and list by month-end at a ~$1.5T valuation after the tech selloff, while OpenAI's Greg Brockman said OpenAI could be IPO-ready in 2027 (Digest AI, TechCrunch).

2. OpenAI released GPT-6 Cyber (48.5% on ExploitGym), and an autonomous pipeline built on it found 2,308 potential Linux kernel flaws and produced working root exploits for 948 of them for ~$1.21M in API credits (~$1,279 each); OpenAI also plans to buy Pierre Computer to take on GitHub (The Neuron, Axios).

3. After voters rejected data centers in the midterms, OpenAI pledged to pay electricity and grid costs and disclose more about its future sites, as a Cleanview map shows 158.6 GW (41%) of planned US data-center capacity sits in states whose governor backs a pause, led by Texas at 88.4 GW (Training Data Daily, @wallstengine/Cleanview).

4. China blocked SoftBank's $5.375B purchase of ABB Robotics' China business, Serve Robotics launched a "Physical AI Services" business pitched as AWS for robots, and Nemi agreed to a SPAC listing at $400M pre-money (The Robot Report, TechCrunch, Unite.AI).

5. Nvidia released seven open models for engineering, robotics and weather and said its Vera CPU runs agents 2x faster with 1.6x more agents per watt than x86, and Meta bought multi-agent coding startup Conductor (NVIDIA Blog, TechCrunch).

6. Anthropic launched read-only Personal Finance in Claude (Plaid-linked bank and card accounts for US Pro/Max/Ultra users) and signed its first paid publisher deal, with AP; METR estimates Anthropic's internal capability progress has accelerated, with caveats (Training Data Daily, Adweek, METR).

READS

1. "AI: The Midterms' 'AI Earthquake' & the Voter Veto (Part 2)", Michael Parekh, AI-RTZ, Nov 5. Why read: the best single post-election map of the data-center risk to Musk, including Texas's ~13 GW exposed, SpaceX's 13 GW 2027 compute plan, and Anthropic as ~35% of SpaceX revenue. https://michaelparekh.substack.com/p/ai-the-midterms-ai-earthquake-and

2. "Perspective on Risk - Nov. 5, 2026 (AI as Financial Stability Risk)", Brian Peters (ex-NY Fed), Perspective on Risk, Nov 5. Why read: a numbers-driven argument that the AI buildout looks like the 2000 telecom bust rather than 2008, flagging off-balance-sheet leases, Nvidia's residual-value guarantees, and CoreWeave's ~15% bonds as the weak links. https://perspectiveonrisk.substack.com/p/perspective-on-risk-nov-5-2026-ai

2026-11-07.subject: Sat Nov 7 briefing: BTC ETFs -$412M/BTC dips under $75K, Musk offers to cancel SpaceX gov contracts, SpaceXAI 6 GW Arizona, Anthropic IPO reset to $1-1.5T, H200 China, MEXC cutoff
2026-11-07.bodyText:
News window: Fri 9:00am – Sat 9:00am ET

Note: Friday's closes for the Dow/S&P/Nasdaq, TSLA, SPCX and BTC, plus OpenAI CFO Friar's CNBC interview, already went out in yesterday's 5pm flash and are left out. Gap-catch for Fri 6–9am ET found nothing missed.

MARKETS

1. Spot BTC ETFs bled another $411.9M Friday, almost all from IBIT (-$403M) while FBTC took in +$42.8M, putting November's first five sessions at about -$1.28B and the week near -$880M, turning 2026 year-to-date ETF flows slightly negative (about -$502M); spot ETH ETFs lost $93.2M (Farside, SoSoValue, Crypto Briefing).

2. Bitcoin slipped below $75K Friday for the first time in over two months before recovering to about $75.9–76K Saturday morning, still under its 200-day EMA (~$76.5K) and sitting on Glassnode's $73–76K support band (short-term-holder cost basis $75.7K), and it barely moved after Trump confirmed new "minor" US strikes on an Iranian air-defense site on Qeshm Island (CoinMarketCap via Crypto Times, CryptoPotato, AP, Glassnode).

3. The Nasdaq finished the week down 3.37% for a fourth straight weekly loss, while preliminary November UMich sentiment beat at 51.0 vs 48.0 expected with 1-year inflation expectations down to 4.3% from 4.7%; October CPI comes Tuesday and PPI Friday (Morningstar, Reuters, The Block).

4. Musk posted that government work will be under 10% of SpaceX revenue this quarter and under 5% a year from now and said he is "happy to cancel any" contracts Democrats don't want, Deutsche Bank reaffirmed its SPCX Buy and $250 target saying political-retaliation risk looks overstated, and an 8-K showed Google's Don Harrison left the SpaceX board effective Nov 4 (TipRanks/The Fly, Gizmodo, TradingView, SEC filing).

5. SpaceXAI has applied for a 747-acre, up-to-6 GW AI data-center and battery campus in Cochise County, Arizona (four 1.5 GW phases, construction as early as March 2027, zoning hearing Dec 9), even as the Washington Post and Houston Chronicle report incoming Texas Democrats plan tighter scrutiny of Musk-company permits, incentives and data-center approvals (DCD, Tucson.com, Washington Post, Houston Chronicle).

6. Tesla rebranded its AI chips "SI" for Super Intelligence (HW4 becomes SI4) and sketched SI6 at about 80x SI4 compute on Samsung 2nm-class for 2029–2030 plus a revived chiplet/HBM Dojo D3 aimed at space, while CNBC reported Scottish Mortgage has fully exited Tesla and cut SpaceX to 11.1% of assets from 15% (Tom's Hardware, CNBC).

7. Strategy (MSTR) closed Friday at $128.93 (-0.3%), with mNAV about 1.11x, below the 1.22x level CEO Phong Le cited as the break-even for issuing stock to buy bitcoin, ahead of MSCI's Nov 11 decision; Strive (ASST) closed at $21.45 and SATA at $96.54 after Strive reported $509.0M of Q3 net income, mostly unrealized BTC gains (exa/market data, TreasurySignal, Yahoo/TIKR, Strive IR).

8. Miners keep leaving bitcoin: Core Scientific sold 816 BTC in Q3, now holds just 32 BTC and will exit mining by Dec 31, IREN's mining revenue fell 58% q/q to $28M as AI cloud revenue jumped 182% to ~$200M with a full mining exit planned by year-end, and TeraWulf's mining revenue fell 69% while HPC lease revenue rose 774% to ~$63M (Crypto Briefing, The Block).

9. On policy, FinCEN cut MEXC Global off from the US financial system over an alleged $16B in transactions tied to Iran, North Korea and Russia, the Labor Department sent its proposed rule allowing crypto and other alternatives in 401(k)s to the White House OIRA, and House Democrats are reportedly planning an SEC-led rewrite of the CLARITY Act (The Block, Disruption Banking).

10. Update on the Binance hack: Elliptic says the attackers have swapped about $124M of stolen altcoins into BTC on top of $1.48B in BTC taken, across 20,000+ wallets with only a negligible amount cashed out and ~$2.85B frozen, and Binance aims to reopen HYPE, INJ, APT, NEAR and LTC withdrawals by the end of next week (The Block/Elliptic).

AI, ROBOTICS, TECH & LONGEVITY

1. Update on Anthropic's IPO: CNBC says investors now see a $1T–1.5T valuation (down from the $2T floated in recent months) for a likely mid-November Nasdaq debut, its amended prospectus shows about $895.4B in committed compute and infrastructure spend, and voters rejected data-center measures in 40 of 41 midterm ballot fights (CNBC).

2. OpenAI closed an $11B first tranche of its round at a $1.25T valuation with funds transferred Friday and the round possibly growing toward ~$20B, while it also published a "community compact" for future compute campuses alongside its pledge to pay its data centers' full power costs (Bloomberg, TechCrunch, Yahoo Finance).

3. The NYT reports Commerce cleared roughly two dozen Chinese firms to buy or handle Nvidia H200s, including New Matrix (an apparently empty Beijing office, owners tied to blacklisted Wise Road) and Maginfra (linked to blacklisted Inspur), while Reuters says ~600K H200s sit in Hong Kong awaiting Beijing's import approval and Bloomberg says chip exports are becoming a Democratic target; Jensen Huang says Vera Rubin will generate $40B of revenue per GW vs $25B for Grace Blackwell (NYT, Reuters, Bloomberg, Motley Fool).

4. AI credit stress is spreading: CoreWeave's bond yield is above 16%, ING is shopping $500M of data-center loans including Stargate exposure, and Google took over Crusoe's stalled Wyoming site as part of a $17B Cheyenne campus powered by fuel cells and gas with carbon capture (CNBC, DCD, Bloomberg).

5. Open models had a big day: Thinking Machines shipped Inkling 2 Small (594B-parameter MoE, billed as the top Western open-weight model), Ricursive released the Apache-2.0 Ripple-65B Preview for ~$32M total R&D, Baidu open-sourced the 280B ERNIE 5.5 Flash Base, and Google's Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash doubled video clips to 15 seconds at ~30% lower price; the DOJ also stood up a "Super Intelligence Task Force" (The Decoder, Google, The Register).

6. In robotics, Xiaomi's CyberOne 02 humanoids completed a reported eight-hour factory parts-sorting trial and MIT Technology Review found a paid humanoid apartment-cleaning service in San Francisco close to useful; in longevity, UChicago reported in Nature Aging that the over-the-counter supplement vanadyl sulfate cleared senescent cells and extended lifespan 7% in aging mice while improving diabetes, liver, heart and lung-fibrosis models (humanoid.guide, MIT Technology Review, UChicago).

READS

1. "State of the Themes: The End of the Trade (as we know it)", Citrini Research, Nov 4. Why read: Citrini rebuilds its whole model portfolio on the call that AI capex growth has peaked (hyperscaler capex near $1T annualized vs at least $200B ecosystem ARR), with sharp detail on frozen neocloud credit, the Texas data-center moratorium, and $15B of hung bridge loans on an Anthropic-backed project. https://www.citriniresearch.com/p/state-of-the-themes-556

2. "Idling at Support" (The Week On-chain, Week 44), Glassnode, Nov 4. Why read: the clearest map of where BTC stands now, with short-term holders down to ~38% in profit, the $73–76K support band, a short cluster near $87K, and why past midterms were followed by one more drop. https://research.glassnode.com/the-week-onchain-week-44-2026/

3. "2026.45: Falling Leaves (and Stocks)", Ben Thompson, Stratechery, Nov 6. Why read: Thompson's weekly wrap ties the midterm vote against data centers to the AI selloff, Google's slowing search growth, and US-China chip policy. https://stratechery.com/2026/falling-leaves-and-stocks/

3. The Nasdaq finished the week down 3.37% for a fourth straight weekly loss, while preliminary November UMich sentiment beat at 51.0 vs 48.0 expected with 1-year inflation expectations down to 4.3% from 4.7%; October CPI comes Tuesday and PPI Friday (Morningstar, Reuters, The Block).

4. Musk posted that government work will be under 10% of SpaceX revenue this quarter and under 5% a year from now and said he is "happy to cancel any" contracts Democrats don't want, Deutsche Bank reaffirmed its SPCX Buy and $250 target saying political-retaliation risk looks overstated, and an 8-K showed Google's Don Harrison left the SpaceX board effective Nov 4 (TipRanks/The Fly, Gizmodo, TradingView, SEC filing).

5. SpaceXAI has applied for a 747-acre, up-to-6 GW AI data-center and battery campus in Cochise County, Arizona (four 1.5 GW phases, construction as early as March 2027, zoning hearing Dec 9), even as the Washington Post and Houston Chronicle report incoming Texas Democrats plan tighter scrutiny of Musk-company permits, incentives and data-center approvals (DCD, Tucson.com, Washington Post, Houston Chronicle).

6. Tesla rebranded its AI chips "SI" for Super Intelligence (HW4 becomes SI4) and sketched SI6 at about 80x SI4 compute on Samsung 2nm-class for 2029–2030 plus a revived chiplet/HBM Dojo D3 aimed at space, while CNBC reported Scottish Mortgage has fully exited Tesla and cut SpaceX to 11.1% of assets from 15% (Tom's Hardware, CNBC).

7. Strategy (MSTR) closed Friday at $128.93 (-0.3%), with mNAV about 1.11x, below the 1.22x level CEO Phong Le cited as the break-even for issuing stock to buy bitcoin, ahead of MSCI's Nov 11 decision; Strive (ASST) closed at $21.45 and SATA at $96.54 after Strive reported $509.0M of Q3 net income, mostly unrealized BTC gains (exa/market data, TreasurySignal, Yahoo/TIKR, Strive IR).

8. Miners keep leaving bitcoin: Core Scientific sold 816 BTC in Q3, now holds just 32 BTC and will exit mining by Dec 31, IREN's mining revenue fell 58% q/q to $28M as AI cloud revenue jumped 182% to ~$200M with a full mining exit planned by year-end, and TeraWulf's mining revenue fell 69% while HPC lease revenue rose 774% to ~$63M (Crypto Briefing, The Block).

9. On policy, FinCEN cut MEXC Global off from the US financial system over an alleged $16B in transactions tied to Iran, North Korea and Russia, the Labor Department sent its proposed rule allowing crypto and other alternatives in 401(k)s to the White House OIRA, and House Democrats are reportedly planning an SEC-led rewrite of the CLARITY Act (The Block, Disruption Banking).

10. Update on the Binance hack: Elliptic says the attackers have swapped about $124M of stolen altcoins into BTC on top of $1.48B in BTC taken, across 20,000+ wallets with only a negligible amount cashed out and ~$2.85B frozen, and Binance aims to reopen HYPE, INJ, APT, NEAR and LTC withdrawals by the end of next week (The Block/Elliptic).

AI, ROBOTICS, TECH & LONGEVITY

1. Update on Anthropic's IPO: CNBC says investors now see a $1T–1.5T valuation (down from the $2T floated in recent months) for a likely mid-November Nasdaq debut, its amended prospectus shows about $895.4B in committed compute and infrastructure spend, and voters rejected data-center measures in 40 of 41 midterm ballot fights (CNBC).

2. OpenAI closed an $11B first tranche of its round at a $1.25T valuation with funds transferred Friday and the round possibly growing toward ~$20B, while it also published a "community compact" for future compute campuses alongside its pledge to pay its data centers' full power costs (Bloomberg, TechCrunch, Yahoo Finance).

3. The NYT reports Commerce cleared roughly two dozen Chinese firms to buy or handle Nvidia H200s, including New Matrix (an apparently empty Beijing office, owners tied to blacklisted Wise Road) and Maginfra (linked to blacklisted Inspur), while Reuters says ~600K H200s sit in Hong Kong awaiting Beijing's import approval and Bloomberg says chip exports are becoming a Democratic target; Jensen Huang says Vera Rubin will generate $40B of revenue per GW vs $25B for Grace Blackwell (NYT, Reuters, Bloomberg, Motley Fool).

4. AI credit stress is spreading: CoreWeave's bond yield is above 16%, ING is shopping $500M of data-center loans including Stargate exposure, and Google took over Crusoe's stalled Wyoming site as part of a $17B Cheyenne campus powered by fuel cells and gas with carbon capture (CNBC, DCD, Bloomberg).

5. Open models had a big day: Thinking Machines shipped Inkling 2 Small (594B-parameter MoE, billed as the top Western open-weight model), Ricursive released the Apache-2.0 Ripple-65B Preview for ~$32M total R&D, Baidu open-sourced the 280B ERNIE 5.5 Flash Base, and Google's Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash doubled video clips to 15 seconds at ~30% lower price; the DOJ also stood up a "Super Intelligence Task Force" (The Decoder, Google, The Register).

6. In robotics, Xiaomi's CyberOne 02 humanoids completed a reported eight-hour factory parts-sorting trial and MIT Technology Review found a paid humanoid apartment-cleaning service in San Francisco close to useful; in longevity, UChicago reported in Nature Aging that the over-the-counter supplement vanadyl sulfate cleared senescent cells and extended lifespan 7% in aging mice while improving diabetes, liver, heart and lung-fibrosis models (humanoid.guide, MIT Technology Review, UChicago).

READS

1. "State of the Themes: The End of the Trade (as we know it)", Citrini Research, Nov 4. Why read: Citrini rebuilds its whole model portfolio on the call that AI capex growth has peaked (hyperscaler capex near $1T annualized vs at least $200B ecosystem ARR), with sharp detail on frozen neocloud credit, the Texas data-center moratorium, and $15B of hung bridge loans on an Anthropic-backed project. https://www.citriniresearch.com/p/state-of-the-themes-556

2. "Idling at Support" (The Week On-chain, Week 44), Glassnode, Nov 4. Why read: the clearest map of where BTC stands now, with short-term holders down to ~38% in profit, the $73–76K support band, a short cluster near $87K, and why past midterms were followed by one more drop. https://research.glassnode.com/the-week-onchain-week-44-2026/

3. "2026.45: Falling Leaves (and Stocks)", Ben Thompson, Stratechery, Nov 6. Why read: Thompson's weekly wrap ties the midterm vote against data centers to the AI selloff, Google's slowing search growth, and US-China chip policy. https://stratechery.com/2026/falling-leaves-and-stocks/

News window: Sat 9:00am – Sun 9:00am ET

Note: quiet weekend for markets (US equities closed; futures reopen 6pm ET tonight). Gap-catch for Sat 6–9am ET found one missed item, Berkshire's Q3 (item 8).

MARKETS

1. The Gulf flared up again over the weekend: CENTCOM said a US aircraft struck the stern of cargo ship M/V Huda as it tried to leave an Iranian port in breach of the US blockade, Iran's Revolutionary Guards said three "non-compliant" tankers caught fire in the Strait of Hormuz, and Saudi Arabia intercepted missiles aimed at Riyadh with debris damaging an Aramco building; Brent last settled at $98.32 and WTI at $90.83, so watch tonight's futures open ahead of Tuesday's October CPI (DW/AP/dpa, The Company Chronicle).

2. Bitcoin went nowhere over the weekend at about $75.7–76.1K (roughly $75.9K Sunday morning) and is on track for a fifth straight red weekly close, down about 2.7% on the week, with the Fear & Greed index at 28 after touching 25 Saturday, BTC dominance back at 60%, and total crypto market cap down about $100B on the week to $2.55T as NEAR (-15%), BCH (-13%), HYPE (-12%) and XLM (-11%) led alt losses (CryptoPotato, crypto.news, Bitcoin Bagger, CryptoTicker).

3. Saylor posted his Sunday Strategy tracker chart ("Connecting the dots"), the usual hint of a Monday 8-K, with Strategy at 849,327 BTC and an average cost of $75,451, now almost exactly where BTC trades; he also published an X Article Saturday tracing STRC's "digital credit" back to the Dutch East India Company, while MSCI's index decision lands Wednesday, Nov 11 (X/@saylor, Unchained, CoinPulseHQ).

4. Update on the Cybertruck wind-down: Musk said Saturday Tesla will add an extra Cybertruck shift because the backlog is "far more than Tesla can make" before the line is dismantled around June/July 2027 for Cybercab expansion, and said efficiency gains will allow a 40 kWh Cybercab pack (vs 47.6 kWh now, ~16% smaller) plus a liquid-silver option; Tesla's Robotaxi app v26.11.0 now compares Cybercab vs Model Y ETAs in Austin, with Cybercab rides due in Dallas this month (Reuters, Eletric-Vehicles, Teslarati).

5. Update on Starship Flight 15: SpaceX published its return-to-launch-site plan Saturday, with Ship 42 deploying Starlink V3 sats (three modified to image the heatshield), coasting ~21 hours in orbit, then reentering over the Pacific and flying over northern Mexico and south Texas for the first-ever ship tower catch alongside a booster catch; the Nov 13 window opens 4:45pm CT and still needs an FAA license modification (SpaceX, SpaceNews, Kurzia).

6. Alphabet's 13F shows it held 555,043,560 SpaceX shares worth $83.73B at Sept 30, adding 3,854,060 shares in Q3 from 551,189,500, a stake that started as a $900M investment in 2015 and that surfaced the same week Google's Don Harrison left the SpaceX board (FourWeekMBA, Venture Atlas, Tesla North).

7. Binance confirmed it will close affected EU accounts by Dec 31 after failing to win MiCA authorization before the transition period expired (deposits blocked, withdrawals open, a 0.025%/10 USDC monthly fee on remaining balances from Nov 29), while the EU launched a 12-month crypto task force against Russian sanctions evasion and Gnosis Pay disclosed a breach exposing card numbers and linked wallets (Investing.com).

8. Missed Saturday pre-9am: Berkshire's Q3 operating earnings fell 5.8% to $12.705B as insurance underwriting dropped 43% to $1.352B, while buybacks doubled to about $9.6B in the quarter ($14.4B YTD) and cash plus T-bills sat near $373B (Berkshire release/10-Q via The Company Chronicle).

AI, ROBOTICS, TECH & LONGEVITY

1. Anthropic agreed in late September to pay about $3.4B for 1.7 GW of heavy-duty Caterpillar gas generators by taking over OnePWR Solutions' existing orders, per the FT, as it heads into a roadshow next week for a Nasdaq listing under ANT before Thanksgiving; investor talk on X now centers on roughly $1.2–1.3T, down from the $2T floated earlier (FT via CNA/Investing.com, Epoch 0, X News).

2. A San Francisco federal magistrate judge ruled Anthropic must face claims that Claude Max's "5x or 20x more usage than Pro" pitch misled buyers, since the multiples were per 5-hour session while weekly caps rose only about 3.5x and 6x by the plaintiff's math; some claims were dismissed with leave to amend (Epoch 0).

3. Google DeepMind said human-supervised AI agents working with cryptographers Nadia Heninger and Emmanuel Thomé found two new weaknesses in legacy 1024-bit RSA, including a signature-forgery method estimated at ~1,600x faster than the best published attack and ~30x cheaper batch factoring, with 2048-bit keys unaffected and the big multipliers theoretical (DeepMind via BYOBot, Interesting Engineering).

4. In longevity, a Stanford-backed preprint built protein "aging clocks" for ten cell compartments from 61,931 people and found those with four or more prematurely aged compartments had up to 8x the risk of death and up to 22x the risk of kidney disease, with lysosome, plasma-membrane and Golgi signatures accelerating after about 60; separately, a worm study found triggering a low-oxygen alarm in a few brain cells extended lifespan up to 26% (The Long Run).

READS

1. "The Provenance of Digital Credit", Michael Saylor (X Article), Nov 7. Why read: Saylor's own long-form case for STRC, tracing the instrument through ten historical foundations from the Dutch East India Company to the B&O Railroad to Bitcoin, worth reading right before MSCI's Nov 11 call. https://x.com/saylor/status/2119069635534361025

2. "Independent Assessment of AI R&D Acceleration at Anthropic in October 2026", METR, Nov 5. Why read: the most detailed outside look yet at whether AI is speeding up a frontier lab, estimating Anthropic's capability gains now run about 1.9x the 2024–25 pace with ~80% attributed to AI-assisted R&D, and candid about what Anthropic redacted ahead of its IPO. https://metr.org/blog/2026-11-05-anthropic-ai-rd-acceleration-assessment/

2026-11-09.subject: Mon Nov 9 briefing: Strategy +1,036 BTC & $188M STRC buyback, BTC $73.8K low/$1B liqs, oil drops on Iran, Robotaxi San Antonio, SpaceX $24B Starbase compute, Nvidia probe
2026-11-09.bodyText:
News window: Sun 9:00am – Mon 9:00am ET

Note: Gap-catch for Sun 6–9am ET found nothing missed. Monday pre-market 8-K check: Strategy, Strive and Super League filed; Metaplanet reported no new buy (still 44,000 BTC).

MARKETS

1. Strategy's 8-K (filed 8:00am) shows it bought 1,036 BTC for $81.9M at an average $79,012 from Nov 2–8, lifting holdings to 850,364 BTC at a $64.16B cost ($75,456 average), and spent $188.3M buying back 1,887,464 STRC shares, all funded by selling 2,051,348 MSTR shares for $283.8M net under the ATM ($18.34B left), with the USD Reserve at $4.77B; BTC now trades about $700 below Strategy's average cost and MSTR was ~$124.9 premarket vs $128.93 Friday, about 0.93x diluted mNAV (SEC 8-K, Decrypt, The Block, StrategyViewer).

2. Bitcoin dropped to about $73,761 late Sunday, its lowest since August, as the Nvidia/Huang story and Rubio calling Iran's demands "outrageous" hit the only open market, triggering over $1B of liquidations in 24h ($913M longs; ETH $448M vs BTC $272M) and a loss of the 50-week moving average; it was ~$74.6–74.9K at 8am, pinned between the 200-day (~$73,150) and 100-day (~$77,430), with ETH briefly under $2,100 (CoinDesk, The Block, CoinGlass).

3. Oil and futures flipped the mood this morning after Trump told CNN further Iran strikes are "highly unlikely" and plans to meet Qatar's prime minister, a mediator: Brent fell ~3–4% to about $94–95 and WTI to ~$88, Dow futures +1% (~+500 pts), S&P +0.7%, Nasdaq 100 +0.4% (dragged by Nvidia), gold ~$4,095, ahead of Tuesday's October CPI and Friday's PPI with December hike fears still live after Friday's payrolls (AP, Reuters, Quartz, RTTNews, TipRanks).

4. Update on MSCI: the final November review drops Wednesday, Nov 11 after 11pm CET (~5pm ET); if Strategy lands on the deletion list, tracking funds must sell by the Nov 30 close, though removal requires failing the non-operating-company screen in both of its two most recent annual filings (TechTimes, MSCI).

5. Strive's 8-K shows 29 BTC bought Oct 31–Nov 6 at about $75,721, taking it to 43,153 BTC as it chases Metaplanet (44,000) for the No. 2 corporate spot, with SATA shares outstanding unchanged at 14,030,176; Super League (SLE) also disclosed 16 BTC bought Nov 4–9 near $76.9K (Strive 8-K, StockTitan).

6. Tesla launched unsupervised Robotaxi in San Antonio at 5am CT today, its largest zone yet at about 275 sq mi and its 8th driverless city, while Musk said Tesla will refund deposits to "a lot of people" as Cybertruck production winds down; TSLA was roughly flat to +0.2% premarket after last week's ~10% drop (Teslarati/Tesla Oracle, Not a Tesla App, TechCrunch, Stocktwits).

7. SpaceX filed plans for a $24B "super-compute facility" at Starbase with its own 748 MW gas plant (35 turbines) and is seeking a property-tax abatement, with a city hearing Dec 9; the project is about 17x the value of its 18,712 BTC (~$1.39B) (CoinDesk, City of Starbase notice).

8. SPCX rose ~2.4% premarket after Stifel's Jonathan Siegmann reiterated Buy with a $190 target, arguing the Democratic midterm sweep could stall rivals' data centers (Goldman reportedly sees ~45% of planned US capacity at risk) and make SpaceX, with an investment-grade balance sheet and $40B of committed Apollo GPU financing, the "buyer of last resort" for powered sites; he also flagged Qualcomm's selection as Starlink Mobile's 5G radio supplier and Flight 15 on Nov 13; a Falcon 9 flies USSF-627 tonight at 7:03pm PT (Stocktwits/Yahoo, TipRanks, SpaceX).

AI, ROBOTICS, TECH & LONGEVITY

1. Nvidia's board opened an independent investigation, led by outside counsel, after NYT/FT reports that Jensen Huang had an affair with Alice Huang, an executive at Singapore's Megaspeed whom US officials believe was passing information to Beijing; Huang admitted the affair to staff and intends to stay CEO, Nvidia says it has no reason to think secrets were compromised, China called it a smear, and NVDA was down ~4.5–5% premarket from $186.64 (Nvidia, Reuters, CoinDesk, AP).

2. Trump said he doesn't mind AI guardrails and could work with Democrats on safeguards so long as the US doesn't fall behind China, a notable shift after the midterms put data-center rules in play; OpenAI CFO Sarah Friar separately said it will keep building US data centers and stop requiring NDAs from public officials in site talks (The Neuron).

3. Apple's new CEO is reportedly pushing faster AI work beyond Siri, with a separate report saying agentic Siri control of first-party apps could arrive in iOS 27.3 and third-party actions in spring 2027; these are reported plans, not shipped products (The Neuron, Kill The AI).

4. DeepSeek's agent platform hit a reported 1.54M daily active users as the Chinese lab moves beyond standalone models, while Alibaba's new real-world coding-agent test found the top model fully completed only 26.4% of tasks despite 99%+ scores on older benchmarks (Bloomberg via The Neuron).

5. In robotics, Figure showed dozens of Figure 03 humanoids walking and interacting with people across its campus, and Apple researchers published work training a Unitree G1 entirely in simulation that hit a 91% success rate in unseen real environments (TechAU, HumanoidMegaHub).

READS

1. "The Bitcoin Bank of 2046", Fred Krueger (X Article), Nov 8. Why read: a clear-eyed 20-year sketch of what a Bitcoin bank built on custody, BTC-backed credit lines and mortgages, and digital credit like STRC could become, including the leverage and rehypothecation risks that could break it. https://x.com/dotkrueger/status/2119472095788941675

2. "Tesla & SpaceX: What a Merger Would Be Worth", Andrea Joseph (Substack), Nov 6. Why read: builds the combined company from both Q3 10-Qs ($3.4T value, $78B backlog, ~2.83 SPCX per TSLA share at market), runs sum-of-the-parts scenarios, and lays out the vote, Shanghai and Congress hurdles. https://ajcuckie.substack.com/p/tesla-and-spacex-what-a-merger-would

3. "Hard Money Dispatch 11/7/26: Can Anything Break Bitcoin?", Brian Nibley, Nov 8. Why read: a tidy recap of last week's ETF bleed and JPMorgan's first-ever 10% bitcoin return assumption, plus a sober takedown of the AI-breaks-ECDSA and quantum scares. https://brian-nibleys-newsletter.beehiiv.com/p/hard-money-dispatch-11-7-26-can-anything-break-bitcoin

Nvidia's board opened an independent investigation, led by outside counsel, after NYT/FT reports that Jensen Huang had an affair with Alice Huang, an executive at Singapore's Megaspeed whom US officials believe was passing information to Beijing; Huang admitted the affair to staff and intends to stay CEO, Nvidia says it has no reason to think secrets were compromised, China called it a smear, and NVDA was down ~4.5–5% premarket from $186.64 (Nvidia, Reuters, CoinDesk, AP).

2. Trump said he doesn't mind AI guardrails and could work with Democrats on safeguards so long as the US doesn't fall behind China, a notable shift after the midterms put data-center rules in play; OpenAI CFO Sarah Friar separately said it will keep building US data centers and stop requiring NDAs from public officials in site talks (The Neuron).

3. Apple's new CEO is reportedly pushing faster AI work beyond Siri, with a separate report saying agentic Siri control of first-party apps could arrive in iOS 27.3 and third-party actions in spring 2027; these are reported plans, not shipped products (The Neuron, Kill The AI).

4. DeepSeek's agent platform hit a reported 1.54M daily active users as the Chinese lab moves beyond standalone models, while Alibaba's new real-world coding-agent test found the top model fully completed only 26.4% of tasks despite 99%+ scores on older benchmarks (Bloomberg via The Neuron).

5. In robotics, Figure showed dozens of Figure 03 humanoids walking and interacting with people across its campus, and Apple researchers published work training a Unitree G1 entirely in simulation that hit a 91% success rate in unseen real environments (TechAU, HumanoidMegaHub).

READS

1. "The Bitcoin Bank of 2046", Fred Krueger (X Article), Nov 8. Why read: a clear-eyed 20-year sketch of what a Bitcoin bank built on custody, BTC-backed credit lines and mortgages, and digital credit like STRC could become, including the leverage and rehypothecation risks that could break it. https://x.com/dotkrueger/status/2119472095788941675

2. "Tesla & SpaceX: What a Merger Would Be Worth", Andrea Joseph (Substack), Nov 6. Why read: builds the combined company from both Q3 10-Qs ($3.4T value, $78B backlog, ~2.83 SPCX per TSLA share at market), runs sum-of-the-parts scenarios, and lays out the vote, Shanghai and Congress hurdles. https://ajcuckie.substack.com/p/tesla-and-spacex-what-a-merger-would

3. "Hard Money Dispatch 11/7/26: Can Anything Break Bitcoin?", Brian Nibley, Nov 8. Why read: a tidy recap of last week's ETF bleed and JPMorgan's first-ever 10% bitcoin return assumption, plus a sober takedown of the AI-breaks-ECDSA and quantum scares. https://brian-nibleys-newsletter.beehiiv.com/p/hard-money-dispatch-11-7-26-can-anything-break-bitcoin

2026-11-10.subject: Tue Nov 10 briefing: Hot CPI & Waller hike call, BTC $74K/ETF outflows, MSTR underwater before MSCI, MARA sells 13.6K BTC, SPCX NASA lunar pool, Anthropic IPO $70–78
2026-11-10.bodyText:
News window: Mon 9:00am – Tue 9:00am ET

Note: Gap-catch for Mon 6–9am ET found nothing missed from the pre-market 8-K batch. One early-Monday item yesterday's briefing missed, Coinbase's full OCC trust charter, is item 7 below (marked missed). Stories already in Monday's 5pm flash (the stock rally, TSLA's +5.5% close, Nvidia's GR00T 2 and NVDA's drop) are skipped.

MARKETS

1. October CPI came in hot at 8:30am: headline +0.4% vs +0.3% expected (Sept +0.6%) and core +0.3% vs +0.2%, with energy +0.7%, gasoline +1%, food +0.5%, transportation services +0.8% and shelter +0.3% (no year-over-year rate because of last year's shutdown); hours earlier Fed Governor Waller said in London he'll back at least a 25bp December hike from the current 3.75–4% range and that 50bp should be considered if core printed about 0.3% or more, which it just did; pre-CPI futures were mixed (S&P ~flat, Dow +0.35%, Nasdaq 100 −0.3%) with WTI ~$85 and Brent ~$90.6 after Trump said Iran action isn't necessary "at this point" (BLS, CNBC, Reuters, Federal Reserve, Yahoo Finance).

2. Bitcoin slid about 1.4% overnight to roughly $74.1–74.3K (low ~$74.0K) as traders added Fed-hike bets into CPI, while US spot BTC ETFs lost $201.1M Monday, a third straight outflow day, led by IBIT −$213.2M (its 7th straight outflow, ~$1.66B gone since Oct 30) with Morgan Stanley's MSBT (+$22.1M) the only fund taking money; ETF assets total $94.43B, about 6.27% of BTC's market cap (CoinDesk, Farside, SoSoValue, Cryptopolitan).

3. Update on Strategy: MSTR fell about 3–4% Monday to roughly $124–125 after the 1,036 BTC/$188M STRC-buyback 8-K, STRC sat at $99.98, and with BTC near $74.6K the 850,364 BTC stack is about $685M under its $75,456 average cost; MSCI's November list lands Wednesday ~5pm ET, with JPMorgan estimating ~$2.8B of forced MSTR selling if it is deleted (effective after the Nov 30 close) (Blockhead, The Coin Republic, TechTimes).

4. MARA posted Q3 net income of $634.4M on ~$885M of bitcoin fair-value gains even as revenue fell 35% to $164.2M, and disclosed it sold 13,597 BTC (~$1.1B) after quarter-end, using $750M to fully repay its bitcoin-backed loans, as it pivots to AI infrastructure (debt down 37% YTD to $1.4B, hashrate 71.2 EH/s); the stock rose 4.6% Monday before the release and was flat after hours (The Block, MARA shareholder letter).

5. SPCX rose 5.8% to $142.07 Monday, a second straight gain after Friday's +8.6%, after NASA named SpaceX one of eight providers in its 10-year CLPS 2 lunar-delivery contract ($10B combined ceiling, won task by task) plus a separate 2028 Starship mission to carry comms satellites to cislunar space, and Barclays called T-Mobile the cleanest fit if SpaceX buys a carrier for its 2027 terrestrial 5G plan; it was −0.5% premarket (NASA, GuruFocus, Stocktwits/Yahoo Finance).

6. Update on Cybertruck: Tesla stopped taking orders for the Premium AWD (RWD was already closed), leaving only the Cyberbeast, which it raised $7,500 to $109,990 with deliveries now Mar–Jun 2027, while Reuters notes Cybertruck sales fell 28% YTD through September to ~11,600; Jefferies cut its TSLA target to $375 from $400 (Hold), saying a SpaceX merger got harder after the midterms, and TSLA was ~$376.27 premarket (Tesla Oracle, Reuters).

7. Missed (Mon ~5am ET): the OCC upgraded Coinbase's national trust bank from conditional to a full charter, letting it offer federally regulated custody and payments under the GENIUS Act framework a month after Ripple got the same, while community bankers (ICBA) are suing the OCC over crypto charters; separately, Coinbase, Kalshi and Kraken's parent backed the CFTC in a legal fight over stock perpetual futures (CoinDesk).

AI, ROBOTICS, TECH & LONGEVITY

1. Anthropic launched its IPO roadshow at a revised $70–78 range (vs $70–80 in Monday night's Reuters report) for 825M Class A shares on Nasdaq as "ANT," reportedly pricing Nov 18 and trading Nov 19 with ~20% retail allocation; at the top it would net up to $64.35B at up to $1.405T fully diluted, AMD, Broadcom, Google, Micron, Microsoft, Nvidia and TSMC agreed to buy $26B more in a private placement at the IPO price, run-rate revenue hit ~$81B at end-October (+$10B in a month), and the book is reportedly already covered (CNBC, Anthropic).

2. Anthropic also released Claude Fable 5.2 (generally available) and Mythos 5.2 (verified orgs only), the same model running ~30% faster than 5.1 at a lower $8/$40 per million input/output tokens, scoring 49.1% on FrontierCode 2.0, with ~1,000 Fable agents formalizing Fermat's Last Theorem in 30 hours; notably, Anthropic says it deliberately held AI-research abilities like kernel optimization to about Opus 5.5's level (Anthropic via PoYo, CNBC).

3. Google unveiled TPU 8tx (confidential inference and small-scale training, up to ~2x lower latency than 8t) and TPU 8i Max (two 8i chips per package, doubling compute, SRAM and HBM bandwidth), its 3rd and 4th eighth-gen TPU systems this year, said it has nearly 100 external TPU customers and open-sourced TorchTPU so PyTorch runs natively (Google/Amin Vahdat, Japan Times).

4. Meta launched Muse Ember, its smallest agent-execution model at $0.10/$0.50 per million input/output tokens with a 1M-token context, claiming more intelligence per dollar than Claude Haiku 5.5 or GPT-6 Luna (37.8 vs 13.9 and 20.2 on AutomationBench-AA) at ~$0.14 per Artificial Analysis task (Meta, TechCrunch).

5. OpenAI put ChatGPT Enterprise (including ChatGPT Work, Codex and dots) on AWS Marketplace so companies can buy it through private offers that count toward their AWS spend commitments (OpenAI).

6. Longevity: a Nature Biotechnology paper found all six proteomic aging clocks tested showed lower biological age in patients on Insilico's TNIK inhibitor rentosertib in a 12-week phase 2a lung-fibrosis trial, with pathway shifts in senescence and metabolism, though the authors say clocks alone can't separate anti-aging from anti-disease effects (Fight Aging!, Nature Biotechnology).

READS

1. "SpaceX Q4 Model - A Super Intelligence Co. with rockets & connectivity", Ryan Zurrer (X Article), Nov 9. Why read: an updated SpaceX model arguing a $288/share target is covered by AI, launch and Starlink alone, with orbital compute, Terafab and a Tesla merger as free upside. https://x.com/kukulabanze/status/2119829630337081666

2. "Anthropic's Second S-1 Is a Bit More Honest", David Appelbaum (The Mentat Project, Substack), Nov 4. Why read: a sharp read of the amended filing before you weigh the ANT roadshow, covering the $895.4B of commitments, Q3's slip back to a GAAP operating loss, compute at 58% of revenue, and why the IPO doesn't solve the capital need. https://davidappelbaum2.substack.com/p/anthropics-second-s-1-is-a-bit-more

3. "The Wrapper Is Now the Risk", Satoshi Institute (Daily Signals #223), Nov 4. Why read: a timely frame for Wednesday's MSCI call, arguing treasury companies are now judged on mNAV, dilution, preferred obligations and index eligibility rather than BTC accumulation alone. https://satoshiinstitute.com/newsletter/23692e9c-2c26-4fc3-8ab0-ca1e9ce8caa0

2026-11-11.subject: Wed Nov 11 briefing: CoreWeave sparks AI rebound, MSCI verdict tonight for MSTR, BTC tests 200-day, Starship double catch Fri, Anthropic eyes $1.5T, OpenAI $10B quarter
2026-11-11.bodyText:
News window: Tue 9:00am – Wed 9:00am ET

Note: Gap-catch for Tue 6–9am ET found nothing missed. Stories already in Tuesday's 5pm flash (the stock close, MSTR's $121.07 close, the SpaceX arbitration ruling, Gemini 4 Carbon, Gemini Robotics 2.5 and NVDA's -5.5% day) are skipped.

MARKETS

1. Futures are rallying on Veterans Day (bond market closed) after CoreWeave's Q3 beat: at 8:26am Dow E-minis were +0.29%, S&P 500 +0.96% and Nasdaq 100 +1.98%, with CoreWeave +15.6% premarket on revenue of $3.66B (+168% y/y), a raised $13.0–13.3B full-year guide, a ~$133B backlog and a target of adjusted profitability in 1H 2028 (net loss still widened to $709M), pulling Nebius +13.9%, Applied Digital +10.1%, Marvell +9.1% and Micron +7.4%; CME FedWatch now treats a December hike as a certainty with an 11.5% chance of 50bp, and oil rose more than 1% after Iran's security chief said enriched nuclear material won't leave the country (Reuters, CoinDesk).

2. Update on MSCI: the November review list lands shortly after 5pm ET tonight, the first under the non-operating-company rules (Strategy, Metaplanet and Yellow Cake were flagged in the May simulation, SharpLink on the watchlist; current members are cut only if they fail the screen in both of their last two annual filings, effective after the Nov 30 close); index funds hold about 13M MSTR shares (3.1% of basic shares, ~$1.57B at Tuesday's close) versus JPMorgan's older ~$2.8B forced-selling estimate, MSTR is down ~16.6% since its $145.16 close on Oct 28, and Metaplanet closed -2.5% at ¥231 in Tokyo today (Bitcoin.com, crypto.news, Stocktwits, MSCI).

3. Bitcoin is sitting out the stock bounce at about $73.9K (7:30am) after tagging its 200-day moving average near $73.1–73.2K and a ~$72.7K low Tuesday, as futures liquidations jumped 288% to $725M; CryptoQuant flags USDT's market cap down $6.6B over 60 days (the biggest contraction in its data since 2022), the Coinbase Premium negative for 30 straight days and its Bull Score down to 20 from 90 on Oct 13, while 8 of Deribit's 10 most active contracts through Nov 27 are $69–74K puts (CoinDesk, Fortune).

4. US spot BTC ETFs lost $95.0M Tuesday, a fourth straight outflow day but the smallest of the run (after -$201M Mon, -$412M Fri, -$430M Thu), led by IBIT -$78.2M and FBTC -$36.8M with Morgan Stanley's MSBT again the lone inflow (+$20.0M); November outflows now total $1.58B and cumulative net inflows since launch are $55.47B (Farside via Gate, CoinDesk).

5. TSLA was +1.75% to $386.44 premarket after Finland's Traficom approved Tesla's supervised Assisted Driving system for immediate rollout by recognizing the Dutch provisional approval (joining the Netherlands, Estonia, Croatia and Belgium), Musk posted that "Cybercab will do a majority of all passenger miles in any jurisdiction where it is not prohibited by law," and Morgan Stanley nudged its target to $410 from $400 (Hold) on robotaxi scaling and FSD take rates (Reuters, Benzinga, GMT Eight).

6. Update on Starship Flight 15: SpaceX's mission page confirms a Friday Nov 13 launch with a 75-minute window opening 5:45pm ET pending approval, attempting the first-ever catch of both halves (Super Heavy ~6.5 minutes after liftoff, Ship ~22.5 hours later after 14 orbits) while deploying 26 Starlink V3 satellites; SPCX was ~$146.20 (+2.2%) premarket even as Dan Ives says it carries a 20–25% "political discount" after the Texas governor race, though he still expects SpaceX to buy Tesla (SpaceX, Yahoo Finance, Benzinga).

7. Institutional crypto plumbing kept advancing: Deutsche Bank's digital-asset custody service (BTC, ETH, stablecoins) went live for European institutions with Asia planned next, and the London Stock Exchange dropped its no-leverage, physical-backing and cold-storage requirements for professional-only bitcoin and ether ETNs, opening the door to leveraged products; separately, France's Capital B added 12 BTC (€0.84M) to reach 3,550 BTC (CoinDesk, Crypto Briefing).

AI, ROBOTICS, TECH & LONGEVITY

1. Update on Anthropic's IPO: the FT reports bankers are weighing a move above the $70–78 range that could lift the valuation to $1.5T or more on strong demand, with Bloomberg tallying roughly $100B in total including the $26B partner placement and ~$9.7B greenshoe (vs SpaceX's $86.2B record in June); Dario Amodei does a livestreamed talk with Jamie Dimon Friday ahead of the Nov 18 pricing, and Anthropic also rolled out Claude Sheets, Whiteboards, Claude Data dashboards and a Claude Meetings beta (FT, Bloomberg, The Neuron).

2. OpenAI's Q3 revenue rose nearly 50% q/q to about $10B (roughly 3x a year ago), but its operating loss widened to $10.9B from $10.1B even as the adjusted operating margin improved to -109% from -150%; it also launched a Businesses in ChatGPT beta with Business Agents for US e-commerce firms and acquired AI travel startup Odessia (WSJ via Reuters, OpenAI, TechCrunch).

3. SoftBank posted a ¥1.115T (~$7B) July–September net loss, its first quarterly loss since late 2024, mostly from ~¥600B of write-offs on US data-center power-equipment prepayments, with NAV falling to ¥59.8T and LTV rising to 15.9%; the stock opened -10.5% at ¥3,465 in Tokyo today before paring to about -2.8% by midday, while OpenAI's mark was held at $99.6B per SoftBank's books (CNBC, Aju Press/Nikkei, SoftBank).

4. Update on Nvidia: NVDA was +3.7% premarket after shedding about $430B of market value over the last two sessions on the Jensen Huang affair and spy-probe story, with Marvell, Micron, Seagate (+9.5%) and Western Digital (+8.6%) leading a broad chip and storage rebound (Reuters).

5. Google DeepMind's AlphaProof Code generated more than six million lines of machine-checked proof to verify specified security properties of Signal's encryption code in four weeks, and confirmed it rejects older versions with known bugs, a notable step for AI-driven formal verification (The Neuron).

6. Longevity: a University of Michigan study in Frontiers in Aging found ergothioneine (a mushroom-derived compound) rose in the brain and blood of mice across all five known lifespan-extending interventions (rapamycin, acarbose, canagliflozin, 17α-estradiol and calorie restriction), and an AI model trained on four of them picked out the fifth in 33 of 35 tests, though causation isn't yet shown (ScienceAlert, Frontiers in Aging).

READS

1. "Anthropic IPO, part three: a price range, a smaller valuation and a fuller filing", Igor Rotor, CFA (Atrani Capital, Substack), Nov 10. Why read: the clearest walk-through of the new terms before pricing, from the $900.9B of commitments and lock-up calendar to the Q4 revenue add (above $5.4B vs below $4B) that would make or break the growth story. https://atranicapital.substack.com/p/anthropic-ipo-part-three-a-price

2. "By The Fingernails", James Check (Checkonchain newsletter), Nov 10. Why read: an on-chain map of why the $75K–$72K zone is the last line for a healthy correction, with a read on cohort panic and the mixed spot and futures signals (paid). https://newsletter.checkonchain.com/p/by-the-fingernails

3. "The Jensen Huang Story Gets Worse, Washington vs. New York, Silicon Valley", Ben Thompson (Stratechery), Nov 10. Why read: frames the Huang scandal as a governance and succession crisis for Nvidia and what a leadership vacuum would mean for hyperscalers and labs like Anthropic (paid). https://stratechery.com/2026/the-jensen-huang-story-gets-worse-washington-vs-new-york-silicon-valley/

4. "Pt. 3 - Understanding Elon's Decision: The Great Wave of Autonomy Must Be Now", Ben Schaffer (X Article), Nov 9. Why read: a bull's case for shifting Cybertruck capacity to Cybercab, arguing autonomy's political window is the next two years. https://x.com/BenSchafferUP/status/2119843160230912090

TSLA was +1.75% to $386.44 premarket after Finland's Traficom approved Tesla's supervised Assisted Driving system for immediate rollout by recognizing the Dutch provisional approval (joining the Netherlands, Estonia, Croatia and Belgium), Musk posted that "Cybercab will do a majority of all passenger miles in any jurisdiction where it is not prohibited by law," and Morgan Stanley nudged its target to $410 from $400 (Hold) on robotaxi scaling and FSD take rates (Reuters, Benzinga, GMT Eight).

6. Update on Starship Flight 15: SpaceX's mission page confirms a Friday Nov 13 launch with a 75-minute window opening 5:45pm ET pending approval, attempting the first-ever catch of both halves (Super Heavy ~6.5 minutes after liftoff, Ship ~22.5 hours later after 14 orbits) while deploying 26 Starlink V3 satellites; SPCX was ~$146.20 (+2.2%) premarket even as Dan Ives says it carries a 20–25% "political discount" after the Texas governor race, though he still expects SpaceX to buy Tesla (SpaceX, Yahoo Finance, Benzinga).

7. Institutional crypto plumbing kept advancing: Deutsche Bank's digital-asset custody service (BTC, ETH, stablecoins) went live for European institutions with Asia planned next, and the London Stock Exchange dropped its no-leverage, physical-backing and cold-storage requirements for professional-only bitcoin and ether ETNs, opening the door to leveraged products; separately, France's Capital B added 12 BTC (€0.84M) to reach 3,550 BTC (CoinDesk, Crypto Briefing).

AI, ROBOTICS, TECH & LONGEVITY

1. Update on Anthropic's IPO: the FT reports bankers are weighing a move above the $70–78 range that could lift the valuation to $1.5T or more on strong demand, with Bloomberg tallying roughly $100B in total including the $26B partner placement and ~$9.7B greenshoe (vs SpaceX's $86.2B record in June); Dario Amodei does a livestreamed talk with Jamie Dimon Friday ahead of the Nov 18 pricing, and Anthropic also rolled out Claude Sheets, Whiteboards, Claude Data dashboards and a Claude Meetings beta (FT, Bloomberg, The Neuron).

2. OpenAI's Q3 revenue rose nearly 50% q/q to about $10B (roughly 3x a year ago), but its operating loss widened to $10.9B from $10.1B even as the adjusted operating margin improved to -109% from -150%; it also launched a Businesses in ChatGPT beta with Business Agents for US e-commerce firms and acquired AI travel startup Odessia (WSJ via Reuters, OpenAI, TechCrunch).

3. SoftBank posted a ¥1.115T (~$7B) July–September net loss, its first quarterly loss since late 2024, mostly from ~¥600B of write-offs on US data-center power-equipment prepayments, with NAV falling to ¥59.8T and LTV rising to 15.9%; the stock opened -10.5% at ¥3,465 in Tokyo today before paring to about -2.8% by midday, while OpenAI's mark was held at $99.6B per SoftBank's books (CNBC, Aju Press/Nikkei, SoftBank).

4. Update on Nvidia: NVDA was +3.7% premarket after shedding about $430B of market value over the last two sessions on the Jensen Huang affair and spy-probe story, with Marvell, Micron, Seagate (+9.5%) and Western Digital (+8.6%) leading a broad chip and storage rebound (Reuters).

5. Google DeepMind's AlphaProof Code generated more than six million lines of machine-checked proof to verify specified security properties of Signal's encryption code in four weeks, and confirmed it rejects older versions with known bugs, a notable step for AI-driven formal verification (The Neuron).

6. Longevity: a University of Michigan study in Frontiers in Aging found ergothioneine (a mushroom-derived compound) rose in the brain and blood of mice across all five known lifespan-extending interventions (rapamycin, acarbose, canagliflozin, 17α-estradiol and calorie restriction), and an AI model trained on four of them picked out the fifth in 33 of 35 tests, though causation isn't yet shown (ScienceAlert, Frontiers in Aging).

READS

1. "Anthropic IPO, part three: a price range, a smaller valuation and a fuller filing", Igor Rotor, CFA (Atrani Capital, Substack), Nov 10. Why read: the clearest walk-through of the new terms before pricing, from the $900.9B of commitments and lock-up calendar to the Q4 revenue add (above $5.4B vs below $4B) that would make or break the growth story. https://atranicapital.substack.com/p/anthropic-ipo-part-three-a-price

2. "By The Fingernails", James Check (Checkonchain newsletter), Nov 10. Why read: an on-chain map of why the $75K–$72K zone is the last line for a healthy correction, with a read on cohort panic and the mixed spot and futures signals (paid). https://newsletter.checkonchain.com/p/by-the-fingernails

3. "The Jensen Huang Story Gets Worse, Washington vs. New York, Silicon Valley", Ben Thompson (Stratechery), Nov 10. Why read: frames the Huang scandal as a governance and succession crisis for Nvidia and what a leadership vacuum would mean for hyperscalers and labs like Anthropic (paid). https://stratechery.com/2026/the-jensen-huang-story-gets-worse-washington-vs-new-york-silicon-valley/

4. "Pt. 3 - Understanding Elon's Decision: The Great Wave of Autonomy Must Be Now", Ben Schaffer (X Article), Nov 9. Why read: a bull's case for shifting Cybertruck capacity to Cybercab, arguing autonomy's political window is the next two years. https://x.com/BenSchafferUP/status/2119843160230912090

2026-11-12.subject: Thu Nov 12 briefing: Jensen Huang resigns, MSTR -6% on MSCI exit, BTC $72.7K/ETF outflows, Robotaxi 24/7, SpaceX 100 GW solar, Nebius slump
2026-11-12.bodyText:
News window: Wed 9:00am – Thu 9:00am ET

Note: Gap-catch for Wed 6–9am ET found nothing missed (Veterans Day, no treasury-company 8-Ks). Stories already in Wednesday's 5pm flash (Cybertruck extension, Anthropic's SpaceX compute exit, AlphaGenome 2, Anthropic roadshow video) are skipped.

MARKETS

1. Update on MSCI: the final November review deletes Strategy from the MSCI USA and World indexes at the Nov 30 close (the only one of 24 USA deletions not moving down to small cap), alongside Metaplanet (out of MSCI Japan Small Cap), Upexi, Yellow Cake, Skel and Agronomics, with 19 names including SharpLink on a watchlist; MSTR was $114.90 premarket (-6.1%, 8:45am) from a $122.35 close, as index funds must sell ~13M shares (~$1.6B, under one day's volume) versus JPMorgan's older $2.8B estimate ($8.8B if other indexers follow), mNAV sits near 1.08x, and 10x Research's Markus Thielen calls it "largely priced in" (MSCI via Unchained, Reuters, CoinDesk, Webull).

2. Futures turned lower after Wednesday's rally (S&P 500 +1.31% to 7,619, Nasdaq +1.60%, Dow +0.49%): at 7:52am Nasdaq 100 E-minis were -0.96% and S&P -0.42% as Nvidia sank ~9% premarket; initial jobless claims rose 9,000 to 200,000 (vs 194,000 expected), the 10-year sits near 5.00%, WTI is $85.78 (-0.9%), gold -1.5%, and PPI is due Friday (Options Recap, DOL, GTA Wire).

3. Bitcoin slipped to about $72.7K (-1.6% on the day) below its 200-day average near $73.1K and Glassnode's short-term-holder cost basis of $75.6K, with Glassnode flagging stablecoin supply down $14.2B in 30 days (fastest contraction since June 2022), the deepest Coinbase discount since February, and the biggest resting bids clustered at $68–72.5K (CoinPulse, Glassnode).

4. US spot BTC ETFs lost $299.9M Wednesday, a fifth straight outflow day, with IBIT -$269.7M and GBTC -$39.1M against MSBT's lone +$9.0M inflow; five-day outflows total $1.44B, November is -$1.88B, total assets are $93.70B and cumulative net inflows have slipped to ~$55.1B (Farside via CoinPulse, Corgano).

5. Tesla's Robotaxi now runs 24/7 in all eight US cities it serves, up from 16 hours a day in August, with Musk posting that "Robotaxi works 168 hours a week"; TSLA was $386.60 premarket (-1.1%) after Wednesday's +2.9% close at $390.84 (Tesla, Benzinga, eletric-vehicles.com, GuruFocus).

6. SpaceX signed Germany's Singulus Technologies for a turnkey heterojunction solar-cell line (first delivery early 2027 at Bastrop, Texas; announced Tue, missed earlier), and Musk confirmed it is ordering 100 GW a year of capacity to power Starmind orbital AI data-center satellites; SPCX was ~$137.6–138.1 premarket (-1.3%) ahead of Friday's 5:45pm ET Starship Flight 15 double-catch attempt (pv magazine, The Space Tap, GuruFocus, Public).

7. Bank and retail crypto rails keep widening: Israel Discount Bank ($150B in assets) will offer in-app BTC/ETH trading from Nov 26 with Fireblocks custody, and Russia's central bank is opening retail crypto trading on local exchanges from Nov 17 with a 300,000-ruble (~$3,600) annual cap for non-qualified investors (X News summaries citing the banks).

AI, ROBOTICS, TECH & LONGEVITY

1. Jensen Huang has resigned as Nvidia's president, CEO and director effective immediately, with CFO Colette Kress named interim CEO (staying CFO), former Synopsys CEO Harvey Jones appointed the company's first-ever board chair and a search under way for internal and external candidates; it follows WSJ and NYT reports of two affairs (one with a Megaspeed executive US intelligence suspects is a Chinese spy, one with healthcare VP Kimberly Powell), NVDA fell from a $173.73 close to $158.78 after hours and was ~-9% premarket at 8:36am, Bernstein halved its target to $200, and Q3 results still land Tue Nov 17 (Nvidia, Forbes, CNBC, WSJ).

2. Nebius beat with Q3 revenue of $980.8M (+571% y/y vs ~$907.5M expected) but pared its 2026 revenue forecast on data-center capacity delays and guided 2027 capex above $40B, sending shares ~10% lower premarket, while CoreWeave gave back ~7% premarket after Wednesday's ~25% surge (Reuters, CNBC, Sina Finance, CNBC TV18).

3. Ramp's AI Index shows US corporate AI spend hit another record in October but grew just 1.65% m/m, with the top 1% of companies accounting for 80% of OpenAI and Anthropic revenue in Ramp's data; separately, Democratic lawmakers are drafting a bill for a Department of Artificial Intelligence that would require federal permission to train advanced models (The Neuron).

4. Google launched the Gemini Decisions API (up to 1,000 yes/no, multiple-choice or scoring decisions per request with confidence scores, from $0.10 per million input tokens) and brought Gemini Live to Apple CarPlay, while Alibaba's Qwen released Qwen4-Max-Preview and Amazon shipped a free AWS Emulator covering 200+ services that it says AI agents wrote entirely (The Neuron).

5. United Airlines is blocking unauthorized AI agents from completing flight bookings, letting assistants show options but requiring humans to check out, an early test of who controls agentic purchasing (The Neuron).

6. Longevity: a mouse study found the short peptide elamipretide reversed multiple markers of age-related ovarian decline, adding to evidence that mitochondria-targeted drugs can slow reproductive aging (Lifespan Research Institute).

READS

1. "Running on Empty" (The Week On-chain, Week 45), Glassnode, Nov 11. Why read: the cleanest map of where BTC stands now, from short-term holders underwater and record stablecoin redemptions to the $68–72.5K bid wall and the levels that would confirm or kill the August trend change. https://research.glassnode.com/the-week-onchain-week-45-2026/

2. "Anthropic's Q&A Briefing: Lots of Key Numbers. Has Expectations Management Begun?", Longbridge Dolphin Research (X Article), Nov 11. Why read: pulls the hard numbers from the syndicate analysts' Q&A (a Q4 guide annualizing to $77.2B vs October's $81B ARR, ~$90B of 2027 training compute) and argues 2027 margins likely turn negative, useful before the Nov 18 pricing. https://x.com/dolphinR123/status/2120493875236409854

3. "MSCI is dropping Strategy from its index, and the exclusion could hit its bitcoin-buying machine", Omkar Godbole (CoinDesk), Nov 12. Why read: lays out the real cost of the MSCI exit, not the forced selling but the squeeze on mNAV (~1.08x) that makes new equity less accretive, with bull and bear views from 10x Research and others. https://www.coindesk.com/markets/2026/11/12/msci-is-dropping-strategy-from-its-index-and-the-exclusion-could-hit-its-bitcoin-buying-machine

2026-11-13.subject: Fri Nov 13 briefing: BTC under $70K/$1.6B liqs, PPI +0.3%, MSTR $111.7 pre, Metaplanet guide cut, Starship Flight 15, Nvidia fallout
2026-11-13.bodyText:
News window: Thu 9:00am – Fri 9:00am ET

Note: Stories already in Thursday's 5pm flash (SpaceX-Tesla merger timing, Gemini 4 Hydrogen, AMAT/Cisco results, Thursday's BTC/MSTR close) are skipped except where there's a new development. Gap-catch for Thu 6–9am ET: the only missed item was Strategy's 8:00am announcement of a live retail-investor Q&A with Michael Saylor and Phong Le (Business Wire); no treasury-company 8-Ks were missed.

MARKETS

1. October PPI came in at +0.3% m/m vs +0.4% expected (September revised up to +1.4%), +6.5% y/y vs +6.6% (the biggest 12-month rise since Nov 2022), with core +0.3% m/m and +5.0% y/y in line, the last PPI before the Dec 8–9 FOMC; futures jumped after the print, with S&P 500 futures +0.70% to 7,668, Nasdaq 100 +0.67% and Dow +0.63% at 8:34am, though CME FedWatch still showed ~87–88% odds of a 25bp December hike, the 10-year was ~5.1% and the Dollar Index sat above 103, its highest since April 2025 (BLS, Markets Insider, FXStreet, CoinDesk).

2. Update on Bitcoin: BTC broke below $70,000 overnight for the first time since August and hit ~$67,770 (CoinDesk) before trading ~$69.2K around 8am (about -5% in 24 hours), as 24-hour crypto liquidations reached $1.64B (88.7% longs, $916M in BTC, the biggest a $31.1M Hyperliquid long at $72,250), one-week 25-delta skew jumped to ~14% toward puts, Fear & Greed fell to 19, ETH touched $1,900, and price tagged the 200-week moving average near $68K for the first time since August (CoinDesk, The Block, nodewitness, Rekt Capital).

3. US spot BTC ETFs posted a sixth straight outflow day Thursday, about -$80.3M with IBIT still unreported (FBTC -$32.6M, BITB -$26.4M, ARKB -$18.5M, MSBT +$3.3M), taking November to roughly -$1.96B and six-day outflows to ~$1.5B (Farside via WhaleRoom, Corgano, CoinDesk).

4. MSTR was $111.72 premarket (-2.35% at 8:14am) after Thursday's -6.49% close at $114.41, and at ~$69.3K BTC, Strategy's 850,364 BTC (average cost $75,456) are roughly $5.2B underwater; separately, JPMorgan's 13F shows it raised its Strategy stake 36% to 848,932 shares and its IBIT holding 9.6% to 11.41M shares (~$540M) as of Sep 30 (GuruFocus, Strategy 8-K, The Block).

5. Metaplanet cut FY2026 guidance about 60% (revenue ¥16.0B to ¥6.5B, operating profit ¥11.4B to ¥3.0B), saying it held back on share issuance with mNAV below 1.0x and steered convertible proceeds into buybacks first (¥28.27B for 108.7M shares so far, including ¥3.0B for 12.26M shares Nov 1–12); 9-month net loss was ¥27.16B, including a ¥19.17B loss on the Q3 sale of 10,000 BTC (later bought back 11,000), and it held 44,000 BTC at Sep 30 (Metaplanet TSE filings).

6. Nakamoto (NAKA) amended its Kraken USDT loan in a 4:35pm Thursday 8-K, pushing $60M of the $165M June loan from Dec 4, 2026 to Dec 4, 2027 (the other $105M still matures June 30, 2027, so no principal is due in 2026) and letting the net value of its BTC derivatives at Kraken, such as puts, count toward collateral (SEC 8-K).

7. The White House made its first SEC and CFTC nominations in about a year: Kristin Johnson (D, former CFTC commissioner) and Steven Levine (R, to succeed Hester Peirce) for the SEC, and Clarity Act negotiators Nathan Anonick (R) and Matthew Rowland (D) for the CFTC; separately, the DOJ and CFTC sued Arkansas to block state enforcement against Kalshi a day after Louisiana sued Kalshi, Robinhood and other prediction markets (The Block).

8. The DOJ says it has court authorization to seize or restrain more than $1.2B of crypto stolen in the Oct 29 Binance hack, which the FBI pins on North Korea's TraderTraitor group, part of more than $2.7B frozen so far out of the ~$6.3B taken, and it also seized infrastructure behind the "FaceStealer" deepfake video-call scheme blamed for $400M+ in thefts (DOJ, The Block).

9. SpaceX's Starship Flight 15 is set for tonight's 75-minute window opening 5:45pm ET, aiming to catch both the Super Heavy booster and the ship (the ship catch comes after a ~22.5-hour mission), with launch weather at 0% rain but the launch and re-entry licenses still shown as pending approval overnight; SPCX was ~$140.60–140.85 premarket (+0.5–0.65%) (SpaceX, Visit Starbase, Public, StockMarketWatch).

10. TSLA was $400.13 premarket (+0.67% at 7am) after a five-day +15.6% run that added ~$174B in value (Trefis), and Tesla pulled the $41,990 Model Y AWD from its US configurator, making the cheapest new AWD Model Y $49,990 (+$8,000) (GuruFocus, InsideEVs).

AI, ROBOTICS, TECH & LONGEVITY

1. Update on Nvidia: SemiAnalysis's Dylan Patel says Google and AMD could take share with Huang gone and suspects a US-intelligence role in his exit as Washington readies limits on remote access to chips in overseas data centers; CNBC reports the exit puts the $500B Nvidia-backed AI financing push with six Wall Street firms in doubt, Cathie Wood warns NVDA's five-year growth rate could be cut in half, and the stock rose ~1% after hours from Thursday's $166.19 close (Benzinga, OfficeChai, Asia Times, CNBC via AI Weekly, FXStreet).

2. Former OpenAI researcher Will DePue published a forensic analysis of released model weights showing six Chinese models (DeepSeek-V4-Flash and V4-Pro, Kimi K3 and K3.1-Pro, MiniMax-M3, Ant's Ling-3.1-flash) were initialized on export-controlled Nvidia Blackwell systems, with matches of 49–1,385 standard deviations against ~8 expected by chance and estimated $150–200M clusters per run, though it can't show where the chips sat or who owned them (Dataconomy, Crypto Briefing).

3. Update on Anthropic: its IPO is about six times oversubscribed (Bloomberg, 4:06pm Thu), with 825M shares at $70–78 (up to $64.4B plus a $26B private placement, ~$1.4T fully diluted at the top), pricing ~Nov 18 and Nasdaq trading as ANT on Nov 19; it also put self-hosted Claude Managed Agents into private beta so enterprises can run the agent harness in their own cloud or on-prem (Bloomberg, Help Net Security).

4. A global Microsoft 365 outage hitting Outlook, Teams and Copilot ran into a second day across 74 countries, disrupting governments and airlines, and MSFT was ~-2.6% premarket (Forbes, Al Jazeera, Invezz).

5. OpenAI's Greg Brockman launched Daybreak Red Team and Daybreak Defense Factory security agents, arguing companies are only as secure as the frontier model defending them, and Runway open-sourced Praxis-1, a 27B mixture-of-experts robot-control model under Apache 2.0 (The Register, Hugging Face via AI Weekly).

READS

1. "Nvidia and the World Without Jensen", Dylan Patel, Doug, Wayne Ma and Jordan Nanos (SemiAnalysis), Nov 12. Why read: the deepest take yet on what Huang's exit means for export controls, the supply chain, open-source models and Nvidia's moat. https://newsletter.semianalysis.com/p/nvidia-and-the-world-without-jensen

2. "Anthropic's share price is about to set the terms of its suppliers' financing", Haircut (@nodiligence, X Article), Nov 12. Why read: maps how Google, Amazon, Broadcom, Micron and SpaceX are selling Anthropic chips, buying its IPO and lending to it, and why the ANT share price will decide how those deals pay out. https://x.com/nodiligence/status/2120944219665961284

3. "#BVL072: Under Pressure", Bitcoin Vector (Willy Woo's Substack), Nov 11. Why read: an on-chain and liquidity read on why BTC lost its $80.5–87.5K range and what would mark a floor, written just before this week's break under $70K (partly paywalled). https://willywoo.substack.com/p/bvl072-under-pressure
