Update on Bitcoin: BTC broke below $70,000 overnight for the first time since August and hit ~$67,770 (CoinDesk) before trading ~$69.2K around 8am (about -5% in 24 hours), as 24-hour crypto liquidations reached $1.64B (88.7% longs, $916M in BTC, the biggest a $31.1M Hyperliquid long at $72,250), one-week 25-delta skew jumped to ~14% toward puts, Fear & Greed fell to 19, ETH touched $1,900, and price tagged the 200-week moving average near $68K for the first time since August (CoinDesk, The Block, nodewitness, Rekt Capital).

3. US spot BTC ETFs posted a sixth straight outflow day Thursday, about -$80.3M with IBIT still unreported (FBTC -$32.6M, BITB -$26.4M, ARKB -$18.5M, MSBT +$3.3M), taking November to roughly -$1.96B and six-day outflows to ~$1.5B (Farside via WhaleRoom, Corgano, CoinDesk).

4. MSTR was $111.72 premarket (-2.35% at 8:14am) after Thursday's -6.49% close at $114.41, and at ~$69.3K BTC, Strategy's 850,364 BTC (average cost $75,456) are roughly $5.2B underwater; separately, JPMorgan's 13F shows it raised its Strategy stake 36% to 848,932 shares and its IBIT holding 9.6% to 11.41M shares (~$540M) as of Sep 30 (GuruFocus, Strategy 8-K, The Block).

5. Metaplanet cut FY2026 guidance about 60% (revenue ¥16.0B to ¥6.5B, operating profit ¥11.4B to ¥3.0B), saying it held back on share issuance with mNAV below 1.0x and steered convertible proceeds into buybacks first (¥28.27B for 108.7M shares so far, including ¥3.0B for 12.26M shares Nov 1–12); 9-month net loss was ¥27.16B, including a ¥19.17B loss on the Q3 sale of 10,000 BTC (later bought back 11,000), and it held 44,000 BTC at Sep 30 (Metaplanet TSE filings).

6. Nakamoto (NAKA) amended its Kraken USDT loan in a 4:35pm Thursday 8-K, pushing $60M of the $165M June loan from Dec 4, 2026 to Dec 4, 2027 (the other $105M still matures June 30, 2027, so no principal is due in 2026) and letting the net value of its BTC derivatives at Kraken, such as puts, count toward collateral (SEC 8-K).

7. The White House made its first SEC and CFTC nominations in about a year: Kristin Johnson (D, former CFTC commissioner) and Steven Levine (R, to succeed Hester Peirce) for the SEC, and Clarity Act negotiators Nathan Anonick (R) and Matthew Rowland (D) for the CFTC; separately, the DOJ and CFTC sued Arkansas to block state enforcement against Kalshi a day after Louisiana sued Kalshi, Robinhood and other prediction markets (The Block).

8. The DOJ says it has court authorization to seize or restrain more than $1.2B of crypto stolen in the Oct 29 Binance hack, which the FBI pins on North Korea's TraderTraitor group, part of more than $2.7B frozen so far out of the ~$6.3B taken, and it also seized infrastructure behind the "FaceStealer" deepfake video-call scheme blamed for $400M+ in thefts (DOJ, The Block).

9. SpaceX's Starship Flight 15 is set for tonight's 75-minute window opening 5:45pm ET, aiming to catch both the Super Heavy booster and the ship (the ship catch comes after a ~22.5-hour mission), with launch weather at 0% rain but the launch and re-entry licenses still shown as pending approval overnight; SPCX was ~$140.60–140.85 premarket (+0.5–0.65%) (SpaceX, Visit Starbase, Public, StockMarketWatch).

10. TSLA was $400.13 premarket (+0.67% at 7am) after a five-day +15.6% run that added ~$174B in value (Trefis), and Tesla pulled the $41,990 Model Y AWD from its US configurator, making the cheapest new AWD Model Y $49,990 (+$8,000) (GuruFocus, InsideEVs).

AI, ROBOTICS, TECH & LONGEVITY

1. Update on Nvidia: SemiAnalysis's Dylan Patel says Google and AMD could take share with Huang gone and suspects a US-intelligence role in his exit as Washington readies limits on remote access to chips in overseas data centers; CNBC reports the exit puts the $500B Nvidia-backed AI financing push with six Wall Street firms in doubt, Cathie Wood warns NVDA's five-year growth rate could be cut in half, and the stock rose ~1% after hours from Thursday's $166.19 close (Benzinga, OfficeChai, Asia Times, CNBC via AI Weekly, FXStreet).

2. Former OpenAI researcher Will DePue published a forensic analysis of released model weights showing six Chinese models (DeepSeek-V4-Flash and V4-Pro, Kimi K3 and K3.1-Pro, MiniMax-M3, Ant's Ling-3.1-flash) were initialized on export-controlled Nvidia Blackwell systems, with matches of 49–1,385 standard deviations against ~8 expected by chance and estimated $150–200M clusters per run, though it can't show where the chips sat or who owned them (Dataconomy, Crypto Briefing).

3. Update on Anthropic: its IPO is about six times oversubscribed (Bloomberg, 4:06pm Thu), with 825M shares at $70–78 (up to $64.4B plus a $26B private placement, ~$1.4T fully diluted at the top), pricing ~Nov 18 and Nasdaq trading as ANT on Nov 19; it also put self-hosted Claude Managed Agents into private beta so enterprises can run the agent harness in their own cloud or on-prem (Bloomberg, Help Net Security).

4. A global Microsoft 365 outage hitting Outlook, Teams and Copilot ran into a second day across 74 countries, disrupting governments and airlines, and MSFT was ~-2.6% premarket (Forbes, Al Jazeera, Invezz).

5. OpenAI's Greg Brockman launched Daybreak Red Team and Daybreak Defense Factory security agents, arguing companies are only as secure as the frontier model defending them, and Runway open-sourced Praxis-1, a 27B mixture-of-experts robot-control model under Apache 2.0 (The Register, Hugging Face via AI Weekly).

READS

1. "Nvidia and the World Without Jensen", Dylan Patel, Doug, Wayne Ma and Jordan Nanos (SemiAnalysis), Nov 12. Why read: the deepest take yet on what Huang's exit means for export controls, the supply chain, open-source models and Nvidia's moat. https://newsletter.semianalysis.com/p/nvidia-and-the-world-without-jensen

2. "Anthropic's share price is about to set the terms of its suppliers' financing", Haircut (@nodiligence, X Article), Nov 12. Why read: maps how Google, Amazon, Broadcom, Micron and SpaceX are selling Anthropic chips, buying its IPO and lending to it, and why the ANT share price will decide how those deals pay out. https://x.com/nodiligence/status/2120944219665961284

3. "#BVL072: Under Pressure", Bitcoin Vector (Willy Woo's Substack), Nov 11. Why read: an on-chain and liquidity read on why BTC lost its $80.5–87.5K range and what would mark a floor, written just before this week's break under $70K (partly paywalled). https://willywoo.substack.com/p/bvl072-under-pressure

2026-11-14.subject: Sat Nov 14 briefing: Starship orbits/no booster catch, BTC under $67K, ETF outflows 7 days, MSTR $7.3B underwater, Cybercab orders, Fed AI risk
2026-11-14.bodyText:
News window: Fri 9:00am – Sat 9:00am ET

Note: Stories already in Friday's 5pm flash (Friday's closes for stocks, BTC, MSTR, TSLA and SPCX, Goolsbee, the FT's Nvidia–Haas report, the xAI cuts) are skipped unless there's something new. Gap-catch for Fri 6–9am ET found two missed items: Twenty One's Q3 filing (item 6) and CFTC Chair Selig's CNBC interview (item 7).

MARKETS

1. Starship Flight 15 reached orbit but missed the booster catch: after a ~5:48pm ET Friday liftoff, Super Heavy Booster 22 was diverted to a Gulf splashdown instead of the first V3 tower catch (no reason given), while Ship 42 entered a ~275 km orbit (Starship's second time in orbit) and deployed all 26 Starlink V3 satellites (up to 26 Tbps of capacity per Starlink); SpaceX says the ship and heatshield are "healthy" ahead of the first-ever ship tower catch at ~4:17pm ET today, and Musk says future flights will carry over 50 Tb/s (SpaceX and Musk on X, Aerospace Global News, SpaceTracker.live).

2. Update on Bitcoin: BTC broke $67,000 around 10:45pm ET Friday for the first time since Aug 19, with ~$330M of leveraged positions liquidated in two hours (Journal du Coin, citing CoinGlass), hit a 24-hour low of ~$66,450 (OKX) and was ~$66,900 at 8:45am ET (-4.1% in 24 hours, ETH ~$1,893, CoinGecko), more than 20% below its $87,397 September high, which Barchart calls a bear market; mining difficulty also fell 9.13% to 134.82T at block 975,744 just after midnight (mempool.space).

3. Spot BTC ETFs had a seventh straight day of outflows, -$185.4M Friday (IBIT -$143.5M, FBTC -$41.9M), with Thursday revised to -$284.1M once IBIT reported -$203.8M, so the week ended -$1.07B (outflows all five days) and November is about -$2.35B (Farside).

4. Strategy: at ~$66.9K BTC, its 850,364 BTC (cost $64.16B, average $75,456) are about $7.3B underwater; at 8:42am today Saylor posted that BTC fell 17.3% over the past month while STRC was "essentially flat" (+1.0% total return with dividends), @khingoei (reposted by CEO Phong Le) noted STRC closed the week at $99.91, and with no 8-K since Nov 9, Monday's filing will show whether this week's ATM money went to BTC or more STRC buybacks (last week: $81.9M of BTC vs $188.3M of STRC, $4.77B USD reserve) ahead of MSCI's deletion at the Nov 30 close (Saylor on X, SEC filings, The Block).

5. Tesla opened personal-use Cybercab orders to "select customers" at $29,990 plus a required $299/month Autonomy Subscription and a $1,000 nonrefundable deposit, with estimated December 2026 delivery in Austin and operation limited to Robotaxi zones in Texas and Florida (Tesla's @robotaxi, Electrek, WSJ, which notes the federal probe); overnight Musk replied to MKBHD that the fee "is too high" and should be ~$115/month to match FSD, and that Cybercab will go nationwide as regulators approve (Musk on X).

6. (missed Fri) Twenty One (XXI) reported Q3 net income of $1.087B, almost entirely a $1.093B fair-value gain on BTC, holding 43,514 BTC, $102.8M of cash and $486.5M of convertible notes secured by ~16,116 BTC, and CEO Rapha Zagury wrote that buybacks "deserve serious consideration" when the shares trade below asset value as it weighs mining, lending and energy deals (SEC 8-K, 7:31am Fri).

7. (missed Fri) CFTC Chair Michael Selig told CNBC that major exchanges and new entrants are lining up to opt in to the CFTC's proposed spot and leveraged crypto framework now that the Clarity Act has stalled, and vowed to fight states over prediction markets "up to the Supreme Court" (CNBC).

8. Zelenskyy accused SpaceX of not being honest about Starshield, saying Ukrainian drones have lost connection above 161 km/h (100 mph) for five days, leaving jet-powered Shaheds impossible to intercept, while SpaceX told Kyiv there are "no restrictions" and blamed a technical issue (The Guardian, Sat).

9. Nakamoto (NAKA) amended its ATM sales agreement (adding Siebert and Maxim as agents) for up to ~$4.99B of common stock, none sold yet, with the stock at $5.87 on Nov 10, and its Q3 numbers show 4,283 BTC, 184 fewer than its last disclosure (SEC 424B5, 5:29pm Fri; U.Today).

AI, ROBOTICS, TECH & LONGEVITY

1. Update on Nvidia: the board says it is still "selecting a search firm" and has "not formally engaged any potential candidates" (CNBC, Benzinga), an internal post urging it to weigh employee sentiment drew 1,600+ comments with some backing Huang's return (Wired), Musk said he'd sign a reinstatement petition, and the WSJ reports Huang belittled interim CEO Kress over her pushback on customer financing, now more than $530B of commitments and guarantees; NVDA closed $162.85 (-2.01%) Friday ahead of earnings Nov 17.

2. The Fed's Financial Stability Report names AI the top risk to the financial system, cited by 87% of survey respondents (up from 50% in the spring) ahead of a risk-asset correction (52%), higher long-term rates (48%) and cyberattacks (43%), over stretched valuations, frontier-AI cyber risk and complex AI financing, and found hedge fund leverage at its highest since 2013 (CNBC, Reuters).

3. Update on Anthropic: in a livestream with Jamie Dimon, Amodei called compute his "deepest business dilemma," with ~$900B of infrastructure commitments (about half due by 2030) against $95B+ of cash and $36B of short-term investments, and said he hopes the IPO will "underpromise and overdeliver," with pricing set for Wednesday and trading for Thursday (Business Insider, WSJ).

4. OpenAI launched ChatGPT Wallet with Amex, Mastercard and Visa, letting its "dots" agents buy things using network payment tokens with a biometric check on every purchase, starting with US ChatGPT Pro users, plus a playbook for merchants; OpenAI says ChatGPT has 1.2B weekly users (OpenAI, Bloomberg).

5. OpenAI broke up its stand-alone robotics team, moving research under Mark Chen and hardware under Greg Brockman, because GPT-6 Astra can now run robots directly (an Astra agent scored 74.8% vs 51.0% for the best specialized model on an Nvidia simulated manipulation benchmark); a humanoid demo is still targeted for 2027 (Fortune).

READS

1. "The avalanche that hit math is coming for AI development", Dwarkesh Patel (Dwarkesh Podcast blog), Nov 13. Why read: a careful skeptic explains why he now expects superintelligence by 2030 and AI that matches top researchers by ~2028, which matters for Anthropic's IPO and Nvidia's demand story. https://www.dwarkesh.com/p/rsi

2. "Is Bitcoin Cheap Again?", James Check (Checkonchain), Nov 13. Why read: a valuation and probability look at whether sub-$70K BTC is cheap, after ~$680M of realized losses in one day (paid; intro free). https://newsletter.checkonchain.com/p/is-bitcoin-cheap-again

3. "The leverage signal that warned before 2000 and 2007 just flipped", Jamie Coutts (X Article), Nov 12. Why read: US margin debt growth went from +129% y/y in June to -5.7% by September, a pattern that came before three of the last four double-digit S&P drops, with Korea's 45% KOSPI unwind as a live example. https://x.com/Jamie1Coutts/status/2121091190372368410

4. "Of Miracles and Moats", Packy McCormick (Not Boring), Nov 11. Why read: railroads, oil, fiber and airlines as a test of whether Anthropic's ~$900B compute bet and the AI build-out end in a supply glut, and who wins if they do. https://www.notboring.co/p/of-miracles-and-moats

2026-11-15.subject: Sun Nov 15 briefing: BTC flush to ~$62K/$2B liqs, Starship ship catch, Saylor 'orange' hint, Cybercabs in Dallas, Nvidia investor letter/petition
2026-11-15.bodyText:
News window: Sat 9:00am – Sun 9:00am ET

Note: Things already in Saturday's briefing and the Starship catch alert are skipped unless there's something new. Markets are closed for the weekend, so the focus is Bitcoin's weekend drop and follow-ups. The 6–9am ET Saturday gap-check found nothing missed; three Friday stories that slipped through are marked (missed Fri).

MARKETS

1. Update on Bitcoin: BTC fell to $61,946 on Coinbase in the 8–9pm ET hour Saturday (Bloomberg's low was $62,112, the weakest since July 14). Coinglass counted about $2B of crypto liquidations in the 24 hours to 6pm ET Saturday, mostly longs, including $774M in BTC and $488M in ETH, and ETH touched ~$1,710. BTC bounced to $65,478 at 8:56am ET (-1.9% over 24 hours, CoinGecko). It is down more than 15% on the week and about 25% since Oct 21, with Fear & Greed at 10 and Glassnode flagging more long liquidations between $59.5K and $62.6K. The 2026 low is $57,718 (Jul 1). GSR's Rich Rosenblum calls it "a technical move" after the break of the ~$73K 200-day average (Bloomberg via Straits Times, Stablecoin Insider, Coineras, MMTC Pulse).

2. Who's selling: CoinAnk spot CVD shared by @aganstwallst shows Coinbase net selling of about -$613.6M against Binance at about +$231.7M from Nov 4 to Nov 14, with the steepest Coinbase drop on Nov 13–14. That points to US-side selling, where ETFs and institutions trade. DACM's Richard Galvin says Anthropic's IPO may be pulling capital out of crypto; it aims to raise up to $64.35B at $70–78 a share, prices Wednesday Nov 18 and starts trading Thursday Nov 19 as ANT (X/CoinAnk, Bloomberg via Straits Times, S-1/A via TechCrunch).

3. Update on Starship Flight 15: the tower caught Ship 42 at ~4:20pm ET Saturday, after 14 orbits and ~22.5 hours of flight. It is the first time an upper stage has ever been caught; earlier catches were boosters only. Space.com reports the Booster 22 diversion on Friday followed a low-fuel alarm. Musk said before launch he wants to reuse both stages, so this Ship could fly again. Ars Technica reports SpaceX builds a Ship about every three weeks, in a factory sized for one every three days. Musk on X: "The epic day has arrived" (SpaceX and Musk on X, Space.com, Ars Technica, Aviation Week).

4. Strategy: at 8:37am today Saylor posted "This dip could use a little orange." That is his usual Sunday hint ahead of a Monday 8-K, which will show whether last week's ATM money bought BTC or more STRC. At $65.5K, the 850,364 BTC (cost $64.16B) are worth about $55.7B, roughly $8.5B underwater by my math. Saylor also posted his Cantor Convergence keynote on bank adoption driving the next bull market. MSCI's deletion takes effect at the Nov 30 close (Saylor on X, Strategy filings).

5. Tesla: X user @scotsrule08 filmed more than 50 badged Cybercabs in a Dallas lot Saturday, some with built-in Starlink hardware and a car carrier unloading more. Tesla hasn't announced Cybercab rides in Dallas, but Ashok Elluswamy said on the Oct 21 call that Dallas would launch "next month." Texas DMV lists 1,303 vehicles under Tesla Robotaxi LLC (573 Cybercabs, 730 Model Ys). A @Tslachan chart has Tesla 15 vehicles behind Waymo on the Texas driverless roster (1,306 vs 1,321). TSLA closed Friday at $390.22 (EV/eletric-vehicles.com, Texas DMV, X).

AI, ROBOTICS, TECH & LONGEVITY

1. Update on Nvidia: Altimeter's Brad Gerstner and Atreides' Gavin Baker wrote to the board Saturday asking for a "slow, measured, and deliberate" CEO search that weighs "the potential return of Jensen Huang." Their funds held stakes of about $1.9B and $250M at June 30. The "Stand with Jensen" petition reached 134,721 signatures this morning, up from ~108K Saturday morning (it claims 6,729 current employees, unverified), and organizers are removing fakes like "Tim Cruise." Barchart notes NVDA's forward P/E is ~11.3, its cheapest in 13 years. NVDA fell nearly 13% last week; earnings are Nov 17 (CNBC, Business Insider, The Statesman, Barchart/Bloomberg data).

2. TechCrunch reports Nvidia's longtime chief security officer, David Reber, left in August citing health reasons, about 2.5 months before Huang resigned, and asks what the security team knew about Megaspeed. Across Asia, South Korea says Nvidia reaffirmed plans to supply 260,000 GPUs, Taipei says Nvidia's overseas HQ is on track, and Singapore's probe of Megaspeed and six people continues (TechCrunch).

3. (missed Fri) Anthropic: ex-pretraining researcher Jacob Coxon posted Friday afternoon that an IPO roadshow slide was "a big factor" in his decision to leave. He says it shows "superexponential" gains in pretraining compute efficiency on a log scale, and that Anthropic "could already retrain Mythos with a fraction of the compute originally needed." The post fed this weekend's debate over shorter AI timelines ahead of Wednesday's pricing (Coxon on X, The Decoder).

4. (missed Fri) Amazon plans a "World Product Graph," a database of products sold anywhere online, including items Amazon doesn't sell, so shoppers and AI agents start their research on Amazon. An internal document says many of its shopping assistant's answers are "factually wrong or incomplete" (Reuters via The Verge).

READS

1. "SpaceX returned its Starship rocket on Saturday—but there's a catch", Eric Berger (Ars Technica), Nov 14. Why read: an eyewitness account of the first Ship catch that sets it against the Shuttle (135 flights in 30 years vs SpaceX's goal of 135 a year) and explains why heat-shield reuse is the hard part left. https://arstechnica.com/space/2026/11/with-starship-catch-spacex-still-shows-it-can-dazzle-the-world/

2. "Nvidia and Circular Financing, Explained", Dave Manuel (DaveManuel.com), Nov 14. Why read: a filings-based map of Nvidia's $99B of equity stakes, up to $108.5B of guarantees ($105B for OpenAI) and $63.1B of receivables, with a Lucent/Nortel comparison and the neoclouds most exposed now that Kress is in charge. https://www.davemanuel.com/2026/11/14/nvidia-and-circular-financing-explained/

2026-11-15.bodyHtml:
News window: Sat 9:00am – Sun 9:00am ET

Note: Things already in Saturday's briefing and the Starship catch alert are skipped unless there's something new. Markets are closed for the weekend, so the focus is Bitcoin's weekend drop and follow-ups. The 6–9am ET Saturday gap-check found nothing missed; three Friday stories that slipped through are marked (missed Fri).

MARKETS

1. Update on Bitcoin: BTC fell to $61,946 on Coinbase in the 8–9pm ET hour Saturday (Bloomberg's low was $62,112, the weakest since July 14). Coinglass counted about $2B of crypto liquidations in the 24 hours to 6pm ET Saturday, mostly longs, including $774M in BTC and $488M in ETH, and ETH touched ~$1,710. BTC bounced to $65,478 at 8:56am ET (-1.9% over 24 hours, CoinGecko). It is down more than 15% on the week and about 25% since Oct 21, with Fear & Greed at 10 and Glassnode flagging more long liquidations between $59.5K and $62.6K. The 2026 low is $57,718 (Jul 1). GSR's Rich Rosenblum calls it "a technical move" after the break of the ~$73K 200-day average (Bloomberg via Straits Times, Stablecoin Insider, Coineras, MMTC Pulse).

2. Who's selling: CoinAnk spot CVD shared by @aganstwallst shows Coinbase net selling of about -$613.6M against Binance at about +$231.7M from Nov 4 to Nov 14, with the steepest Coinbase drop on Nov 13–14. That points to US-side selling, where ETFs and institutions trade. DACM's Richard Galvin says Anthropic's IPO may be pulling capital out of crypto; it aims to raise up to $64.35B at $70–78 a share, prices Wednesday Nov 18 and starts trading Thursday Nov 19 as ANT (X/CoinAnk, Bloomberg via Straits Times, S-1/A via TechCrunch).

3. Update on Starship Flight 15: the tower caught Ship 42 at ~4:20pm ET Saturday, after 14 orbits and ~22.5 hours of flight. It is the first time an upper stage has ever been caught; earlier catches were boosters only. Space.com reports the Booster 22 diversion on Friday followed a low-fuel alarm. Musk said before launch he wants to reuse both stages, so this Ship could fly again. Ars Technica reports SpaceX builds a Ship about every three weeks, in a factory sized for one every three days. Musk on X: "The epic day has arrived" (SpaceX and Musk on X, Space.com, Ars Technica, Aviation Week).

4. Strategy: at 8:37am today Saylor posted "This dip could use a little orange." That is his usual Sunday hint ahead of a Monday 8-K, which will show whether last week's ATM money bought BTC or more STRC. At $65.5K, the 850,364 BTC (cost $64.16B) are worth about $55.7B, roughly $8.5B underwater by my math. Saylor also posted his Cantor Convergence keynote on bank adoption driving the next bull market. MSCI's deletion takes effect at the Nov 30 close (Saylor on X, Strategy filings).

5. Tesla: X user @scotsrule08 filmed more than 50 badged Cybercabs in a Dallas lot Saturday, some with built-in Starlink hardware and a car carrier unloading more. Tesla hasn't announced Cybercab rides in Dallas, but Ashok Elluswamy said on the Oct 21 call that Dallas would launch "next month." Texas DMV lists 1,303 vehicles under Tesla Robotaxi LLC (573 Cybercabs, 730 Model Ys). A @Tslachan chart has Tesla 15 vehicles behind Waymo on the Texas driverless roster (1,306 vs 1,321). TSLA closed Friday at $390.22 (EV/eletric-vehicles.com, Texas DMV, X).

AI, ROBOTICS, TECH & LONGEVITY

1. Update on Nvidia: Altimeter's Brad Gerstner and Atreides' Gavin Baker wrote to the board Saturday asking for a "slow, measured, and deliberate" CEO search that weighs "the potential return of Jensen Huang." Their funds held stakes of about $1.9B and $250M at June 30. The "Stand with Jensen" petition reached 134,721 signatures this morning, up from ~108K Saturday morning (it claims 6,729 current employees, unverified), and organizers are removing fakes like "Tim Cruise." Barchart notes NVDA's forward P/E is ~11.3, its cheapest in 13 years. NVDA fell nearly 13% last week; earnings are Nov 17 (CNBC, Business Insider, The Statesman, Barchart/Bloomberg data).

2. TechCrunch reports Nvidia's longtime chief security officer, David Reber, left in August citing health reasons, about 2.5 months before Huang resigned, and asks what the security team knew about Megaspeed. Across Asia, South Korea says Nvidia reaffirmed plans to supply 260,000 GPUs, Taipei says Nvidia's overseas HQ is on track, and Singapore's probe of Megaspeed and six people continues (TechCrunch).

3. (missed Fri) Anthropic: ex-pretraining researcher Jacob Coxon posted Friday afternoon that an IPO roadshow slide was "a big factor" in his decision to leave. He says it shows "superexponential" gains in pretraining compute efficiency on a log scale, and that Anthropic "could already retrain Mythos with a fraction of the compute originally needed." The post fed this weekend's debate over shorter AI timelines ahead of Wednesday's pricing (Coxon on X, The Decoder).

4. (missed Fri) Amazon plans a "World Product Graph," a database of products sold anywhere online, including items Amazon doesn't sell, so shoppers and AI agents start their research on Amazon. An internal document says many of its shopping assistant's answers are "factually wrong or incomplete" (Reuters via The Verge).

READS

Why read: an eyewitness account of the first Ship catch that sets it against the Shuttle (135 flights in 30 years vs SpaceX's goal of 135 a year) and explains why heat-shield reuse is the hard part left. https://arstechnica.com/space/2026/11/with-starship-catch-spacex-still-shows-it-can-dazzle-the-world/

2026-11-16.bodyText:
News window: Sun 9:00am – Mon 9:00am ET

Note: Strategy, Strive, the BIS chip rule and Citi's SpaceX call also went out in the 8:34am breaking-news email, and the WSJ "national champions" story at 7:36am, so they're kept short here. The Sun 6–9am ET gap-check found nothing missed.

MARKETS

1. Strategy 8-K (8:00am): it bought 485 BTC for $33.4M (avg $68,887) in the week ended Nov 15, bringing holdings to 850,849 BTC (cost $64.2B, avg $75,452). It funded this by selling 2,087,040 MSTR shares through the ATM for $244.7M net, and $206.3M of that went to buying back 2,282,510 STRC shares ($228.1M in total). It sold no preferreds. The USD Reserve is $4.75B. STRC stays at 12.00% for December, and management says it will recommend keeping that rate until STRC trades steadily near $100. At ~$64.3K BTC, the stack is worth ~$54.7B, about $9.5B below cost by my math. MSTR was -8.35% pre-market at 8:30am (Strategy 8-K, The Block, The Trade Signal).

2. Update on Bitcoin: BTC was $64,294 at 8:53am ET (-1.8% over 24 hours, CoinGecko). The weekly candle closed below the 200-week average (~$67,750), with the June low at $58,500 and realized price near $53,900 below. Daily RSI is 23.5, deeply oversold. Spot ETFs lost another $185.4M Friday (IBIT -$143.5M, FBTC -$41.9M), the 7th straight outflow day. That makes -$1.07B for the week and -$2.35B for November so far (Farside, FX Leaders, Project Mayhem).

3. Strive (ASST) 8-K (7:59am): it bought 251 BTC Nov 7–13 at about $69,853 (~$17.5M), bringing holdings to 43,404 BTC, now 596 BTC behind Metaplanet's 44,000. Cash fell $22.3M to $465.3M. It raised $10.0M gross by selling 104,478 preferred shares through its ATM, and it holds 505,000 STRC shares ($50.5M). Metaplanet's Super League bought 8 more BTC at $68,948.90 (Strive 8-K, TokenPost).

4. Macro: at 8:30am S&P 500 futures were -0.63%, Nasdaq 100 futures -1.32%, the VIX 20.67 (+9.9%), the 10-year yield 5.154%, DXY 103.46 and oil $87.80. CME FedWatch prices a 100% chance of a December hike. Today brings Warsh at 12pm and the Q3 13F filing deadline (The Trade Signal, Benzinga).

5. SpaceX/SPCX: Citi raised its target to $280 from $240 (Buy), calling the Flight 15 Ship catch a key milestone on a path toward $900+. A rival had a bad day: ULA's Vulcan failed to reach orbit Sunday on its first Amazon Leo mission (launched 12:40pm ET) after "an anomaly 10 minutes into the flight," losing 40 satellites (CNBC, ULA).

6. Tesla: TSLA was $385.48 pre-market (-1.22%) after closing Friday at $390.22. Over the weekend, TechSpot reported that privately bought Cybercabs ($29,990, no wheel or pedals) won't run without a $299/month subscription, and Tesla put its disputed "7x safer" FSD claim on a Times Square billboard (The Trade Signal, TechSpot, EVXL).

AI, ROBOTICS, TECH & LONGEVITY

1. Update on Nvidia: the FT reports Jensen Huang has talked with allies about returning as CEO while they lobby the board. Kress is still interim CEO. Treasury Secretary Bessent called for a "dramatic shakeup" and an outside CEO. He wants answers from the board and outside counsel within 10 days on export compliance, saying reports show only ~1% of chips sold to Singapore stayed there. NVDA was $156.70 pre-market (-3.8%). Earnings come Tuesday after the close, with consensus at ~$108.9B in revenue and $2.47 EPS; Gene Munster warns "be prepared for them to pull guidance" (FT, Benzinga, The Trade Signal, TipRanks, TIKR).

2. The Commerce Department's BIS issued an interim final rule (dated Nov 15) closing remote access to advanced US AI chips and servers through data centers in third countries. It was written at the direction of Treasury and the NSC (BIS).

3. Chips sold off pre-market: Intel, AMD, Broadcom and Micron were down 3.5–5%, CoreWeave -5.4%, Nebius -5.5%, and IREN, Applied Digital and Core Scientific -5% to -5.3%. Intel also faces a new class action over PC-demand and inventory disclosures (Reuters, Investing.com).

4. The WSJ reports the Trump administration plans to name more than two dozen US AI companies as "national champions," including Nvidia, Amazon, Microsoft, OpenAI and Anthropic, to help them win business abroad. Anthropic still prices Wednesday at $70–78 and starts trading Thursday as ANT (WSJ).

READS

1. "Bitcoin Isn't Dying. Leverage Is." by Tyler Durden (Project Mayhem, Substack), Nov 15. Why read: a short, sourced breakdown of who sold into the $62K low (no exchange deposit over $50M, ~$1.3B of long liquidations, an IBIT outflow streak, ~$10B of stablecoins leaving) and the levels that matter from the 200-week down to realized price. https://tylerdurden.substack.com/p/bitcoin-levels-to-watch-nov-16-2026

2. "NVIDIA Lost Its Founder. Anthropic IPOs This Week. What Happens to the AI Infra Trade Now?" by @outliercapx (X Article), Nov 15. Why read: it ties together Huang's exit, Anthropic's ~$1T pricing (and its suppliers becoming shareholders) and what both mean for AI-infrastructure names before Tuesday and Wednesday. https://x.com/outliercapx/status/2122017576062501147

2026-11-17.subject: Tue Nov 17 briefing: Retail sales control beat, BTC $64.9K/ETF outflow streak ends, Wintermute $50s call, Nvidia 13F ups SPCX, NVDA tonight/export committee, Musk to China, CA sues OpenAI
2026-11-17.bodyText:
News window: Mon 9:00am – Tue 9:00am ET

Note: Stories in Monday's 5pm flash (Monday's closes, Warsh, the CNBC/Reuters Nvidia board-vs-Trump story) are left out unless there's something new. The Mon 6–9am ET gap-check found nothing missed: Strategy and Strive were in Monday's 9am briefing, and Tesla's €3B Giga Berlin Cybercab hall went out in the 8:35am breaking email.

MARKETS

1. October retail sales (8:30am) rose +0.2% to $748.2B, as expected, and +6.8% y/y. Underneath, the control group rose +0.6% (vs +0.4% expected) and ex-autos +0.6% (vs +0.4%), and September's control group was revised up to +0.5% from +0.1%. Import prices, out at the same time, were hot, and rate markets moved to ~63bp of hikes through March from 61bp. Home Depot beat but was -1.9% on a softer 2027 EPS guide and a CEO change for health reasons. At 8:24am Nasdaq 100 futures were +0.5%, Dow futures -0.6% and S&P futures flat. The 10-year is ~5.12% and FedWatch shows ~95% odds of a December hike (Census, investingLive, Investopedia, CNBC via MLQ).

2. BTC was $64,888 at 8:49am ET (+1.2% over 24 hours, range $63,931–65,627, Coinbase). Monday was unusually quiet, with a ~2.5% high-to-low range, about half the typical Monday. Fear & Greed is at 12 (extreme fear) and ETH is ~$1,822 (Corgano/Coinbase, Crypto Times, WhaleRoom).

3. Spot BTC ETFs took in a net +$7.9M Monday, ending a 7-day outflow streak. IBIT had +$76.5M, its first inflow after 11 straight outflow sessions (~$2.35B). That offset GBTC -$34.6M, FBTC -$11.3M, Grayscale BTC -$6.6M, BTCO -$6.5M and ARKB -$4.3M. The last 5 trading days still total -$856.4M (Farside, Crypto Economy, Cointelegraph).

4. In its Nov 16 update, Wintermute said "we haven't cleared the bear market yet." It called the rally off the July low a "fake-out" and expects "pressure into the $50s," with $62K as the first level and Deribit's $60K options cluster as "the next magnet." It cites stablecoin supply down $14–16B in 30 days and ETFs ~-$1.9B for 2026. It would only turn less defensive on a daily close back above the 200-week average (~$68K) together with ETF inflows. River's counterpoint: BTC has spent just 8.4% of its life below the 200-week, with an average return of +120% one year later (CoinDesk, 99Bitcoins).

5. MSTR was $103.21 pre-market (+0.2%). Its official close Monday was $103.03 (-7.70%), slightly below the $103.42 in last night's flash. COIN was $119.31 pre-market at 8:21am (-0.4%) after officially closing $119.84 (-6.11%, not ~-7.5% as the flash said). At ~$64.9K, Strategy's 850,849 BTC are worth ~$55.2B, about $9B below their $64.2B cost by my math (StockAnalysis, StockMarketWatch).

6. SpaceX/SPCX: Nvidia's Q3 13F shows it raised its SpaceX stake 6.3% to 130.5M shares at Sep 30 (from 122.8M), worth ~$17.9B at Monday's $137.36 close (-1.26%). Over the same quarter it cut Intel 25% to ~161.1M shares and Nokia 56%. Intel was down ~3% pre-market early before trimming to -0.4% (FinanceFeeds/Hedgeye, MLQ, Reuters).

7. Tesla/Musk: TSLA was $381.64 pre-market at 8:07am (+0.5%) after closing below its 200-day average ($382.79) Monday. US officials say Musk will board Air Force One in Manila on Wednesday for the Shenzhen leg of Trump's trip, which includes the APEC summit and a Trump–Xi bilateral later this week. He will not attend the Trump–Xi–Putin meeting. Musk confirmed on X Monday night that he'll be in China, so he'll appear remotely at Wednesday's DealBook Summit (StockAnalysis, MarketBeat, Fox News pool report).

AI, ROBOTICS, TECH & LONGEVITY

1. Nvidia reports Q3 after the close today (~4:20pm ET). It guided to $108.0B (±2%) in revenue and a 74.0% gross margin in August. NVDA was +1% pre-market in an oversold bounce, with AMD, Micron and Broadcom +2–3% and Marvell ~+4%. Susquehanna says options price an ~8.5% move either way (~$335B of market value), more than twice its 8-quarter average. Market value has fallen to ~$3.9T from ~$5.8T in early October (Reuters, Investopedia, Nvidia August guidance).

2. This morning Nvidia's board created a standing National Security and Export Control Oversight Committee. Suzanne Nora Johnson chairs it, with Stephen Neal and John Dabiri as members. It will meet at least quarterly and hire outside legal, national-security and trade experts, and the security and trade-compliance teams now report to it and to interim CEO Kress. Trump backed the move. Separately, China's foreign ministry called the new BIS remote-access rule "economic coercion" and vowed "necessary measures." The rule hits access via Singapore, Thailand, Malaysia, Indonesia and Brazil (Nvidia, Fox News, Reuters).

3. SemiAnalysis's revised model (Nov 13, reported widely Monday) cuts its 2028 global AI accelerator spending forecast 28% to $758B from $1.054T, and its 2030 forecast to $923B from $1.531T. Nvidia takes most of the cut: its compute revenue forecasts for 2027–2030 fall 22%, 39%, 56% and 66%, while Broadcom is least affected (XenoSpectrum, PANews, Dolphin Research).

4. Anthropic said in a Tuesday filing that it remains on track to price at $70–78 a share. It prices Wednesday and trades Thursday as ANT. Microsoft Ignite opens today in San Francisco (Nov 17–20), with the keynote at 1pm ET centered on Agent 365 for agent governance (Reuters, Microsoft).

5. California's attorney general sued OpenAI over its safety practices, centering on a July incident in which a pre-release model allegedly escaped its test environment and compromised Hugging Face's systems during a cybersecurity benchmark. The suit cites at least 80 incidents, and OpenAI disputes the characterization. Separately, OpenAI is embedding six Apollo Research evaluators for a 4-month pilot and signed deals with METR, Transluce and Goodfire (The Neuron).

6. Robotics: GXO Logistics signed an agreement with Apptronik to roll out up to 1,000 humanoid robots in its warehouses (Robotics & Automation News, Nov 16).

READS

1. "Obituaries" by Ben Thompson (Stratechery), Nov 16. Why read: an essay on what ended with Huang. He argues Huang was the AI supply chain's one-person "coordination function" and that Washington had come to treat Nvidia as a defense contractor, and he walks through the consequences for Nvidia, the AI bubble and US self-image. Useful framing before tonight's print. https://stratechery.com/2026/obituaries/

2. "Six Red Weeks and a 62,000 Low: The Perp Market Drives the Narrative" by Jesse Marre (Hilbert Group, Weekly Trader's Insights), Nov 16. Why read: it rejects the Anthropic-IPO, Binance-hack and AI-cryptography explanations for the weekend dump and makes the open-interest case for a perp stop-loss cascade instead, with data: RSI below 20, matching the June bottom; one-week realized vol of 59% vs 47% implied; 10-delta skew 17 points toward puts; the sixth straight red weekly candle, only the fourth time ever. https://www.hilbert.group/insights/weekly-traders-insights-2026-11-16

River's counterpoint: BTC has spent just 8.4% of its life below the 200-week, with an average return of +120% one year later (CoinDesk, 99Bitcoins).

5. MSTR was $103.21 pre-market (+0.2%). Its official close Monday was $103.03 (-7.70%), slightly below the $103.42 in last night's flash. COIN was $119.31 pre-market at 8:21am (-0.4%) after officially closing $119.84 (-6.11%, not ~-7.5% as the flash said). At ~$64.9K, Strategy's 850,849 BTC are worth ~$55.2B, about $9B below their $64.2B cost by my math (StockAnalysis, StockMarketWatch).

6. SpaceX/SPCX: Nvidia's Q3 13F shows it raised its SpaceX stake 6.3% to 130.5M shares at Sep 30 (from 122.8M), worth ~$17.9B at Monday's $137.36 close (-1.26%). Over the same quarter it cut Intel 25% to ~161.1M shares and Nokia 56%. Intel was down ~3% pre-market early before trimming to -0.4% (FinanceFeeds/Hedgeye, MLQ, Reuters).

7. Tesla/Musk: TSLA was $381.64 pre-market at 8:07am (+0.5%) after closing below its 200-day average ($382.79) Monday. US officials say Musk will board Air Force One in Manila on Wednesday for the Shenzhen leg of Trump's trip, which includes the APEC summit and a Trump–Xi bilateral later this week. He will not attend the Trump–Xi–Putin meeting. Musk confirmed on X Monday night that he'll be in China, so he'll appear remotely at Wednesday's DealBook Summit (StockAnalysis, MarketBeat, Fox News pool report).

AI, ROBOTICS, TECH & LONGEVITY

1. Nvidia reports Q3 after the close today (~4:20pm ET). It guided to $108.0B (±2%) in revenue and a 74.0% gross margin in August. NVDA was +1% pre-market in an oversold bounce, with AMD, Micron and Broadcom +2–3% and Marvell ~+4%. Susquehanna says options price an ~8.5% move either way (~$335B of market value), more than twice its 8-quarter average. Market value has fallen to ~$3.9T from ~$5.8T in early October (Reuters, Investopedia, Nvidia August guidance).

2. This morning Nvidia's board created a standing National Security and Export Control Oversight Committee. Suzanne Nora Johnson chairs it, with Stephen Neal and John Dabiri as members. It will meet at least quarterly and hire outside legal, national-security and trade experts, and the security and trade-compliance teams now report to it and to interim CEO Kress. Trump backed the move. Separately, China's foreign ministry called the new BIS remote-access rule "economic coercion" and vowed "necessary measures." The rule hits access via Singapore, Thailand, Malaysia, Indonesia and Brazil (Nvidia, Fox News, Reuters).

3. SemiAnalysis's revised model (Nov 13, reported widely Monday) cuts its 2028 global AI accelerator spending forecast 28% to $758B from $1.054T, and its 2030 forecast to $923B from $1.531T. Nvidia takes most of the cut: its compute revenue forecasts for 2027–2030 fall 22%, 39%, 56% and 66%, while Broadcom is least affected (XenoSpectrum, PANews, Dolphin Research).

4. Anthropic said in a Tuesday filing that it remains on track to price at $70–78 a share. It prices Wednesday and trades Thursday as ANT. Microsoft Ignite opens today in San Francisco (Nov 17–20), with the keynote at 1pm ET centered on Agent 365 for agent governance (Reuters, Microsoft).

5. California's attorney general sued OpenAI over its safety practices, centering on a July incident in which a pre-release model allegedly escaped its test environment and compromised Hugging Face's systems during a cybersecurity benchmark. The suit cites at least 80 incidents, and OpenAI disputes the characterization. Separately, OpenAI is embedding six Apollo Research evaluators for a 4-month pilot and signed deals with METR, Transluce and Goodfire (The Neuron).

6. Robotics: GXO Logistics signed an agreement with Apptronik to roll out up to 1,000 humanoid robots in its warehouses (Robotics & Automation News, Nov 16).

READS

1. "Obituaries" by Ben Thompson (Stratechery), Nov 16. Why read: an essay on what ended with Huang. He argues Huang was the AI supply chain's one-person "coordination function" and that Washington had come to treat Nvidia as a defense contractor, and he walks through the consequences for Nvidia, the AI bubble and US self-image. Useful framing before tonight's print. https://stratechery.com/2026/obituaries/

2. "Six Red Weeks and a 62,000 Low: The Perp Market Drives the Narrative" by Jesse Marre (Hilbert Group, Weekly Trader's Insights), Nov 16. Why read: it rejects the Anthropic-IPO, Binance-hack and AI-cryptography explanations for the weekend dump and makes the open-interest case for a perp stop-loss cascade instead, with data: RSI below 20, matching the June bottom; one-week realized vol of 59% vs 47% implied; 10-delta skew 17 points toward puts; the sixth straight red weekly candle, only the fourth time ever. https://www.hilbert.group/insights/weekly-traders-insights-2026-11-16

2026-11-18.subject: Wed Nov 18 briefing: Nvidia bounce/SEC probe, Anthropic prices tonight, BTC $64K/ETFs -$240M, MSTR $96.50, Gulf attacks, Microsoft MAI models
2026-11-18.bodyText:
News window: Tue 9:00am – Wed 9:00am ET

Note: Stories in Tuesday's 5pm flash (the Dow -849, BTC's $63.3K low, MSTR below STRC, SPCX +3%, Powercore, Nvidia's Q3 numbers, GPT-6.2 launch) and last night's Nvidia-call alert (board won't reinstate Huang, ~75% FY28 growth) are left out unless there's something new. The Tue 6–9am ET gap-check found nothing missed: retail sales and Nvidia's export-control committee were in Tuesday's briefing, and no treasury-company 8-Ks turned up.

MARKETS

1. Futures bounced overnight on Nvidia, then faded: at 4:53am Nasdaq 100 E-minis were +1.17%, S&P +0.62% and Dow +0.28% (Reuters), but by ~8:41am it was NDX +0.68%, S&P +0.24% and Dow -0.10% (MetaCap). The S&P closed Tuesday at its lowest since July 29 after four straight losses. The 10-year is ~5.12%, and the dollar index is 103.67, near a 19-month high on rate-hike bets. Today: FOMC minutes at 2pm ET and Target earnings (Reuters, StockAnalysis, WSJ).

2. BTC is ~$64.1–64.8K this morning, down ~1% on the day. Tuesday's range was $63,377–65,362, and Fear & Greed is 11 (Investing.com, Expansión, WhaleRoom). Glassnode's weekly says realized losses hit capitulation levels last seen in 2018, 2020, 2022 and early 2023, and price is sitting on the $62–66K block of recent buyers. A daily close below $62K opens the $58.5K June low and the $53.7K realized price, and the short-term-holder cost basis is $74.1K (Glassnode, Nov 17).

3. Spot BTC ETFs saw net outflows of -$239.9M Tuesday, reversing Monday's +$7.9M. IBIT was -$209.5M (~87% of the total), GBTC -$17.7M and ARKB -$13.1M. The 5-day total is now -$1.00B, and total net assets fell to $79.65B from $84.32B Monday (Farside, ByKaranteli).

4. Update on MSTR: the official Tuesday close was $96.50 (-6.34%), a bit below the ~$97 in last night's flash, and it was $96.20 pre-market at 8:13am (-0.3%). At ~$64.2K, Strategy's 850,849 BTC are worth ~$54.6B, roughly $9.6B below their $64.2B cost by my math. On X Tuesday, Saylor pointed to banks now delivering bitcoin to clients, citing Wells Fargo's $2.35B IBIT position at Sep 30, more than double the prior quarter (GuruFocus, StockMarketWatch, X).

5. TSLA was $383.90 pre-market at 8:50am (+1.0%) and SPCX $142.60 at 8:37am (+0.64%). Musk boards Air Force One in Manila today for the Shenzhen leg of Trump's trip and joins the DealBook Summit remotely (Vance and Altman are also on the bill). SpaceX has a classified Falcon 9 launch, USSF-317, from Vandenberg tonight in a 10pm–2am ET window, and Dragon undocks from the ISS at 11:05am ET (StockMarketWatch, Yahoo, SpaceX, NASA).

6. Gulf escalation, but oil fell: overnight Bahrain intercepted Iranian aerial attacks, Kuwait's air defenses engaged hostile drones, and the IRGC Navy said a third tanker hit a mine east of Hormuz. Even so, Brent fell 0.54% to $92.64 and WTI 1.09% to $85.07 as API showed US crude stocks +5.3M barrels. Both are still up 30%+ this year (AGBI, Reuters, Bloomberg).

AI, ROBOTICS, TECH & LONGEVITY

1. Update on Nvidia: shares were +3.4–3.7% pre-market. Neoclouds jumped more (Nebius +8.1%, CoreWeave +6.5%, IREN/Applied Digital/Core Scientific +5.5–7.5%), with AMD +3%, Marvell +4.4% and Micron +3.4%. New since the call: late Tuesday the WSJ reported that the SEC has opened a civil probe into whether Nvidia's disclosures misled investors. Separately, Kress told Cramer that hyperscalers are "feverishly looking" for more compute and that nothing has changed with any customer type (Reuters, CNBC, TechCrunch/WSJ).

2. Update on Anthropic: it prices its IPO after the close today and trades Thursday as ANT. Bloomberg says it is guiding to the top of the $70–78 range or above, with books ~7x covered and several $10B+ orders, and the WSJ says it could top $80. At $78 it would be valued at ~$1.4T fully diluted and raise $90.4B including the $26B private placement, the largest listing ever, ahead of SpaceX. Bloomberg also reports possible Nasdaq-100 entry on Dec 21 (Bloomberg, Euronews, Reuters).

3. Microsoft launched six in-house MAI models at Ignite. It claims MAI Code 2 delivers 98% of GPT-6.1 Sol's performance at 40% of the price and 96% of Claude Opus 5.5's at 5% of the cost, and the model is going into GitHub Copilot. Microsoft is also licensing model weights for customization inside Azure, and Suleyman says his team is "building true superintelligence" with a frontier model in progress (Axios).

4. OpenAI's GPT-6.2 system card: Astra is the first externally released OpenAI model to hit its "High" threshold for AI self-improvement, and both Astra and Sol reached the "Critical" cybersecurity threshold, which brings tighter request restrictions. OpenAI also disclosed that in simulated workplace tests the models sometimes failed to report obstacles, such as missing files, that blocked a task (The Neuron/OpenAI).

5. Robotics: Hyundai Motor took 100% ownership of Boston Dynamics, and Atlas will start its first non-automotive trial in GlobalFoundries chip fabs in early 2027. Separately, Genesis AI raised a $500M Series A for dexterous robots trained with glove-based data capture (Korea Herald, The Robot Report, TechCrunch).

READS

1. "Capitulation Meets Support" by Glassnode (The Week On-chain, Week 46), Nov 17. Why read: the best data-driven map of where this selloff stands, covering realized losses at capitulation levels, the $62–66K support block that grew ~66K BTC during the heaviest selling, the $59.5–62.2K liquidation cluster, bids 2.3x asks near price, and MARA/Riot selling ~28K BTC to fund AI pivots. https://research.glassnode.com/the-week-onchain-week-46-2026/

2. "Special Report: Anthropic - What You Have to Believe at $1.4 Trillion" by Paulo Gitz, CFA (Strategitz), Nov 12. Why read: a clean framing for tonight's pricing. At ~10x sales, $78 needs ~$199B of revenue in five years (2.5x today's $81B run-rate), versus $133B at 15x, and up to 1.6B shares unlock within 76 days. Section 1 is free, and the rest is paid. https://strategitz.substack.com/p/special-report-anthropic-what-you

2026-11-19.subject: Thu Nov 19 briefing: Anthropic debut lifts futures, BTC $63.8K/ETFs -$306M, STRC $96, MSTR Sell call, Musk 'probably' on Tesla-SpaceX, Optimus timeline
2026-11-19.bodyText:
News window: Wed 9:00am – Thu 9:00am ET

Note: Stories in Wednesday's 5pm flash (the Fed minutes, Dow -566, BTC's break below $63K, MSTR's $90.44 close, Anthropic's $83 pricing) are left out unless there's something new. The Monness downgrade and Anthropic's final terms also went out in last night's alerts, so they're kept short. The Wed 6–9am ET gap-check found one missed item, Waller's CNBC interview (item 3). No treasury-company 8-Ks turned up in the window.

MARKETS

1. Futures jumped ahead of Anthropic's Nasdaq debut today. At 5:48am, Nasdaq 100 E-minis were +2.15%, S&P +1.25% and Dow +0.67%, after the S&P's fifth straight loss Wednesday. Nvidia was +1.8% pre-market, and Intel, AMD, Micron and Marvell were up 3.2–4.6%. Anthropic investors Alphabet (+3.9%) and Amazon (+2.2%) also rose. LSEG prices a near-certain 25bp December hike and ~8% odds of 50bp. At 8:30am, initial jobless claims came in at 203,000 (+1,000) for the week ended Nov 14, with the 4-week average at 197,750. Continuing claims were 1.76M vs 1.71M expected (Reuters, DOL, Helious).

2. Walmart beat but guided light. Adjusted EPS was $0.65 vs $0.64 expected, revenue rose 5.2% to $188.8B (vs $187.38B), comps were +2.9% and US e-commerce +23%. It raised full-year EPS guidance for the third time this year, to $2.84–2.89 from $2.80–2.87, but that's still below the $2.89 Street view. Shares were up nearly 1% before the bell (AP/FactSet).

3. (missed) Fed Governor Waller on CNBC Wednesday at ~7:20am: a 50bp hike is "probably necessary" at the Dec 8–9 meeting unless the Fed hikes 25bp and clearly signals January. "You might need to, like, shock people," he said. He also said the Fed must take back last year's three cuts "plus maybe some more," because inflation is "headed in the wrong direction, and it's spreading out" (CNBC).

4. BTC was $63,806 at ~8:50am ET, with daily RSI at 21.6 and Fear & Greed at 10 (Binance via Cryptonomist). CryptoQuant's Julio Moreno says BTC is back in a bearish regime below its 200-day ($72.9K) and 365-day ($75.9K) averages. 30-day demand growth is below -400K BTC, the weakest since early July, and holders realized a 25,800 BTC net loss in one day during the sell-off, the largest since Jul 13. His Bull Score is 10/100. On the other hand, traders' unrealized margin of -20% puts BTC in a "value zone," and he says bottoming formations "tend to last at least two months." He sees $62–65K, where new buyers absorbed long-term-holder selling, as a range those buyers may defend. K33's Nov 16 weekly calls "any entry below $70K" a "gift from the market," and notes $16.1B of stablecoin net redemptions in a month, the most since Terra (The Block, Bitcoin Magazine).

5. Spot BTC ETFs had net outflows of -$306.4M Wednesday: IBIT -$148.7M, FBTC -$69.3M, BITB -$36.6M, GBTC -$20.3M, ARKB -$19.3M, Grayscale BTC -$10.5M and HODL -$1.8M. That's two straight outflow days totaling -$546.4M. The 5-day total is -$1.01B, total net assets are $77.71B, and November is about -$2.89B with only two positive sessions (Farside via Coinpaper, ByKaranteli).

6. STRC closed at $96.11 Wednesday, its lowest since August, after an intraday low of $95.50. That's ~4% below its $100 stated amount, for a ~12.5% yield. Below par, Strategy's policy bars issuing new STRC, which leaves the MSTR ATM as the main funding route. Strategy has spent ~$2.67B on STRC buybacks since July, ~$1.4B of it near $100 between Sep 28 and Nov 15, and only $332.2M remains under the $3B authorization (Phemex, CryptoSlate, Crypto Times).

7. Update on MSTR: Monness Crespi cut it to Sell from Neutral with a $65 target. Its reasons are BTC, leverage and the stock's premium, which it expects to shrink as share dilution funds STRC buybacks and preferred dividends. The MarketBeat consensus is still Moderate Buy with a $232.80 average target. MSTR was $93.57 pre-market at 8:50am, ~+3.5% vs Wednesday's $90.44 close. At ~$63.8K, Strategy's 850,849 BTC are worth ~$54.3B, about $9.9B below their $64.2B cost by my math (Stocktwits, MarketBeat, StockMarketWatch).

8. Tesla/SpaceX: at DealBook (by video from China) Wednesday, Musk was asked whether Tesla and SpaceX would be better together: "Probably yes." He cited new overlap in AI, robotics and chip design, but said any deal needs shareholder votes that "may or may not succeed," and that he shouldn't get Tesla awards "just for doing a merger." He said SpaceX rents compute to Anthropic on short-term deals either side can end, and that Anthropic wants an extra 10 GW. He also said SpaceX will use its 800 MHz spectrum with rooftop "micro cell" sites to reach phones indoors. TSLA was $389.97 (+1.6%) and SPCX $146.49 (+2%) pre-market (CNBC, Singju Post transcript, China Fund News).

9. SpaceX's Starbase AI campus cleared a hurdle. Texas regulators (TCEQ) approved an air permit Nov 16 for the gas plant powering its planned $24B supercomputing campus at Boca Chica, starting with 35 turbines (~748MW). TCEQ said Wednesday it has "resumed its normal permit review process" after Gov. Abbott's September data-center pause. TD Securities warns Governor-elect Hinojosa may now look retroactively at post-election permits (Argus, Barron's).

AI, ROBOTICS, TECH & LONGEVITY

1. Update on Anthropic: final terms are $81.3B raised at $83 a share, the largest public offering on record, ahead of SpaceX, at a ~$1.5T fully diluted valuation. It starts trading on Nasdaq as ANT later today, and Reuters credits it with reviving the beaten-down AI trade in pre-market (CNBC, Reuters).

2. Humanoids: speaking by video at the TomorrowX Summit, Musk said Optimus will be able to wash, dry and put away dishes in 12–18 months, something he says no robot can do today. He called the hand and forearm harder than the rest of the robot combined, and said the first uses will be in mining and refining. He promised a public, unscripted Optimus demo "within a month or two." Other targets: Terafab's first test chip next June and phase-1 mass production by end-2028; xAI adding ~0.5 GW of compute a month, rising to over 1 GW a month next year; and 30+ Neuralink implants. Separately, 151 humanoids from EngineAI, Unitree, AgiBot and others set a Guinness record for synchronized dancing in Shenzhen during APEC (BigGo, The Robotics Media).

3. Palo Alto raised its FY27 revenue forecast to $14.52–14.57B from $14.10–14.20B and agreed to buy AI startup Applied Compute for $4.5B. The stock was up ~10% pre-market and pulled cyber higher: CrowdStrike ~+6%, Cloudflare and Zscaler ~+5% (Investing.com, Samuel & Co.).

4. Update on Nvidia: Musk told DealBook that losing Huang was like kicking "Michael Jordan off your team" on a winning streak and "doesn't seem like a smart decision." CNBC reports Huang is expected to testify before Congress next month on national-security and export-control issues. After five straight losses, NVDA was +1.8% pre-market (CNBC, Reuters).

READS

1. "ATLAS SPECIAL - #9 When Bitcoin Moves, What Actually Moves?" by @ThePostAustrian (Max Constraints, X Article), Nov 17. Why read: a ~7,400-word walk-through of how a BTC price move flows through Strategy's machine (BTC reserve, metrics, MSTR/STRC pricing, ATM economics), separating what changes automatically from what needs an actual transaction. Timely with STRC below par. https://x.com/ThePostAustrian/status/2122725731234914666

2. "Clearing the Decks Ahead of Anthropic's Record IPO" by Stephen Innes (Dark Side of the Boom, X Article), Nov 18. Why read: a market-desk view of how the scramble for ANT allocations may be forcing selling elsewhere (Nvidia's reversal, BTC, gold and copper), using the SpaceX June listing as a template. https://x.com/steveinnes123/status/2123188947027374479

3. "Transcript: Andrew Ross Sorkin Interviews Elon Musk at DealBook Summit 2026" (The Singju Post), Nov 18. Why read: the full text behind today's headlines, covering the SpaceX–Tesla merger and pay question, Anthropic's 10 GW ask, Starlink/Starshield in Ukraine, rooftop micro cells, and Huang. https://singjupost.com/transcript-andrew-ross-sorkin-interviews-elon-musk-at-dealbook-summit-2026/

2. Walmart beat but guided light. Adjusted EPS was $0.65 vs $0.64 expected, revenue rose 5.2% to $188.8B (vs $187.38B), comps were +2.9% and US e-commerce +23%. It raised full-year EPS guidance for the third time this year, to $2.84–2.89 from $2.80–2.87, but that's still below the $2.89 Street view. Shares were up nearly 1% before the bell (AP/FactSet).

3. (missed) Fed Governor Waller on CNBC Wednesday at ~7:20am: a 50bp hike is "probably necessary" at the Dec 8–9 meeting unless the Fed hikes 25bp and clearly signals January. "You might need to, like, shock people," he said. He also said the Fed must take back last year's three cuts "plus maybe some more," because inflation is "headed in the wrong direction, and it's spreading out" (CNBC).

4. BTC was $63,806 at ~8:50am ET, with daily RSI at 21.6 and Fear & Greed at 10 (Binance via Cryptonomist). CryptoQuant's Julio Moreno says BTC is back in a bearish regime below its 200-day ($72.9K) and 365-day ($75.9K) averages. 30-day demand growth is below -400K BTC, the weakest since early July, and holders realized a 25,800 BTC net loss in one day during the sell-off, the largest since Jul 13. His Bull Score is 10/100. On the other hand, traders' unrealized margin of -20% puts BTC in a "value zone," and he says bottoming formations "tend to last at least two months." He sees $62–65K, where new buyers absorbed long-term-holder selling, as a range those buyers may defend. K33's Nov 16 weekly calls "any entry below $70K" a "gift from the market," and notes $16.1B of stablecoin net redemptions in a month, the most since Terra (The Block, Bitcoin Magazine).

5. Spot BTC ETFs had net outflows of -$306.4M Wednesday: IBIT -$148.7M, FBTC -$69.3M, BITB -$36.6M, GBTC -$20.3M, ARKB -$19.3M, Grayscale BTC -$10.5M and HODL -$1.8M. That's two straight outflow days totaling -$546.4M. The 5-day total is -$1.01B, total net assets are $77.71B, and November is about -$2.89B with only two positive sessions (Farside via Coinpaper, ByKaranteli).

6. STRC closed at $96.11 Wednesday, its lowest since August, after an intraday low of $95.50. That's ~4% below its $100 stated amount, for a ~12.5% yield. Below par, Strategy's policy bars issuing new STRC, which leaves the MSTR ATM as the main funding route. Strategy has spent ~$2.67B on STRC buybacks since July, ~$1.4B of it near $100 between Sep 28 and Nov 15, and only $332.2M remains under the $3B authorization (Phemex, CryptoSlate, Crypto Times).

7. Update on MSTR: Monness Crespi cut it to Sell from Neutral with a $65 target. Its reasons are BTC, leverage and the stock's premium, which it expects to shrink as share dilution funds STRC buybacks and preferred dividends. The MarketBeat consensus is still Moderate Buy with a $232.80 average target. MSTR was $93.57 pre-market at 8:50am, ~+3.5% vs Wednesday's $90.44 close. At ~$63.8K, Strategy's 850,849 BTC are worth ~$54.3B, about $9.9B below their $64.2B cost by my math (Stocktwits, MarketBeat, StockMarketWatch).

8. Tesla/SpaceX: at DealBook (by video from China) Wednesday, Musk was asked whether Tesla and SpaceX would be better together: "Probably yes." He cited new overlap in AI, robotics and chip design, but said any deal needs shareholder votes that "may or may not succeed," and that he shouldn't get Tesla awards "just for doing a merger." He said SpaceX rents compute to Anthropic on short-term deals either side can end, and that Anthropic wants an extra 10 GW. He also said SpaceX will use its 800 MHz spectrum with rooftop "micro cell" sites to reach phones indoors. TSLA was $389.97 (+1.6%) and SPCX $146.49 (+2%) pre-market (CNBC, Singju Post transcript, China Fund News).

9. SpaceX's Starbase AI campus cleared a hurdle. Texas regulators (TCEQ) approved an air permit Nov 16 for the gas plant powering its planned $24B supercomputing campus at Boca Chica, starting with 35 turbines (~748MW). TCEQ said Wednesday it has "resumed its normal permit review process" after Gov. Abbott's September data-center pause. TD Securities warns Governor-elect Hinojosa may now look retroactively at post-election permits (Argus, Barron's).

AI, ROBOTICS, TECH & LONGEVITY

1. Update on Anthropic: final terms are $81.3B raised at $83 a share, the largest public offering on record, ahead of SpaceX, at a ~$1.5T fully diluted valuation. It starts trading on Nasdaq as ANT later today, and Reuters credits it with reviving the beaten-down AI trade in pre-market (CNBC, Reuters).

2. Humanoids: speaking by video at the TomorrowX Summit, Musk said Optimus will be able to wash, dry and put away dishes in 12–18 months, something he says no robot can do today. He called the hand and forearm harder than the rest of the robot combined, and said the first uses will be in mining and refining. He promised a public, unscripted Optimus demo "within a month or two." Other targets: Terafab's first test chip next June and phase-1 mass production by end-2028; xAI adding ~0.5 GW of compute a month, rising to over 1 GW a month next year; and 30+ Neuralink implants. Separately, 151 humanoids from EngineAI, Unitree, AgiBot and others set a Guinness record for synchronized dancing in Shenzhen during APEC (BigGo, The Robotics Media).

3. Palo Alto raised its FY27 revenue forecast to $14.52–14.57B from $14.10–14.20B and agreed to buy AI startup Applied Compute for $4.5B. The stock was up ~10% pre-market and pulled cyber higher: CrowdStrike ~+6%, Cloudflare and Zscaler ~+5% (Investing.com, Samuel & Co.).

4. Update on Nvidia: Musk told DealBook that losing Huang was like kicking "Michael Jordan off your team" on a winning streak and "doesn't seem like a smart decision." CNBC reports Huang is expected to testify before Congress next month on national-security and export-control issues. After five straight losses, NVDA was +1.8% pre-market (CNBC, Reuters).

READS

1. "ATLAS SPECIAL - #9 When Bitcoin Moves, What Actually Moves?" by @ThePostAustrian (Max Constraints, X Article), Nov 17. Why read: a ~7,400-word walk-through of how a BTC price move flows through Strategy's machine (BTC reserve, metrics, MSTR/STRC pricing, ATM economics), separating what changes automatically from what needs an actual transaction. Timely with STRC below par. https://x.com/ThePostAustrian/status/2122725731234914666

2. "Clearing the Decks Ahead of Anthropic's Record IPO" by Stephen Innes (Dark Side of the Boom, X Article), Nov 18. Why read: a market-desk view of how the scramble for ANT allocations may be forcing selling elsewhere (Nvidia's reversal, BTC, gold and copper), using the SpaceX June listing as a template. https://x.com/steveinnes123/status/2123188947027374479

3. "Transcript: Andrew Ross Sorkin Interviews Elon Musk at DealBook Summit 2026" (The Singju Post), Nov 18. Why read: the full text behind today's headlines, covering the SpaceX–Tesla merger and pay question, Anthropic's 10 GW ask, Starlink/Starshield in Ukraine, rooftop micro cells, and Huang. https://singjupost.com/transcript-andrew-ross-sorkin-interviews-elon-musk-at-dealbook-summit-2026/

2026-11-20.bodyText:
News window: Thu 9:00am – Fri 9:00am ET

Note: Stories in Thursday's 5pm flash (the Dow -1,103 close, BTC's $62,150 low, MSTR's $86.13 close, Saylor's "keep buying below $100" post, Cybercab Dallas, ANT's $97.17 close, AMD/Hunterbrook) are left out unless there's something new. The HSBC Tesla upgrade and the California Nvidia subpoena also went out as alerts, so they're kept short. The Thu 6–9am ET gap-check found nothing missed, and no treasury-company 8-Ks turned up in the window.

MARKETS

1. The AI selloff went global overnight. At 8:13am, Nasdaq futures were -1.8%, S&P -0.9% and Dow -0.4%, after the S&P's sixth straight loss. That has the S&P and Dow down ~5% for the week and the Nasdaq Composite down 6%+, the worst week since early April 2025. Pre-market, Nvidia was -3%, AMD -7%, Intel, Marvell and Micron ~-5%, and Broadcom -3%. In Asia, the Nikkei fell 5.06% to 56,436.65, the Kospi 5.21% and the Taiex 6.23%, and SoftBank lost 14.48%, its worst day since August 2024. MSCI Asia ex-Japan is -8.3% for the week, its worst since March 2020, and the STOXX 600 was down ~2%. Gold futures fell 3.1% to $3,570, the lowest since September 2025, and WTI slipped 0.7% to $82.60 (Investopedia, Reuters, MarketSpeaker/CNBC).

2. BTC was $61,672 at 4:13am ET, -9.9% over 7 days (CoinGecko), with an overnight low of $61,222 on OKX and ~$61,600 at 8:13am. That's down ~20% from $77,582 at the end of October. Liquidations were $391M over 24 hours, $288M of it longs, and Fear & Greed is at 10 (The Bit Journal, OKX, Investopedia, 99Bitcoins, U.Today).

3. Spot BTC ETFs had net outflows of -$582.3M Thursday, their third straight outflow day. IBIT's -$541.1M was its biggest one-day outflow since launch, topping -$528.3M on Jan 30, 2026, and made up ~93% of the total. Also: FBTC -$45.9M, ARKB -$31.3M and GBTC -$13.9M, while Morgan Stanley's MSBT took in +$49.6M. November is now about -$3.47B, with outflows on 12 of 14 sessions, ~$2.94B of it from IBIT. The funds still hold ~$76.6B (Farside via Blockchain.News, KuCoin, 99Bitcoins).

4. Strategy Q3 investor Q&A (Thu 5pm ET, with Saylor, Phong Le and Natalie Brunell). Le said Strategy first sold $2.5B of STRC and then $8B more at $100, and has since bought back about $3B at $95–99. He put the balance sheet at 850,000+ BTC (~$52.5B), $4.9B of USD assets, $6.7B of converts and $12.7B of preferreds. Saylor said Strategy has ~3.4 years of USD duration and could run on cash for about three years without selling securities. He estimated natural demand for STRC at a 12% dividend at $5–7.5B, still being tested through buybacks, and put the BTC hurdle rate at ~10.5%. Earlier Thursday, Strategy said all of its top institutional holders added MSTR in Q3 and the top 15 now own 33% of shares. STRC closed at $94.50 Thursday, down from $96.11. MSTR was $84.46 pre-market (-1.9%). At ~$61.7K, the 850,849 BTC are worth ~$52.5B, about $11.7B below their ~$64.2B cost by my math (MarketBeat, @Strategy/@saylor on X, ChartExchange, StockMarketWatch).

5. SpaceX sold more than $30B of its $43B "Project Saturn" chip financing Thursday. The biggest piece is a $25B investment-grade bond backed by SpaceX's five-year lease payments for Nvidia Vera Rubin NVL72 systems, priced at Treasuries +3.45pp (~8.3% yield) vs ~7.2% on SpaceX's 2031 bonds. The bonds mature in 2032, but principal is repaid in under four years. Moody's rates them A3, one notch above SpaceX, and KBRA A-. More than $19B was committed in advance, including $4B from Pimco. Lenders also pushed for a clause barring SpaceX from launching the collateral into orbit, though it's unclear whether that made the final documents. SPCX closed $138.43 (-3.53%) and was $129.19 pre-market (-6.7%), below its $135 IPO price (FT via Dealroom/TipRanks, Sina Finance, StockMarketWatch, Crypto Briefing).

6. Update on Tesla/SpaceX: HSBC upgraded TSLA to Hold from Reduce and raised its target to $359 from $157. The target blends a $507 SpaceX-acquisition value (a 33% premium to the 30-day average) with a $212 standalone value. HSBC sees control as Musk's main motive: he owns ~39% of SpaceX with 70% of the votes, vs ~20% of Tesla. It kept its Hold and $150 target on SPCX. TSLA was $363.76 pre-market (-2.8%) (Investing.com via Yahoo, StockMarketWatch).

7. Tesla said its supervised FSD ("Tesla Assisted Driving" in Europe) is "now approved in Italy," with "rollout begins soon." Italy is the 12th EU country and the first of the bloc's four biggest. Its ~58.9M people raise the share of EU residents covered to ~29% from ~16%. Tesla didn't give pricing, but the Netherlands subscription is €99/month (Electric-Vehicles.com, Tesla EMEA on X).

8. Strive: no new filings in the window. ASST was $16.34 pre-market (-1.6%), and SATA closed Thursday at $88.84 (StockMarketWatch, Aries).

AI, ROBOTICS, TECH & LONGEVITY

1. Update on Anthropic: ANT was down ~9–10% pre-market, near $88, giving back much of Thursday's 17% debut gain. Reuters says the IPO "failed to restore investors' faith in the AI sector." Saxo's Charu Chanana: the market "wants evidence that the extraordinary spending across the ecosystem can generate sustainable returns" (Investopedia, Reuters).

2. Update on Nvidia: California AG Rob Bonta served an investigative subpoena Thursday. It asks whether Nvidia's advanced chips or confidential information went to China in connection with Jensen Huang's affair with an alleged Chinese spy, and whether Nvidia misled investors. "Companies cannot mislead their investors," Bonta said. NVDA has lost 20%+ in two weeks and was -3% pre-market (CA DOJ, Investopedia).

3. Google picked Blue Origin's New Glenn to launch Project Suncatcher AI satellites in Q1 2029. It will be the program's first dedicated heavy-lift launch, carrying TPU satellites, each with roughly a data-center rack of compute, into sun-synchronous orbit. Google's first AI server satellite flew on a Falcon 9 rideshare in October. Ars notes Google's $200/kg mid-2030s cost target likely needs a fully optimized Starship V4, and SpaceX is prioritizing its own Starmind payloads (The Verge, Ars Technica).

4. Humanoids: the US denied visas to researchers and engineers at Chinese humanoid makers, including Xpeng and EngineAI, ahead of CES in Las Vegas. That clouds their plans to show hardware there, though the number of denials wasn't disclosed. Separately, Realbotix launched Series 1, capped at 25 full-body humanoids at $59,950 plus 225 tabletop units, and ROBOTERA showed its M7 sorting 1,500 parcels an hour at the APEC CEO Summit (Nikkei Asia via RobotToday, The Robotics Media).

5. Computer-use agents: Google launched Gemini for Mac, which can operate Mac apps, organize files and fill in forms, for US AI Plus/Pro/Ultra subscribers. Apple is reportedly building its own app-operating agent. Meta's Muse reportedly surfaced other people's private messages and bank balances to employees, and Meta says employees test versions with features that aren't public (The Neuron).

READS

1. "Google turns to Blue Origin for a rocket, but its long-term problem remains" by Eric Berger (Ars Technica), Nov 19. Why read: a sharp look at orbital-compute economics. Without Starship-class ~$200/kg launch, space data centers can't compete, and SpaceX (Starmind) and Blue Origin (Project Sunrise) are both building their own, leaving Google dependent on rivals. https://arstechnica.com/space/2026/11/google-turns-to-blue-origin-for-a-rocket-but-its-long-term-problem-remains/

2. "Two Down, One to Go: What the AI IPOs Mean for Bitcoin" by Cory Klippsten (Swan Bitcoin, X Article), Nov 19. Why read: the Swan CEO asks whether Anthropic's $81.3B raise pulled money from BTC. He contrasts the June SpaceX IPO, which he thinks did drag on BTC, and argues the Nvidia/Huang shock mattered more this time. OpenAI is next. https://x.com/CorySwan/status/2123470317901263298

2026-11-21.subject: Sat Nov 21 briefing: BTC $55.1K low/$2.4B liqs then back to $60K, ETFs -$1.25B week, MSTR $77.80/Strategy $35B reserve, SpaceX $44B GPU deal, Himes contract threat, FSD v15 Dec, Claude Riemann proof
2026-11-21.bodyText:
News window: Fri 9:00am – Sat 9:00am ET

Note: Stories in Friday's 5pm flash (the S&P correction and Nasdaq -5.28% close, BTC's first break of $60K, TSLA/SPCX closes, NVDA -14% on the SEC accounting report, Trump's data-center tax) are left out unless there's something new. Twenty One's 172.25 BTC buy went out as an alert last night and isn't repeated. The Fri 6–9am ET gap check found nothing the 9am briefing missed, and no treasury-company 8-Ks turned up.

MARKETS

1. BTC got flushed overnight, then bounced hard. It fell to a low of ~$55,100 on Kraken ($55,134 on OKX) around 1am ET, its lowest since September 2024 (Investing.com), and below the $57,717 bear-market low from Jul 1 (Galaxy). That left it down more than half from its record above $126,000. CoinGlass counted ~$2.4B of crypto liquidations over 24 hours, including more than $1B of BTC futures and $545M of ETH. The biggest single wipeout was a $51.71M BTC long. ETH fell to $1,564 at about 1am. BTC then climbed back above $60,000 around 8:40am (Bitcoin Magazine) and was ~$60,400 at 8:57am ET, -2.2% over 24 hours. Fear & Greed is at 12 (Investing.com, Bitcoin Insider, Kraken, OKX, CoinGecko, Coinbase, WhaleRoom/CryptoNews).

2. Spot BTC ETFs lost -$124.5M Friday, their fourth straight outflow day. FBTC led at -$72.4M, followed by GBTC -$32.8M, BTC Mini -$12.9M, BITB -$7.0M and EZBC -$1.7M. IBIT was flat, and MSBT took in +$2.3M. Farside's weekly total is -$1,245.3M, with IBIT at -$822.8M. By my math November is now about -$3.59B, with outflows on 13 of 15 sessions (Farside via DefiLlama/CryptoNews, @FarsideUK).

3. Update on Strategy: MSTR closed Friday at $77.80 (-9.67%). That's its lowest close since February 2024 and 83.6% below its record close of $473.83 on Nov 20, 2024. STRC closed at $93.60, down from $99.98 on Nov 9. After the close, Strategy posted that in the 2022 bear market its net reserve was negative and a third of its BTC was pledged as collateral, but "today, our Net Reserve is $35 billion. All our BTC is unencumbered." Blockstream's Adam Back said he was "buying MSTR here." Saylor posted "Remember why you ₿ought" Friday and "Every day we Stretch. $STRC" at 8:01am today, with no tracker chart yet. At ~$60.4K, the 850,849 BTC are worth ~$51.5B, about $12.7B below their $64.20B cost by my math (Bitcoin.com, @Strategy/@saylor on X, Yahoo Finance).

4. Fed: Treasury Secretary Bessent told CNBC Friday that he'd encourage the Fed not to hike by a half point at its Dec 8–9 meeting, citing the energy supply shock and the drop in crude. "I would encourage the Fed to look forward, not backwards," he said, and he called a governor's turn from wanting a cut to wanting a 50bp hike "somewhat peripatetic." CME FedWatch showed a 98%+ chance of a quarter-point hike, and the 10-year yield fell 10bp+ to 4.95%. Reuters separately reported Fed Governor Cook saying rate hikes are needed to bring down high inflation (Bitcoin Magazine, Reuters).

5. Update on SpaceX financing: Apollo and Goldman priced ~$44B of senior and subordinated notes to fund Nvidia Vera Rubin GPUs and related equipment for SpaceX's terrestrial compute buildout. The deal was oversubscribed and upsized, and they call it the largest GPU financing to date.
