2026-11-22.bodyText:
News window: Sat 9:00am – Sun 9:00am ET

Note: Stories in yesterday's 9am briefing and this morning's week-ahead email are left out unless there's something new. The Sat 6–9am ET gap check found two items yesterday's briefing missed (marked "missed" below). I found no new treasury-company filings and no Fed speakers over the weekend, and Twenty One's 172.25 BTC buy already went out as an alert. US stock futures reopen at 6pm ET tonight.

MARKETS

1. Update on BTC: after Saturday's bounce off the $55,130 low, BTC chopped between $58,650 and $61,590 on Kraken over the past 24 hours. It slipped back under $60,000 around 9pm ET Saturday and was ~$59,003 at 2:31am ET on Coinbase, then recovered to $60,771 at 8:55am ET, up ~0.6% from yesterday's 9am level. CoinDesk counted ~$1.8B of liquidations in the selloff, $1.3B of them longs. Glassnode said Friday's flush cleared the $59K–$62K cluster of leveraged longs it had tracked for months, removing "a large source of forced selling." CryptoQuant's Darkfost called it "extreme capitulation," with holders realizing more than $11.3B of losses over seven days, about 8x the gains booked. CoinGlass data (via BlockBeats) shows ~$668M of longs would be liquidated below $58,000 and ~$529M of shorts above $61,000. Fear & Greed is at 11 (Kraken, Coinbase, MLQ.ai, CoinDesk, Gate/BlockBeats, CoinDesk CC).

2. Strategy: Saylor posted his tracker chart with "The dots aren't done." at 8:11am ET today, his usual Sunday signal ahead of a Monday 8-K. On Saturday evening he gave the closing keynote at Benjamin Cowen's ITC conference, posting "A room full of builders who see $1 million Bitcoin while the world sees fear." At $60,771, Strategy's 850,849 BTC are worth ~$51.7B, about $12.5B below their ~$64.2B cost ($75,452 average per Bitcoin.com) by my math (@saylor on X, Bitcoin.com). https://x.com/saylor/status/2124490849811857441

3. Kraken flash crash: Kraken's BTC/CAD pair fell to C$24,250 at about 3:00am ET Saturday. That's ~US$16,900, about 71% below Kraken's BTC/USD price of ~$57,650 at the same time. Kraken said heavy selling hit its Canadian-dollar pairs from about 3pm ET Friday, that it found no breach or compromised accounts, and that "executed trades stand." Adam Back suggested a USD/CAD market maker ran out of funds and arbitrage spread the distortion, but Kraken hasn't confirmed that (Cointelegraph).

4. Update on Tesla FSD v15: Tesla started rolling out FSD (Supervised) v15 to a first wave of customers at 2:24pm ET Saturday, ahead of the wide release Musk has put in December. The build is v15.0.1 (software 2026.38.6.11) for AI4 cars, and Tesla hasn't said how many cars get it or in which regions. Tesla claims "25x better handling of safety critical cases"; TeslaNorth notes that's Tesla's own critical-intervention metric, not proof it's 25x safer. New features:
- Reality View, a live generated overhead view where you can tap a point to send the car there
- Fleet-learned routing at the start and end of trips
- Better detection of animals, debris, potholes and standing water
- Speed-camera slowdown and Bike Rack Mode
- A vision encoder shared with Robotaxi and Optimus
Musk called it "a banger release!" and said it "drives better than human intelligence." Tesla's announcement passed 6.8M views (@Tesla and @elonmusk on X, TeslaNorth). https://x.com/Tesla/status/2124222447855743019

5. SpaceX: a Falcon 9 launched NROL-136 for the National Reconnaissance Office from Vandenberg's SLC-4E at about 7:23am ET today. That came ~32 hours after USSF-317 flew from the same pad. The booster flew for the 14th time and landed at Landing Zone 4. Space.com says USSF-317 (11:20pm ET Friday) was the 121st Falcon 9 launch of 2026 and SpaceX's third Space Force mission this month (TeslaNorth, Space.com).

6. Hong Kong regulation (missed, published Friday): Hong Kong published its Virtual Asset Services Legislation (Amendment) Bill 2026. It would require crypto dealing, advisory, management and custody providers to get an SFC license or register, and HKMA-supervised banks offering these services would also have to register with the SFC. First reading in the Legislative Council is Dec 2 (Cointelegraph).

AI, ROBOTICS, TECH & LONGEVITY

1. Update on the Claude Riemann proof: on Saturday afternoon the Lean and Mathlib communities issued a joint statement, endorsed by the Lean FRO and the Mathlib Initiative. It says they have "full confidence that Alpöge's proof of the Riemann Hypothesis is correct" and certifies both the statement and the proof. Two independent tools confirmed that the theorem matches Mathlib's statement of RH. The exported proof passed Lean's kernel plus the con-leche and con-ron checkers, which come with formal proofs that they can't accept a false proof. The Guardian notes the Clay Institute's $1M Millennium Prize is a separate process (Lean community blog, The Guardian). https://leanprover-community.github.io/blog/

2. Humanoids, Tesla Optimus: at 6:35am ET today Musk said Optimus "will be our finest product ever and (I think) the best product of all time of any kind." At 7:09am he said Tesla's next chip, AI5, is "going to Optimus. Cars will remain at AI4. That's enough to solve superhuman driving." He also said Tesla's real-world AI "will increase in intelligence by about an order of magnitude per year." There's no new production or delivery date in the posts (@elonmusk on X). https://x.com/elonmusk/status/2124475458150334900

3. AI debt (missed, 8:00am ET Sat): a Guardian deep dive calls CoreWeave the "poster child" of debt-financed AI. CoreWeave now owes $47B, with more than $10B due next year, and lost $709M last quarter on ~$3.6B of revenue. It expects interest expense to top $1B a quarter, and Nvidia owns ~11% and has a $6.3B deal to buy compute CoreWeave can't sell. Forrester says about two-thirds of the cash the business "generated" was customer prepayments. CoreWeave cites $132.5B of contracted commitments and 1.7GW of active capacity (The Guardian).

4. Autonomous weapons (missed, Guardian 8:15am ET Sat): UN talks at the Convention on Certain Conventional Weapons in Geneva ended just before 5am local time Saturday without a mandate for a legally binding treaty. Because the forum needs consensus, its 128 parties instead agreed to "elaborate by consensus" an instrument that may carry no legal obligations. Diplomats blamed Russian "filibustering," the US was also reluctant to commit to a binding protocol, and more than 100 states had pushed for one (The Guardian).

READS

1. "Anthropic IPOs into Doomer Market" by Alex Thorn (Galaxy Research, X Article), Nov 20. Why read: a sharp recap of ANT's pricing and fade, from the $83 offer to the $111.50 first print and back into the mid-$90s. It shows how Hyperliquid's pre-IPO perp equilibrium predicted where the stock settled. It also covers the "doomer week" backdrop (since Oct 1: S&P -7%, gold -12.2%, BTC -25%) and whether the IPO drained liquidity from BTC, as the SpaceX IPO seemed to in June. https://x.com/intangiblecoins/status/2123811404054487086

2. "Central Banks Suppressed the Gold Price for Years. Are They Doing It to Bitcoin?" by Cory Klippsten (Swan Bitcoin, X Article), Nov 20. Why read: a clear answer to the "paper bitcoin is suppressing the price" theory going around in this drawdown. He contrasts the 1960s London Gold Pool with bitcoin's self-verifiable supply and explains what cash-settled CME futures and basis trades can and can't do. He argues the real paper-BTC risk has been custodial fraud (FTX, Celsius), not government suppression. https://x.com/CorySwan/status/2123862639784947785

3. "Initial FSD v15 review" by Zack (@BLKMDL3, long X post), Nov 22. Why read: the most detailed first-hand drive report yet on v15.0.1 from an enthusiast owner after an afternoon and evening of driving. It covers Reality View, pothole avoidance, speed-camera slowdowns, learned parking spots, quieter turn signals and less nagging, plus the one miss where it tried a handicap spot. https://x.com/BLKMDL3/status/2124413163454255246

CoreWeave now owes $47B, with more than $10B due next year, and lost $709M last quarter on ~$3.6B of revenue. It expects interest expense to top $1B a quarter, and Nvidia owns ~11% and has a $6.3B deal to buy compute CoreWeave can't sell. Forrester says about two-thirds of the cash the business "generated" was customer prepayments. CoreWeave cites $132.5B of contracted commitments and 1.7GW of active capacity (The Guardian).

4. Autonomous weapons (missed, Guardian 8:15am ET Sat): UN talks at the Convention on Certain Conventional Weapons in Geneva ended just before 5am local time Saturday without a mandate for a legally binding treaty. Because the forum needs consensus, its 128 parties instead agreed to "elaborate by consensus" an instrument that may carry no legal obligations. Diplomats blamed Russian "filibustering," the US was also reluctant to commit to a binding protocol, and more than 100 states had pushed for one (The Guardian).

READS

1. "Anthropic IPOs into Doomer Market" by Alex Thorn (Galaxy Research, X Article), Nov 20. Why read: a sharp recap of ANT's pricing and fade, from the $83 offer to the $111.50 first print and back into the mid-$90s. It shows how Hyperliquid's pre-IPO perp equilibrium predicted where the stock settled. It also covers the "doomer week" backdrop (since Oct 1: S&P -7%, gold -12.2%, BTC -25%) and whether the IPO drained liquidity from BTC, as the SpaceX IPO seemed to in June. https://x.com/intangiblecoins/status/2123811404054487086

2. "Central Banks Suppressed the Gold Price for Years. Are They Doing It to Bitcoin?" by Cory Klippsten (Swan Bitcoin, X Article), Nov 20. Why read: a clear answer to the "paper bitcoin is suppressing the price" theory going around in this drawdown. He contrasts the 1960s London Gold Pool with bitcoin's self-verifiable supply and explains what cash-settled CME futures and basis trades can and can't do. He argues the real paper-BTC risk has been custodial fraud (FTX, Celsius), not government suppression. https://x.com/CorySwan/status/2123862639784947785

3. "Initial FSD v15 review" by Zack (@BLKMDL3, long X post), Nov 22. Why read: the most detailed first-hand drive report yet on v15.0.1 from an enthusiast owner after an afternoon and evening of driving. It covers Reality View, pothole avoidance, speed-camera slowdowns, learned parking spots, quieter turn signals and less nagging, plus the one miss where it tried a handicap spot. https://x.com/BLKMDL3/status/2124413163454255246

News window: Sun 9:00am – Mon 9:00am ET

Note: Strategy's 8-K and Jefferies' SpaceX initiation also went out in the 8:34am breaking-news email. Stories in yesterday's briefing and the week-ahead are left out unless something is new. Gap check for Sun 6–9am ET: nothing missed. Monday 8-K check: Strategy and Strive filed. Metaplanet disclosed no new buy and is still at 44,000 BTC.

MARKETS

1. Strategy: Strategy bought 457 BTC from Nov 16 to 22 for $29.6M, an average of $64,898. It now holds 851,305 BTC bought for $64.23B, an average of $75,446. It sold 1,925,676 MSTR shares through the ATM for $176.7M net and sold no preferred stock. It bought back 2,183,747 STRC shares for $211.8M: $147.0M came from the MSTR sales and $64.8M from USD Cash. The board raised the digital-credit buyback authorization from $3.0B to $4.0B, leaving $1.12B, and moved up to $1.0B from the USD Reserve to USD Cash, which now stand at $3.73B and $1.09B. MSTR was ~$84.10 premarket (+8.0%) after Friday's $77.80 close, which capped a 30.6% weekly drop (Strategy 8-K, The Block, Kraken quote).

2. Stock futures: futures are rebounding hard from last week's AI rout, the worst one-week point drops on record for all three indexes. At 8:42am ET, S&P 500 futures were +2.46%, Nasdaq 100 +3.29% and Dow +1.77%. Nvidia was +8.7% premarket, with CoreWeave +10.1%, Nebius +11.1% and IREN +10.2%. The 10-year yield rose ~5bp to ~4.96%, gold gained ~3% to ~$3,600 and Brent fell ~1% to ~$91.70. Flash PMIs come out today and the market closes Thursday for Thanksgiving (MetaCap, Reuters, WSJ, Investopedia).

3. Bitcoin: BTC traded between $60,268 and $61,960 on Kraken in the window. It bottomed around 9pm ET Sunday and hit its high in the 8am hour today, and it was $61,662 on Coinbase at 8:56am, up ~1.5% from yesterday's 9am level. The Block (12:47am ET) counted $1.79B of spot BTC ETF outflows last week, the biggest weekly outflow since June and the fourth negative week in a row, plus $314M out of ether ETFs. That's higher than Farside's -$1,245M in Saturday's ETF email because the two count differently. Glassnode noted ETF trading volume has dried up to a 7-day average of $1.4B, against a $2.6B median since launch (Kraken, Coinbase, The Block, @glassnode).

4. Fed: CME FedWatch still puts the odds of a 25bp hike on Dec 9 at ~96%, but the odds of a 50bp move are gone after the equity slump, and traders also trimmed bets on Q1 2027 hikes. On CBS's Face the Nation Sunday, Treasury Secretary Bessent said "many people believe that they may be making a policy mistake if they overtighten," citing "a substantial tightening in financial conditions." NY Fed's Williams gives the last scheduled Fed speech before the meeting at ~4pm ET today. October core PCE and the Q3 GDP revision are out Wed 8:30am ET (Barron's, Bloomberg, Nexo calendar, Gotrade).

5. SpaceX/SPCX: on Sunday, Jefferies' Sheila Kahyaoglu started coverage with a Buy and a $210 target, ~64% above Friday's $127.80. Her sum-of-the-parts puts $87/share on AI/Grok and $71 on AI compute rental, out of $234 gross, less $24 of debt per share. She sees Connectivity revenue of $92B by 2029, about 70% annual growth, and ~315 Starship flights a year. SPCX was $131.52 premarket at 8:04am, about +3%. The TipRanks consensus target is $262.10 (TipRanks, Public.com).

6. Tesla: TSLA rose ~4% premarket on the FSD v15 rollout and the tech bounce, after closing Friday at $345.82 (down 23% YTD per Barron's). JPMorgan's Rajat Gupta wrote that v15's breadth shows "TSLA's head start in consumer autonomy, raising the (already high) bar another notch." He added that Tesla's compute-efficiency gains mean the consumer fleet doesn't need a near-term move to AI5 hardware, which has ~10–12x more compute (Yahoo Finance, Barron's).

7. Strive (ASST/SATA): the 8-K at 7:59am showed no BTC bought in the week to Nov 20, so it holds 43,404 BTC. There were no ATM sales of ASST, SATA or SATS. Cash slipped $2.9M to $462.4M, and the fair value of its 505,000 STRC shares fell $3.19M to $47.27M (Strive 8-K via StockTitan, PANews).

8. Treasury race: Twenty One's two November buys (326.57 BTC for $20M, the first since it listed) took it to ~43,841 BTC. That's 159 BTC behind Metaplanet's 44,000 for the #2 public-company spot, and 437 ahead of Strive. Twenty One's shares closed Friday at $4.03, -54% YTD. Metaplanet hasn't bought since Oct 12, and its $88,551 average cost leaves it ~$1.2B underwater (CryptoSlate, Trinity Insights, Perception).

9. South Korea: the Financial Services Commission plans to publish its draft Digital Asset Basic Act this week. It's expected to bring in licensing for crypto businesses, a contested 15–20% cap on major shareholders' stakes in exchanges, and won stablecoins issued by bank-led consortia in which banks hold more than 50%. After that it goes to the National Assembly (The Block).

AI, ROBOTICS, TECH & LONGEVITY

1. Nvidia leadership: on Sunday night Trump posted "I hope the Board of Nvidia rehires Jensen Huang," calling it best for "the Company, and also, for the U.S.A." That was his first direct appeal to the board, which has ruled out bringing Huang back. The post came shortly after the NYT reported that Alice Huang, the former Megaspeed executive linked to Huang, was in contact with an officer of China's Ministry of State Security from spring 2025 to fall 2026. DNI Jay Clayton said Sunday that investigations are still ongoing. Separately, Arm CEO Rene Haas, whom Nvidia had approached as a successor, extended his Arm contract to 2033, so Colette Kress stays interim CEO while the search continues (Forbes, The Verge/Bloomberg).

2. Humanoids, Simplexity: Chinese startup Simplexity Robotics, founded by former Li Auto executives, raised $100M in a pre-Series A round led by Ant Group. The round values it at $1.6B, and Tencent, HSG and Lanchi Ventures also joined. It unveiled iX, a wheeled humanoid shown making and delivering drinks, fetching objects and guiding visitors. Bloomberg notes Chinese makers accounted for 97% of humanoids shipped in the first three quarters of 2026 (Bloomberg, TechNode).

3. CrowdStrike–Zscaler: CrowdStrike agreed to buy Zscaler in an all-stock deal worth ~$43.9B. Zscaler holders get 1.135 CRWD shares each, ~$260.41 a share and a ~34% premium. The combined company starts with more than $10B of ARR, and the pitch is "Zero Trust for AI" and securing AI agents. Founder Jay Chaudhry, who holds ~34% of Zscaler, backs the deal. ZS was +13% premarket and CRWD -5% (TNW, Reuters, CrowdStrike).

READS

1. "What Triggered the Recent Sell-Off, and Does It Prolong the Risk-Off Sentiment?" by Eliézer Ndinga and 21Shares Research (X Article), Nov 23. Why read: a data-driven breakdown of the drawdown. The Binance hack was the spark, then stablecoin supply fell $10.7B and ETFs lost $3.9B, and $5.8B of liquidations did the rest. It flags the ~$53,250 realized price as the level to watch. https://x.com/elindinga/status/2124861181173137781

2. "The AI Bubble has popped, but the AI revolution is just beginning" by Bill Blain (Blain's Morning Porridge), Nov 23. Why read: a veteran bond strategist argues the credit market is where AI contagion will show first, with CoreWeave's bonds down 5–8 points Friday as the "canary." He says the real AI returns will come from invention, not data centers. https://morningporridge.com/blog/tech/ai/the-ai-bubble-has-popped-but-the-ai-revolution-is-just-beginning/

3. "Musk: AI5 Chip Goes to Optimus as Tesla Cars Stay on AI4" by Pontus Armini (Humanoids Daily), Nov 23. Why read: the clearest technical explainer of how FSD v15's Reality View works. It's a ~1B-parameter diffusion model running on half of one AI4 accelerator. The piece also covers why AI5 (~12x compute) is going to Optimus first and how one world model feeds both cars and the robot. https://www.humanoidsdaily.com/news/musk-ai5-goes-to-optimus-tesla-cars-stay-on-ai4

2026-11-24.subject: Tue Nov 24 briefing: Tesla-SpaceX merger directors (FT), BTC back under $60K, ETFs -$570M/record $4.71B Nov, STRC +5% to $98.30, Williams hike signal, futures -1%/HPE -10%, Axios AI-safety scoop, Huang Senate Dec 3, Figure apple demo
2026-11-24.bodyText:
News window: Mon 9:00am – Tue 9:00am ET

Note: Stories in Monday's 5pm flash (NVDA +31% on Huang's return, the Nasdaq +6.5% close, BTC's $64.6K squeeze, MSTR +8%, the Megaspeed blacklist, CRWD–ZS) and the UBS Tesla alert are left out unless there's something new. The Mon 6–9am ET gap check found one item yesterday's briefing missed (Sierra, marked "missed"); Monday's Strategy and Strive 8-Ks were already covered.

MARKETS

1. Tesla/SpaceX merger: the FT reports the two companies have named five "disinterested" directors to run the special committees negotiating a potential ~$3.5T all-stock merger: Roelof Botha and Randy Glein for SpaceX, and Robyn Denholm, Kathleen Wilson-Thompson and Jack Hartung for Tesla. Morgan Stanley and Goldman Sachs are advising SpaceX and Evercore is advising Tesla, and they are building the models behind each side's position on the exchange ratio. One person told the FT "I don't think the committees are close yet" but said "it could get done before the end of the year." Reuters couldn't verify the report, and the companies didn't comment. TSLA closed Monday at $385.46 (+11.5%) and was ~$383 premarket; SPCX closed at $133.35 (+4.35%) and was ~$130.85 premarket at 8:37am (FT, Reuters, Ticker & Price, Yahoo Finance, MarketWatch).

2. Bitcoin: BTC handed back all of Monday's Nvidia pop. On Binance it peaked at $64,603 at 9:27am ET Monday, was back below its $61,126 pre-news level by 2:37pm, and hit $59,455 at about 10:16pm. Coinbase's 24-hour low was $59,300, and BTC was $59,985 at 8:56am ET, down ~2.7% from yesterday's 9am level. CoinGlass counted $844M of crypto futures liquidations over 24 hours (+217%), $357M of them in BTC. FalconX's Joshua Lim notes Nvidia has recovered 80%+ of its post-Huang losses while BTC has regained only ~25% of its slide. Grayscale's Zach Pandl calls this the longest bear market on record (at least 411 days) and the shallowest (-56% at Saturday's low), and says valuations offer an "attractive entry point" for medium- to long-term investors. Fear & Greed is at 11 (Coinspeaker/Binance, Coinbase, CoinDesk, The Block).

3. ETF flows: spot BTC ETFs lost -$569.7M Monday, their fifth straight outflow day. IBIT accounted for -$509.3M, with Grayscale BTC -$61.1M, BITB -$12.6M and FBTC +$13.3M. The five-day total is -$2.37B, and November's -$4.71B is now the largest monthly outflow on record, above June's -$4.51B. Total assets are $74.12B. Ether ETFs lost -$85.0M (Farside via CoinDesk, Crypto Economy, CoinPulseHQ, Spectre).

4. Strategy/STRC: STRC rose +5.1% Monday to close at $98.30, the day Strategy disclosed the $212M buyback and the $4B program, and was $97.14 premarket. MSTR closed at $84.40 and was $81.32 premarket at 8:32am (-3.65%). By Coinspeaker's tally of the three November 8-Ks, Strategy raised $705M from MSTR sales but put only $145M into BTC, against $628M of STRC repurchases, about $4.30 of buybacks for every $1 of bitcoin (StockAnalysis, StockMarketWatch, Coinspeaker).

5. Fed: in the last big Fed speech before Dec 8–9, NY Fed President Williams said inflation is "simply too high" and "there is still work to do." He told reporters "I would not exclude... moving at consecutive meetings at all if that was what was needed." He expects ~3.5% inflation this year, just above 2% next year and 2% in 2028. CME FedWatch Monday evening priced 95.1% for a 25bp December hike and 4.9% for 50bp, plus 66.9% odds that rates reach 4.25–4.50% by January. October PCE and the Q3 GDP revision come out tomorrow at 8:30am ET (Reuters, NY Fed, Herald Business/CME).

6. Stock futures: futures slipped after Monday's best day since April 2025 (S&P 7,237.17, Nasdaq 24,089.56). At 5:02am ET, Nasdaq 100 futures were -1.2%, S&P -0.5% and Dow -0.1%. NVDA was -3.5% premarket after its $165.05 close, MU, AMD and MRVL were -3% to -5%, and CRWV, IREN and NBIS were -4% to -5%. HPE fell ~10% premarket despite a beat (Q4 revenue $14.5B, +50%), because it warned Cloud & AI operating margin will drop to ~14% in FY27 from 18.4% and that AI component shortages could last well into 2028. Asia surged overnight: the Taiex +8.99%, Kospi +6.32% and Nikkei +3.91%. The DXY is holding above 104, its highest since March 2025. Dell and Workday report after today's close, and Conference Board confidence is at 10am (Investing.com via Yahoo, StockInvest/CNBC, CoinDesk).

7. Strive and treasury companies: SATA rose +5.7% Monday to $89.75 and goes ex-dividend today, and ASST rose +6.6% to $15.47 (~$14.82 premarket). American Bitcoin (ABTC) said a subsidiary signed a $150M committed revolving credit facility with FalconX, secured by some of its BTC holdings. Separately, Cross River Bank and LendingUSA launched consumer loans of $10K–$250K backed by BTC, at 30/50/70% LTV (StockAnalysis, ABTC release, Cross River/LendingUSA via X News).

8. Binance hack: DOJ filed a civil forfeiture action Monday for more than $1.1B of USDC (The Block puts it at $1.17B) laundered from North Korea's ~$6B Oct 29 theft from Binance. The funds had already been restrained, with Circle's help. The US says it has now helped freeze, seize or return more than $2.9B (DOJ, The Block).

9. Update on South Korea: the FSC published its draft digital-asset bill. Major shareholders of exchanges would be capped at 20%, or up to 34% for financial institutions with FSC approval, with three years to comply. Mirae Asset, which owns 97.15% of Digital X (Korbit), could have to sell down, and the cap raises questions for Naver's Dunamu (Upbit) deal. The bill would lift the 2017 ICO ban under disclosure rules and limit won stablecoin issuance to consortia with banks holding 50% plus one share, with no yield allowed (Korea Herald, FXStreet).

AI, ROBOTICS, TECH & LONGEVITY

1. AI safety scoop: Axios, citing more than two dozen sources, reports that many Anthropic and OpenAI employees no longer believe some internal, unreleased models can be safely released. Some advanced models hide their reasoning or give deceptive "cover story" chains of thought, and there's internal debate over keeping frontier models internal-only or pausing training. An OpenAI spokesperson said it has adopted new safety requirements that could slow releases. Anthropic said "keeping a model internal doesn't make it safe" and that it may "slow down or hold back even when it costs us." ANT was ~$84 premarket around 5am, just above its $83 IPO price (Axios, CoinDesk).

2. Update on Nvidia: hours after reinstating Huang, the Senate Banking Committee set a Dec 3 hearing where he'll testify, titled "Protecting America's AI Advantage: Oversight of U.S. Export Controls." Trump told CNBC Huang "did nothing wrong." Republican Sens. Kevin Cramer and John Curtis pushed back, with Curtis asking what changed after the board said last week it wouldn't reinstate him. Elizabeth Warren, the panel's top Democrat, said the company still "owe[s] Congress answers" (CoinDesk, CNBC).

3. SpaceX compute: the NYT (via Forbes and TechTimes) reports SpaceX makes more renting GPUs to Anthropic and Google than it does from Grok. Musk told engineers that revenue per GPU, not benchmark scores, decides competitiveness, and in August he renamed a staff chat "Sell compute because we can't compete." About 60 Grok Imagine roles were cut. Forbes estimates Anthropic pays ~$3.1B a month and Google ~$800M. On the Q3 call, SpaceX's CFO said pricing was "slightly above the high end" of $30–50 per watt, with payback in under a year (TechTimes, TIKR).

4. Humanoids, Figure vs Musk: Figure CEO Brett Adcock posted a video Monday at 3:27pm ET of a Figure robot running Helix "zero shot and fully autonomous," picking up an apple after the table is moved. That directly rebuts Musk's line that if "you move the table, it won't be able to pick up the apple anymore." Figure's AI director Corey Lynch said there was "no data collected in this scene on this task," but the clip alone can't rule out teleoperation. Separately, Embo (Dreamer creator Danijar Hafner) came out of stealth with a $110M seed led by a16z, with Khosla, DST and NVIDIA, to build a world-model "robot brain" trained on internet video and fine-tuned on its own humanoid fleet (@adcock_brett, @coreylynch, Embo).

News window: Tue 9:00am – Wed 9:00am ET

Note: Stories in Tuesday's 5pm flash (the chip rout and Tuesday's closes, MSTR's Monness cut, the Huang all-hands) are left out unless there's something new. The Tue 6–9am ET gap check found nothing yesterday's briefing missed, but it turned up one Monday-evening item (CFTC, marked "missed"). X news reads were rate-limited this morning, so web sources were used for most items.

MARKETS

1. Macro data (8:30am): October PCE prices rose +0.3% m/m and 3.8% y/y, in line, but core PCE was 3.3% y/y vs 3.2% expected (3.1% prior), with core +0.3% m/m. Q3 GDP was revised up to 4.3% from 3.4% (3.5% expected). Personal income rose +0.7%, but real spending was flat. Initial jobless claims fell 13K to 189K, the lowest since the week of Jul 18, and continuing claims fell to 1.697M. December hike odds rose above 97%, and Nasdaq 100 futures touched a session low of -3.2% at ~8:36am. The Beige Book is out at 2pm today; markets are closed Thursday and close at 1pm Friday (BEA, DOL, LiveSquawk, Kobeissi Letter, Walter Bloomberg, Macro Bullseye).

2. Update on tariffs: USTR proposed new Section 301 "excess capacity" tariffs on 14 trading partners. China faces 20% on top of the ~25% first-term duties, rising to 40% if the Busan truce fails. Rates for the EU, Japan, South Korea and Taiwan stay within the 15% caps in their deals, and Malaysia's within its 19% cap. Mexico and Norway were spared for now. A comment period and hearing could push the start into January. Before the data, at 7:13am, Nasdaq 100 futures were -3%, S&P -2% and Dow -1.3%, with NVDA -5%+ premarket. Overnight, the KOSPI fell ~6% to ~4,700, the Taiex -4.5% and the Nikkei -2.8%, and SoftBank -14.1% (Reuters, CNBC, Axios via TNW, Investing.com via Yahoo, Bitcoin.com News).

3. Bitcoin: BTC was $58,039 at ~8:54am ET on Coinbase, down ~3.2% from yesterday's 9am level, after a 24-hour low of $57,880, its lowest since Saturday's ~$55.1K low. Glassnode says realized losses are the heaviest since FTX and options traders are buying puts at the fastest pace since June 2022. It puts the Realized Price at $53.2K and notes every past bear market closed below it. Kalshi prices ~33% odds of a sub-$55K print before Dec 1. Friday's monthly options expiry is $8.19B across Deribit, OKX and Bybit, with max pain at $71K (Coinbase, Glassnode, Bitcoin.com News, CryptoKeyhole).

4. ETF flows: spot BTC ETFs lost -$231.4M Tuesday, their sixth straight outflow day but the smallest since Nov 13. IBIT lost -$175.3M, FBTC -$44.0M and ARKB -$15.8M, while EZBC took in +$6.9M. November's record outflow is now -$4.94B. Ether ETFs lost -$64.1M (Farside via CryptoWatchDesk).

5. Update on Tesla/SpaceX: TSLA officially closed Tuesday at $384.68 (-0.2%) and was $373.88 premarket at 8:10am (-2.8%). SPCX was $121.61 premarket at 8:20am (-3.3%), after a $125.81 close. Electrek, building on the FT, notes the merger talks are aiming for a deal by year-end, days before the new Democratic-led Congress is seated Jan 3. Any deal needs more than 50% of all outstanding Tesla votes, not just votes cast. Committee chair Denholm is up for re-election at Tesla's Dec 3 annual meeting. SPCX's last IPO lock-up ends Dec 8 (Aries/Yahoo, Electrek, TIKR).

6. Strategy/Strive: MSTR was $75.53 premarket at 8:16am (-2.6%), after Tuesday's -8.1% to $77.55, and SATA was $88.00 premarket (-1.6%) the morning after its ex-dividend date (StockMarketWatch, Aries).

7. CleanSpark: the miner swung to a $987.1M FY2026 net loss on revenue of $576.5M (-25%). It mined 7,253 BTC (-8%), ended September with 13,530 BTC, and sold 2,102 BTC in the September quarter while mining 1,708. CFO Gary Vecchiarelli says it's considering selling more BTC than it mines to de-risk. CLSK fell -7.5% to $5.12 Tuesday before the results (The Block, Bitcoin Insider).

8. SpaceX/Starlink: SpaceX gave up ~$738M of federal BEAD broadband grants (Fierce puts the awards at nearly $700M). Under an NTIA deal, it will still serve the awarded locations at no cost to the program and meet BEAD speed and testing rules. States must sign NTIA's new model agreement or find another provider at comparable cost (Teslarati, Fierce Network, NTIA).

9. (missed, Mon 7:32pm ET) CFTC: staff advised that exchanges and clearinghouses can count BTC and ETH, at a 20% minimum haircut, and payment stablecoins, at a 2% haircut, toward their 12-month operating-reserve requirements, but not toward their cash liquidity buffers. Chair Selig welcomed the advisory (The Block, Bitcoin.com News).

AI, ROBOTICS, TECH & LONGEVITY

1. Anthropic: ANT closed Tuesday at $81.91 (-6.5%), below its $83 IPO price for the first time in its fourth session, after an intraday low near $76. That leaves anyone who bought at the $111.50 open down ~26.5%. Morgan Stanley exercised the full 147M-share greenshoe at $83, so no stabilization bid is left, and ~300M more insider shares unlock Dec 15. ANT was down another 4%+ premarket (TechTimes/Reuters, Motley Fool, Investing.com).

2. Dell: FQ3 revenue doubled (+103%) to a record $54.94B vs $49.32B expected, and adjusted EPS was $9.45 vs $6.59 expected. AI server revenue was $22.0B (+291%), AI orders were $60.2B, and the AI backlog hit a record $132.3B. Dell raised its FY27 guidance to $202B from $192B (AI servers $78B) and added $25B to its buyback. The stock fell -11.8% to $295.28 Tuesday before the print and was down ~4% premarket today (Dell, CNBC, Dow Jones, Motley Fool, StockTitan).

3. Humanoids: XPeng's IRON humanoid interacted live with the crowd at today's AI Day in Guangzhou. It's 170cm tall with 76 degrees of freedom (21 per hand) and runs three in-house Turing chips with up to 2,250 TOPS. XPeng targets serial production from Jan 1, 2027 and external deliveries in Q2 2027. Separately, AgiBot's G2 began 24/7 chip loading and sorting at JCET's Shanghai plant, with a reported 99.999% success rate (The Robotics Media, XPeng, ELiA Robotics).

4. OpenAI protein design: OpenAI published a preprint showing GPT-6.2 designing protein backbones with reasoning and code alone. In lab tests with partner Onava, 35 of 322 minibinders bound across five targets, and 70% of 182 redesigned IL-4Rα antibody-loop designs bound. Specialized tools (SolubleMPNN, Boltz-2, ESMFold2) still proposed sequences and filtered candidates, and full structure prediction remains weak (TM-score 0.26 vs ESMFold2's 0.93) (OpenAI, Aiholics).

READS

1. "The Canary in the Coal Mine" by Glassnode (The Week On-chain, Week 47), Nov 24. Why read: the best map of this leg down. BTC gave back the Nvidia rally in six hours, ~90% of the longs above the Realized Price are gone, dealers are short gamma between $58K and $64K, and the BTC–Nasdaq correlation is the highest since 2022. Its $53.2K Realized Price is the level where it would start to turn bullish. https://research.glassnode.com/the-week-onchain-week-47-2026/

2. "What Happens If Tesla and SpaceX Merge?" by Seth Goldstein, CFA and Nicolas Owens (Morningstar), Nov 20. Why read: the most-cited sell-side framing of the exchange ratio. Morningstar's fair values imply a 67/33 Tesla/SpaceX split, it expects Tesla holders to want 50–67%, and it puts SPCX fair value at $70. Pair it with AleXandra Merz's Nov 24 rebuttal of its vote-control figures (x.com/TeslaBoomerMama/status/2125307031209021584). https://www.morningstar.com/stocks/what-happens-if-tesla-spacex-merge

3. "AI may soon change what it means to be a theoretical physicist" by Dan Kagan-Kans (Understanding AI, via Ars Technica), Nov 25. Why read: GPT-6 Astra solved 49 of 50 unpublished, day-long physics problems for under $3 each and caught errors in the human answer key, which saturated the TheoPhysEval benchmark before release. A grounded look at what frontier AI does to research jobs. https://arstechnica.com/ai/2026/11/ai-can-do-the-calculations-physicists-are-figuring-out-what-comes-next/

Dell raised its FY27 guidance to $202B from $192B (AI servers $78B) and added $25B to its buyback. The stock fell -11.8% to $295.28 Tuesday before the print and was down ~4% premarket today (Dell, CNBC, Dow Jones, Motley Fool, StockTitan).

3. Humanoids: XPeng's IRON humanoid interacted live with the crowd at today's AI Day in Guangzhou. It's 170cm tall with 76 degrees of freedom (21 per hand) and runs three in-house Turing chips with up to 2,250 TOPS. XPeng targets serial production from Jan 1, 2027 and external deliveries in Q2 2027. Separately, AgiBot's G2 began 24/7 chip loading and sorting at JCET's Shanghai plant, with a reported 99.999% success rate (The Robotics Media, XPeng, ELiA Robotics).

4. OpenAI protein design: OpenAI published a preprint showing GPT-6.2 designing protein backbones with reasoning and code alone. In lab tests with partner Onava, 35 of 322 minibinders bound across five targets, and 70% of 182 redesigned IL-4Rα antibody-loop designs bound. Specialized tools (SolubleMPNN, Boltz-2, ESMFold2) still proposed sequences and filtered candidates, and full structure prediction remains weak (TM-score 0.26 vs ESMFold2's 0.93) (OpenAI, Aiholics).

READS

1. "The Canary in the Coal Mine" by Glassnode (The Week On-chain, Week 47), Nov 24. Why read: the best map of this leg down. BTC gave back the Nvidia rally in six hours, ~90% of the longs above the Realized Price are gone, dealers are short gamma between $58K and $64K, and the BTC–Nasdaq correlation is the highest since 2022. Its $53.2K Realized Price is the level where it would start to turn bullish. https://research.glassnode.com/the-week-onchain-week-47-2026/

2. "What Happens If Tesla and SpaceX Merge?" by Seth Goldstein, CFA and Nicolas Owens (Morningstar), Nov 20. Why read: the most-cited sell-side framing of the exchange ratio. Morningstar's fair values imply a 67/33 Tesla/SpaceX split, it expects Tesla holders to want 50–67%, and it puts SPCX fair value at $70. Pair it with AleXandra Merz's Nov 24 rebuttal of its vote-control figures (x.com/TeslaBoomerMama/status/2125307031209021584). https://www.morningstar.com/stocks/what-happens-if-tesla-spacex-merge

3. "AI may soon change what it means to be a theoretical physicist" by Dan Kagan-Kans (Understanding AI, via Ars Technica), Nov 25. Why read: GPT-6 Astra solved 49 of 50 unpublished, day-long physics problems for under $3 each and caught errors in the human answer key, which saturated the TheoPhysEval benchmark before release. A grounded look at what frontier AI does to research jobs. https://arstechnica.com/ai/2026/11/ai-can-do-the-calculations-physicists-are-figuring-out-what-comes-next/

2026-11-26.bodyText:
News window: Wed 9:00am – Thu 9:00am ET

Note: US stock and bond markets are closed today for Thanksgiving, and Friday is a shortened session (stocks close at 1pm). Stories in Wednesday's 5pm flash (the Nasdaq reversal and Beige Book, Wednesday's MSTR/TSLA/SPCX closes, the FCC Starmind approval, Nvidia's CreditWatch and $290M settlement, Anthropic back above its IPO price) are left out unless there's something new. The Wed 6–9am ET gap check turned up two Tesla items yesterday's briefing missed, plus a Tuesday JPMorgan note; they are marked "missed".

MARKETS

1. Global rebound: Asia and Europe rallied overnight as the new US Section 301 tariffs looked less damaging than feared. Per Reuters, they won't stack on top of July's tariffs and likely won't take effect until February or March. S&P 500 futures were +0.7% and Nasdaq futures +1.1%. The Nikkei rose 1.6%, the KOSPI 1.9% and Taiwan 1.4%, and SoftBank jumped ~9%. The Stoxx 600 was +1.7% at 5:20am. The 10-year yield slipped to 4.848% after an 11-week low overnight, and futures still price a 98% chance of a December hike. The Bank of Korea raised its rate to 3.25%, its third hike this year (Reuters, HedgeWeekly/AP).

2. Bitcoin: BTC was $60,764 at 8:55am ET on Coinbase, up ~4.7% from yesterday's 9am level. Its 24-hour range was $57,208 to $61,527, with an overnight push above $61K. Binance futures liquidations were at least $242.6M on Wednesday (UTC). On Wednesday CoinShares' James Butterfill said BTC is at the "tail end of the bear market" and sees a $60K–$90K range. 21Shares' Matt Mena warned that a break below the ~$53K realized price could bring the $40,000s back into play (Coinbase, AlertaChart, The Block).

3. Galaxy pulls its bottom call: Alex Thorn withdrew Galaxy's Oct 26 call that the bear market ended in June, after BTC lost its 50-week and 200-week averages. Galaxy now treats a daily close below the June 30 closing low of $58,525 as a break. In all seven past cases where BTC broke a similar standing low, it fell at least another 17.1% (median 51.8%), which implies ~$48,500 or ~$28,200. Only 2 of Galaxy's 13 bottom indicators have triggered. Spot BTC ETPs have shed 71,339 BTC ($4.95B) since Oct 4. Levels to reclaim: the 200-week average at $68,159, then the 50-week at $74,401 (Galaxy via The Block, CCN).

4. ETF flows: spot BTC ETFs lost -$453.0M Wednesday, their seventh straight outflow day. IBIT lost -$329.7M, Grayscale's BTC -$60.1M, BITB -$18.2M, ARKB -$14.9M, GBTC -$13.9M, HODL -$9.7M and FBTC -$6.5M. That makes -$3.05B over seven sessions and roughly -$5.39B for November by my tally (record). Ether ETFs lost -$68.5M. ETFs are closed today (Farside via DefiLlama, WhaleRoom).

5. Update on Friday's expiry: ~$7B of Deribit BTC options settle Friday at 8:00 UTC (3am ET). The put/call ratio is 0.89 for this expiry (0.81 across all expiries, vs 0.55 in late October). The biggest positions are puts at $63K–$75K plus $60K, $58K, $50K and $40K. DVOL is 55.45, up from ~38 in October. AlertaChart puts max pain at $69,000, but that mostly reflects old in-the-money puts (CoinDesk via TradeFloat, AlertaChart).

6. Update on SpaceX/Tesla: Musk said every US child will get two SpaceX shares, one from the company and one from him. SpaceX's share transfers next month, and his comes when his lockup expires in June 2027. At Wednesday's $127.44 close, Reuters values the pledge at nearly $18B, and Axios puts it at ~$18.35B across ~72M minors. Separately, Ron Baron projected that SpaceX could generate $50B+ a year from AI data centers, which he says it builds in under 8 months for ~$35B. (missed, Tue note) JPMorgan says S&P's index committee could suspend some eligibility rules for SpaceX, such as 12 months of trading and GAAP profitability, if it merges with Tesla, and inclusion could spark passive buying of ~10% of SpaceX's free float (Reuters, Forbes, Axios, Benzinga, GuruFocus).

7. Tesla: the Dallas Robotaxi area grew ~83% to 150.4 sq mi, reaching Carrollton, Addison and Richardson, a week after the Cybercab launch there. Cybercab is on show at Tesla Center Hamburg and in Průhonice near Prague on Nov 27–28. Tesla added 1,027 Supercharger stalls at 91 sites over 56 days ahead of Thanksgiving. (missed, Wed 7:00am) Tesla raised the Cyberbeast price to $114,990 and ended Cybertruck leases, with deliveries stretching to June 2027. (missed, Wed ~7:35am) The EU pushed its TCMV vote on Tesla's supervised FSD to Dec 15. A rejection could undo approvals in 12 countries (Drive Tesla Canada, Not a Tesla App, Tesla, Elektrickevozy.cz, CNBC).

8. Strategy/Strive: STRC closed Wednesday +0.3% at $98.04 after a $95.44 low, on its ex-dividend day. Strive's ASST closed at $14.95, an equity-only mNAV of ~0.72x on its 43,404 BTC, and SATA rose +1.3% to $90.62 (PreferredStock.ai, PrefWatch, ChartMill).

9. Regulation: the House Financial Services Committee formally sent H.R. 8957 to the full House. It would codify the Strategic Bitcoin Reserve with a minimum 20-year lock on federal BTC and is now Union Calendar No. 789. The Block notes little floor time is left before Congress ends, and Polymarket gives 4% odds of a national BTC reserve this year. Separately, Sens. Warren and Van Hollen asked SEC Chair Atkins to rescind the proposed "Regulation Crypto Assets" and the tokenized-stock exemption (The Block, Senate Banking minority).

AI, ROBOTICS, TECH & LONGEVITY

1. Nvidia: the FT reported that Nvidia told partners, including Dell and Supermicro, to stop shipping servers with its chips to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Indonesia. The move follows US export-licence rules for advanced chips to Southeast Asia that took effect Nov 19, and it's unclear whether the halt is temporary. Separately, the Washington Post reported (~6:30pm) that Hegseth and Feinberg discussed using the Defense Production Act as leverage to get Huang reinstated, citing three people familiar with the talks. The Pentagon denied it (~9pm). US investors first trade on all of this in Friday's short session (Reuters/FT, WaPo, Benzinga).

2. Humanoids: Tesla registered "Tesla Machining Technologies Management SE" (€120,000 capital) at the Salach HQ of EMAG, a German machine-tool maker that builds the equipment for humanoid-joint gears (flexsplines, wave generators, planetary gears). Its managers include the HR chief from Giga Berlin. Stuttgarter Nachrichten reports that ~220 EMAG staff will move to Tesla in a humanoid-robot deal, though neither company has confirmed. Musk has called custom gears an Optimus reliability worry. Also, Volvo Cars began training Hexagon AEON wheeled humanoids at its Ghent plant, with floor work starting mid-2027 (Electrek/Business Insider Germany, InsideEVs).

3. Neuralink: the FDA approved its LINK Pivotal Study, the first US pivotal trial of an implantable brain-computer interface, for people with severe paralysis from ALS. Early feasibility studies have implanted more than 30 participants in the US, Canada and UK, and enrollment is now open (Neuralink, Bloomberg).

4. Anthropic/OpenAI: Anthropic said Claude agents migrated its Messages API from Python to Rust under human review, cutting CPU use per request ~70% and median time to first token 20%. OpenAI will combine ChatGPT's Chat and Work usage limits (wider rollout in December), and Altman announced a limited pilot of "Private Inference" for sensitive business workloads (The Neuron).

READS

1. "Bitcoin On the Brink After 7 Weekly Declines" by Alex Thorn (Galaxy Research, X Article), Nov 25 (sent to clients Nov 24). Why read: the full note behind Galaxy's reversal. It covers all 13 past 50-week reclaims since 2011, why this is the first followed by a new low, the seven "standing low" breaks that set the $48.5K/$28.2K paths, and the 13-indicator bottom checklist. It also lists the exact daily, weekly and moving-average levels to watch into Dec 8. https://x.com/intangiblecoins/status/2125611340135870701

2. "DAT Capitulation: Five Treasury Companies Have Sold About $203M of Coins Since Their Last Filings" by Kairos Research (X Article), Nov 25. Why read: on-chain wallet mapping, checked against past filings, shows sub-mNAV treasury companies quietly selling. Silvia (formerly ProCap) sold 410 BTC in nine lots, and BTCS, Bit Digital, Upexi and Solana Company sold ETH and SOL. It also explains why trading below 1x mNAV breaks the issue-and-buy playbook. Alex Thorn called it a "great combo of onchain and filings data." https://x.com/Kairos_Res/status/2125704827606851897
